An engineer working on Tesla Optimus is building GROXIE, a compact AI assistant for a kitchen counter or desk, with Grok as its voice.

→ suggests meals from the ingredients you have and walks you through recipes
→ manages a calendar, drafts emails, and makes calls
→ expressive robot movements instead of a full-size humanoid

It's still a concept. The next step is a formal prototype review before any approval for further development.

https://t.co/TN2f1PiOUK
author: RoundtableSpace
quoted_text:
Excited to share a small project I've been leading alongside our larger robotics work at @Tesla_Optimus, and one I'm particularly excited about.

The inspiration actually came from my wife. We started exploring the idea of a compact physical AI assistant that could sit on a kitchen counter or desk and help with everyday tasks.

During our development, she began testing GROXIE at home while cooking, using it to suggest meals based on available ingredients, walk her through recipes, manage her calendar, draft emails, make calls, and provide real-time updates throughout the day.

What makes GROXIE interesting is the idea of integrating @grok AI as its conversational intelligence.

Using @grok would power GROXIE's ability to understand natural conversations, answer complex questions, provide information, and adapt to individual preferences. Combined with expressive robotic movements, voice recognition, and a personalized assistant interface, the goal is to make AI feel more natural and accessible.

Rather than building another full-sized humanoid robot, we wanted to explore how much useful intelligence could fit into a compact desktop companion.

The next step in this concept is a formal prototype review, where we'd evaluate the hardware, AI integration, privacy, safety, and reliability before considering approval for further development or a potential consumer release.

I'm excited about where this could go.

Volta is the first official Uniswap V4 launchpad on the Elysium chain, and has built its own RPC, Explorer, and cross-chain Bridge.

Simply put, it's a "one-click token launch + trade directly on official Uniswap V4" platform. Users can create a token, set up a liquidity pool, and configure fee distribution rules in a single transaction.

The project mainly addresses fairness and liquidity issues: many traditional launchpads have pre-mines, team allocations, and bonding curve migrations afterward. Volta requires every token to have a fixed supply of 1 billion, with 100% going into the pool and no team reserve.

Compliance and sustainability: Many other launchpads on Elysium use unauthorized Uniswap V4 forks, while Volta deploys directly with official Uniswap + custom Hooks.

Rigid fee distribution: Creators can decide where trading fees go themselves—to themselves, for buybacks and burns, or distributed to holders.

The VOLTA token is the platform token.
It adopts a Pons-like model: of the 30% trading fee the protocol collects, 80% is used to buy back and burn VOLTA on the market.
The higher the trading volume → the more burned → the lower the supply.
Additionally, 20% is used for airdrops to active traders in the Elysium ecosystem.

VOLTA burned: 38.71M tokens, worth approximately $193.7K at current prices, about 3.87% of total supply.
Protocol fees: 406.913 HYPE (approximately $30.2K), of which 80% is used for buybacks.

Token allocation:

10% to Volta platform traders and creators.

text:
Built a physical simulation of a record player with WebGL2 and Web Audio. It's *shockingly* accurate: https://t.co/MBNaTfKoai.

Instead of playing a song, it works by converting it into the physical shape of a groove. Then a simulated stylus rides those walls 384,000 times a second, and you hear the voltage that motion would induce in a cartridge.

So the crackle, the pops, the wow/flutter, the dull inner grooves are natural byproducts of the simulation. You can also "DJ" the record.

(The converted songs are in the public domain or CC-licensed. Code is linked for you to remix and re-deploy.)

我说什么来着？特朗普家族的加密生意，终于烧到白宫椭圆形办公室了！

最新一期 CBS《60 Minutes》，主持人直接当面拷问特朗普：你儿子经营 World Liberty Financial，你本人也是这家公司的共同所有人，对吧？

特朗普：没错。

主持人：这家公司还有与阿联酋政府高层有关联的投资者。如果这是拜登家族，你会不会觉得这很腐败？

特朗普：区别就在于，我对此一无所知。

好家伙！承认自己是共同所有人，转头就说自己什么都不知道。

主持人继续追问：既然如此，为什么不直接退出公司？

特朗普的解释是：公司是儿子们在经营，自己很难要求他们因为自己当总统就停止做生意。

2025年，阿联酋关联投资实体花5亿美元买下 World Liberty 49%的股权，其中1.87亿美元流向特朗普家族控制的实体。

现在特朗普亲口承认自己是共同所有人，却把经营责任推给儿子，把自己和公司的关系解释成我不知道。

孙哥之前花4500万美元买入WLFI，后来因为代币被冻结与项目方翻脸，起诉、追问公司股权披露，甚至把阿联酋关联背景带进了法庭争议。

这下真有好戏看了。
author: oragnes
quoted_text:
卧槽，特朗普现在最大的软肋可能是两个华人😂😎

民主党中期选举大胜后，一场针对特朗普家族的调查风暴正在酝酿。

我看了下，民主党未来两年准备重点调查的方向，大概涉及以下8个领域：

1.特朗普家族生意：WLFI加密货币、房地产、1789 Capital投资、中东主权基金。
2.爱泼斯坦案：政府有没有故意隐瞒关键证据。
3.移民执法：ICE暴力执法、非法拘捕及资金滥用。
4.司法部：是否利用司法权力打击政治对手，以及争议性总统特赦。
5.马斯克：旗下公司与美国政府的合同及利益往来。
6.白宫工程：宴会厅私人捐款、政府工程及矿产交易。
7.国防军事：伊朗战争、军事决策和国防部履职。
8.医药保险：药厂、医疗保险及政府药价协议中的利益冲突。

民主党现在的思路很清楚，先调查，不急着弹劾。毕竟弹劾定罪需要参议院三分之二支持，难度极高，但国会调查可以持续传唤证人、索取文件、举行公开听证，这也在为2028年的总统大选作准备。

我分析来分析去，发现最容易率先找到突破口的，可能就是特朗普家族的加密货币生意。

因为其他调查很多还停留在寻找证据的阶段，而加密这边已经有人打官司、有人追资金、有人正式要求交文件了。

而帮民主党撕开这道口子的，可能就是孙哥和大表哥。

先说孙哥：

2024年11月，孙哥拿出3000万美元支持特朗普家族的WLFI项目，后来累计投资达到7500万美元，一度被奉为座上宾。

2026年3月，孙哥此前面临的SEC诉讼迎来和解，旗下公司支付1000万美元罚款，SEC撤销对孙哥个人的相关指控。

结果才过一个多月，孙哥就跟特朗普家族彻底翻脸了！

原来孙哥持有的WLFI代币早在2025年9月就遭到冻结，无法正常转让和出售。

到了今年4月，孙哥直接把WLFI告上美国法庭，要求解冻代币，恢复自己的资产处置权。

高潮发生在11月3日，也就是美国中期选举当天。

孙哥帖子链接：https://t.co/DumKywpRTG

孙哥突然向法院申请制裁WLFI及其律师，指控对方在诉讼中隐瞒阿联酋股东身份。

WLFI最初披露的公司身份只有美国佛罗里达州，后来又修改文件，承认股权链条涉及22个成员以及阿联酋，并以涉及外国股东为由挑战美国联邦法院的管辖权。

而此前曝光的另一笔交易显示，阿联酋国家安全顾问塔赫农支持的投资实体，曾以5亿美元取得WLFI约49%的股权。

这下事情就大了。

孙哥原本只想拿回自己的币，现在却把特朗普家族与中东资本的股权关系拉进了司法程序。

如果诉讼继续涉及股东身份、协议及相关资金往来，民主党调查特朗普家族海外商业利益时，就多了一条现成的取证线索。

再说大表哥：

2023年，币安因反洗钱等违规问题与美国政府达成43亿美元和解，大表哥认罪并在2024年服刑约4个月。

到了2025年，事情发生了戏剧性变化。

5月，阿联酋投资机构MGX选择使用特朗普家族WLFI发行的20亿美元USD1稳定币，完成对币安的投资。

这笔交易的商业价值非常直接：USD1的发行方可以通过稳定币储备资产获得利息收入。20亿美元的资金规模，对刚起步的USD1来说是极其重要的业务。

同年10月23日，特朗普正式特赦大表哥。

一边是中东资本通过USD1投资币安，一边是特朗普家族的稳定币业务受益，随后大表哥获得总统特赦。

几件事本身都有公开记录，民主党自然会追问其中有没有不当利益交换。

麻烦还没结束。

2026年2月，美国民主党参议员Blumenthal针对币安启动调查，质疑该平台涉及约17亿美元与伊朗关联实体及俄罗斯影子船队有关的可疑资金流转。

币安明确否认有关违规指控，但民主党已经把这个问题与大表哥的特赦、特朗普家族的加密业务联系起来审查。

现在最有意思的事情发生了。

11月5日，Blumenthal正式向WLFI、币安等机构发出通知，要求最迟在2027年1月4日前提交相关资料，否则考虑采取进一步措施。

这就形成了两条线：

孙哥在法庭上追查WLFI股权与阿联酋资本。

民主党在国会追查USD1资金流、币安合规以及大表哥的特赦。

两条线最后都指向同一个问题：

特朗普家族到底从这些交易中获得了多少商业利益，这些利益与美国政府的决策之间有没有不当关联？

PS：写到最后不得不服孙哥的政治敏感性有多强，孙哥只花了1000万美金搞定了美国，而大表哥花了40多亿美金搞定了美国。

That's the gains you would've made if you bought $PENDLE during the bear market low of 2022.

I think PENDLE is a great case study of how an altcoin can die into the bear. But then starts to perform really well when the team finally finds product-market-fit.

I wasn't buying alts at the time, but PENDLE had a -98.5% drawdown into the 2022 bear market low.

From watching @tn_pendle's interview, I learned that they struggled to find product-market-fit for a long time.

Then after a while, things finally started clicking.

Pendle found its niche in yield trading and allows users to split a yield-bearing asset into yield tokens (YT) and principal token (PT).

YT = lets you speculate on the variable yield or airdrop points. typically considered higher risk.

PT = lets you fix the yield of an asset. this is especially great when the yields run hot because you can fix a really high yield.

Then revenue started kicking in, and prices reversed.

PENDLE even front ran ETH's reversal and ended up pulling a +20,121% gain from the lows.

It did take 513 days for it to reach there though so patience is definitely required.

But, this is exactly why I love betting on teams and founders rather than the v1 of the product. 

Ofc it's great if the product already found initial traction, but the team is still the most important factor imo.

Since PENDLE is more established now, I think the multiple won't be as high as before but the risk is also much lower than before.

One of my fav projects and worth looking into imo.

Pendle.

(Ofc, not every coin is going to do this. But, I think the idea is still very useful. Nfa dyor like always).

TLDR: Great founders persist and build great products. Buying the dip during the bear and being patient often yields great results.

3. Optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with decentralization and CROPS

Whenever I ask what people appreciate the most about Ethereum (as opposed to either other blockchains, or anything outside the blockchain world), the most common answer is: decentralization and CROPS (censorship and capture resistance, open source, privacy and security).

Decentralization and CROPS have a lot of value, even to institutions. For individuals, privacy is often viewed as an abstract ideology. For institutions, it's prudent risk management, data protection law compliance, and a number of other things. Likewise for security. And likewise for running your own node (enterprise buzzword: "on-prem deployment").

But what about for the ETH holder? Well, it depends why you're an ETH holder. If you want ETH to optimally chase financial trends and collect fees from them, then you want a Fearless Leader™ who bravely shouts on the socials that Ethereum loves [insert opportunity here] and will pragmatically reconfigure itself to give it explicit protocol support.

But if your primary reason to hold ETH is as an SoV, then you will be judging ETH by SoV-ish metrics. And what is the first and most important SoV-ish metric?

To survive.

That's what a big chunk of this last Devcon was about ("post-quantum and post-AI"). You want a chain that is taking conservative tradeoffs ("hash-only security, all formally proven, >3x more rounds than known to be necessary for security"). You want a chain that is aiming for at least partial ossification, where the great balance of work will move to higher levels of the stack once the core is complete. You want a chain that aims to minimize protocol politics, by having a very high bar before it accepts either precompiles that bloat the protocol or new kinds of in-protocol rewards that could get captured.

What other SoV'ish metrics?

The ability to easily hold it safely (hence, work on multisigs).
The ability to hold it privately (hence, kohaku work).
The ability to hold it privately *and* safely (hence, 8288 and private-AA workstreams already starting).
The guarantee that if you have coins, you can send them, and block builders can't stop you (FOCIL)
Minimized infrastructure dependence (basically the whole decentralization roadmap, including the fact that I am able to currently run a node on this laptop, and it synced in < 6 hours and takes up only 1/8 of my hard drive - better stats than in 2019!)

Now, are there "adoption" goals that are highly synergistic with SoV?

Very much so.

The more assets there are natively issued on L1, including both RWAs and native decentralized assets, the larger a set of things you can "do" with your ETH, the better. Being able to easily (including safely, trustlessly) convert back and forth between ETH and other assets, use ETH as collateral to do things with other assets, etc, all forms part of the utility of holding ETH.

There are still some conflicts between serving these use cases and decentralization (eg. we want to be careful about fast slots and impact on centralization), but on the whole much less than what you get if you maximize fees.

Conclusion:

The best social reason to care about Ethereum is because it makes decentralization and CROPS properties a reality for more people and uses.

The best private reason to hold ETH is its SoV properties, which are a direct consequence of that decentralization and CROPS.

Buckle up.

text:
这一周，美国 AI 圈最值得关注的名字，可能不是 Altman，也不是黄仁勋，而是一位阿布扎比王室成员。

@0xPickleCati 发了一篇很有意思的长文，把最近的纳指暴跌、OpenAI 融资、Anthropic 上市、黄仁勋调查和美国中期选举，串成了一条时间线。

故事的起点，是一笔此前没有公开的 5 亿美元投资。

2025 年 1 月，特朗普就职前四天，阿联酋国家安全顾问、王室成员塔赫农支持的投资公司，花 5 亿美元买下特朗普家族加密公司 World Liberty Financial 的 49% 股份。

两个月后，塔赫农担任主席的 MGX 宣布向币安投资 20 亿美元。随后披露，这笔交易使用的是 World Liberty 发行的稳定币 USD1。

同年 10 月，特朗普赦免了币安创始人赵长鹏。

重点来了，这位塔赫农控制和影响的资本网络，后来又出现在 OpenAI 的融资名单里。

2026 年 10 月，OpenAI 原本打算以 1.4 万亿美元估值融资至少 300 亿美元。但 AI 股遭遇抛售，投资者的热情开始降温，最终融资目标削减至约 200 亿美元，估值下调到 1.25 万亿美元。

据 FT 和彭博社报道，包括 MGX 在内的阿联酋投资财团参与了融资谈判，并被认为可能成为本轮最大的出资方。

也就是说，同一位阿布扎比王室成员，一边通过关联资本投资特朗普家族的加密生意，一边通过另一家基金参与美国最重要 AI 公司的融资。

然后，美国政治风向突然变了。

11 月 3 日，民主党赢得参众两院。与此同时，美国地方选民在 41 项涉及数据中心建设的公投中，有 40 项投票结果倾向限制开发。

11 月 5 日，纳指 100 暴跌 6.4%，一天蒸发约 2.5 万亿美元。

同一天，OpenAI 发布新的社区承诺，宣布未来自有自营数据中心将承担全部用电及相关基础设施成本，并限制地方官员保密协议的使用。

11 月 6 日，OpenAI 完成首批约 110 亿美元融资。

而民主党准备在明年 1 月接掌国会后，调查特朗普家族的商业利益，其中 World Liberty 正是重点对象之一。

Anthropic 也在争取感恩节前上市，即便估值已经从此前讨论的 2 万亿美元明显回落。

黄仁勋则收到三名共和党委员会主席的闭门简报要求，涉及外国情报活动风险。英伟达董事会也已启动独立调查。

Pickle Cat 提出一个大胆猜测，AI 公司正在与政治风险赛跑，希望赶在新的国会调查全面展开前，尽快把融资和上市完成。

当然，目前没有证据证明这些融资安排是在躲避调查，也不能把塔赫农关联企业之间的投资直接等同于利益输送。OpenAI 与 Anthropic 的融资时间表，同样有商业竞争、资金需求和市场窗口等解释。

但我觉得，这条时间线真正揭示的，是 AI 行业的权力结构正在发生变化。

过去，硅谷讲究的是谁有最好的模型、最多的 GPU、最雄厚的资本。只要技术持续进步，投资人就愿意继续给钱。

现在，游戏规则变了。

阿布扎比的钱能解决融资问题，却可能带来新的政治审查；英伟达控制着最重要的算力供应，却不能回避国会的国家安全质询；OpenAI 拿得出巨额资金，却不一定能说服当地居民接受新数据中心。

更讽刺的是，AI 的需求并没有消失，GPU 租赁价格甚至还在上涨，但资本市场已经开始重新评估它的政治成本。

过去，AI 公司最怕的是没有足够的钱买 GPU。现在，哪怕钱和 GPU 都有了，也不代表能顺利把数据中心建起来。

硅谷一直相信技术可以绕开政治。但当一个产业需要数万亿美元资本、跨国主权基金、电网扩容和地方政府许可时，它就不可能再只是一个技术产业。

AI 正在从算力稀缺的时代，走向政治许可同样稀缺的时代。

他把使用 Token 称为购买「时间的折叠权」：过去几个月才能梳理完的学科知识，现在可以借助 AI 快速提炼成知识图谱。但他也提出一个反思：读薄交给 AI，读厚必须交给自己。 知识获取越来越快，不代表真正理解得更多。

更有意思的是，AI 开始成为他的自我觉察工具。神鱼把多年经历和交易记录交给 Agent 分析，甚至被问到一个问题：「你到底是在做交易，还是在满足某种心理需求？」

在组织层面，他发现了另一个反差：个人借助 Agent 可以成为超级个体，但放进传统组织后，效率反而可能被协作流程和信息管道拖累。Cobo 正尝试让员工拥有专属 Agent，由 Agent 之间完成更多跨部门协作。

神鱼还提出了两个管理 Agent 闭环的关键参数：K，控制每次改动的最小单元；τ，缩短获得现实反馈的周期。核心原则是：最小化改动，一个 PR 只做一件事，并尽快验证结果。

从 ISTJ 到更偏向直觉抽象的 N 型，神鱼认为 AI 不只是在替人执行任务，也在改变人的认知方式。

AI 时代真正稀缺的，或许不再是获取知识的能力，而是品味、判断力，以及对自己的持续觉察。

Excited to share a small project I've been leading alongside our larger robotics work at @Tesla_Optimus, and one I'm particularly excited about.

The inspiration actually came from my wife. We started exploring the idea of a compact physical AI assistant that could sit on a kitchen counter or desk and help with everyday tasks.

During our development, she began testing GROXIE at home while cooking, using it to suggest meals based on available ingredients, walk her through recipes, manage her calendar, draft emails, make calls, and provide real-time updates throughout the day.

What makes GROXIE interesting is the idea of integrating @grok AI as its conversational intelligence.

Using @grok would power GROXIE's ability to understand natural conversations, answer complex questions, provide information, and adapt to individual preferences. Combined with expressive robotic movements, voice recognition, and a personalized assistant interface, the goal is to make AI feel more natural and accessible.

Rather than building another full-sized humanoid robot, we wanted to explore how much useful intelligence could fit into a compact desktop companion.

The next step in this concept is a formal prototype review, where we'd evaluate the hardware, AI integration, privacy, safety, and reliability before considering approval for further development or a potential consumer release.

I'm excited about where this could go.

text:
Quick rant and thoughts on the state of software design & engineering. It comes as no surprise that the models have allowed designers to implement and explore their wildest dreams. But I cannot explain enough how much more important that makes understanding the lowest levels of the stack

Take for example these demos. It turns out that instant launch, a fast + instantly zoomable grid, and morphing photo clusters onto the surface of a globe are actually all underpinned by the same technical component: a really fast image thumbnail cache (and cache management). There is a lot more detail that goes into making each experience independently high quality, but that cache is the biggest performance bottleneck for each one - because ultimately they all depend on extremely fast data retrieval to even exist. You can’t use a globe that doesn’t spin and you can’t use a grid you can’t see or scroll. Therefore they never get built and die in imagination land. Achieving your design goals requires being able to identify their core infrastructural overlap

Obviously you don’t need to know every detail, but it’s now your responsibility now to use the models to help you uncover your unknown unknowns about the hidden connections in any system you are building. The proper solution is latent in your unoptimized code. Its complexity is the raw material you need to chisel away at and navigate to the “correct” side of the solution space

Will the models be able to come to conclusions like this autonomously soon? Yes. I think there will need to be advancements in the ability to quickly reason about and quantify the complexity (whatever that means) of a given piece of software and instantly determine what to chop up / refactor / redesign as it develops into its simplest possible form. That might not mean the fewest or tersest LOC but perhaps how few turns it takes a model to achieve a verified solution to any given task, or how tangled its code reference graph is. 

But I think it will always be an advantage to know where to poke

这次英伟达 $NVDA 周末休市期间的消息发酵，说明了一个很现实的问题：美股可以休市，但风险不会跟着放假。传统市场上的现货价格停在收盘那刻，但外面的消息、情绪和预期却一直在变。数字没动，不代表你手里的风险没动。

做事件驱动交易，最难受的就是消息出来了，判断也有了，交易窗口却还没开，只能眼睁睁的等死。等到周一晚上开盘，一个跳空直接把你按在市场里动弹不得。尤其现在这种消息密集、预期反复的行情，能不能及时处理仓位，本身就是交易里很重要的一环。

币安TradFi永续合约的24/7全天候交易，用处就在这里。周末或者标的市场休市期间，也可以通过合约表达多空判断、调整仓位、进行对冲，把应对消息的主动权留在自己手里。

这次NVDA就是个现成的例子。从币安 TradFi 休市行情来看：NVDA永续合约指数价格较上次收盘参考价下跌约3%，成交量约3.6亿美元，接近同期对比中第二名的2倍；未平仓量约9060万美元，约为第二名的1.6倍。美股开盘前，合约市场已经在用真金白银给预期重新报价了。

从这个角度看，币安TradFi值得关注的地方，是把币圈早已习惯的全天候交易带到了传统资产上。对我们这种盯宏观、看消息、做事件驱动交易的人来说，休市行情也多了一个观察窗口：消息到底引发了多少交易，资金怎么反应，可以直接去看价格和成交。当然，周末合约价格反映的是当时的市场预期，周一现货怎么开，仍然要等市场验证。

美股休市，市场照样变动。消息不等开盘，交易也不必等。

0 - rpc shutdown (and preparation of a 2+ hour window)

text:
현재 시장 내러티브에 대한 생각 정리

1. TSMC의 메모리 시장 진출

DRAM은 로직 반도체와 공정부터 다르고 기술 확보와 양산 수율 안정화까지 상당한 시간이 필요함. 

TSMC 역시 파운드리 사업에 집중하겠다는 입장을 재확인했기에 단기간에 기존 메모리 3사의 경쟁력을 위협할 가능성은 낮다고 봄.

2. 민주당의 데이터센터 규제와 텍사스

민주당 역시 중국과의 AI 패권 경쟁을 포기할 수는 없음. 

텍사스에서도 신규 데이터센터 인허가 중단이 추진되고 있지만, 이미 허가받고 착공한 프로젝트는 영향을 제한적으로 받을 가능성이 높음. 

더 중요한건 이 규제가 기존 투자까지 훼손할 것인지, 향후 신규 프로젝트의 비용과 일정에 한해 집중될 것인지에 있다고 봄.

3. OBBBA와 기업 세제혜택

2025년 통과된 OBBBA는 적격 설비투자 100% 비용처리와 미국 내 R&D 비용의 즉시 공제를 허용함. 

이미 법제화된 정책인 만큼 민주당이 의회를 장악하더라도 트럼프의 거부권을 고려하면 쉽게 폐지하기 어려움.

4. 엘리자베스 워런(민주당 상원 핵심 의원)의 부유층 증세 법안

워런이 추진하는 부유층 증세 역시 새로운 법률 제정이 필요함. 

민주당이 상하원을 확보했더라도 대통령 거부권을 넘어서야 하기에 실제 입법까지는 상당한 장벽이 존재함.

5. GENIUS Act와 친시장 정책

2025년 GENIUS Act는 초기 절차표결에서 제동이 걸렸지만 이후 초당적 합의를 거쳐 정식 법률로 제정됐음. 

이미 제도화된 디지털자산 관련 법률을 민주당이 일방적으로 폐지하기는 어려운 구조

6. 빅테크 친화적 인프라 정책

트럼프 행정부는 데이터센터 인허가 간소화와 AI 인프라 확충을 추진해 왔으며, 일부 주에서는 관련 장비와 전력 구매에 세제혜택을 제공해 왔음. 

다만 지역별로 혜택 축소 움직임도 있어 정책의 지속성을 구분해서 볼 필요는 있음.

7. 빅테크 CAPEX와 AI 공급망의 협상력 변화

만약 민주당의 규제 강화로 데이터센터 건설이 지연되고 하이퍼스케일러들이 CAPEX를 조절한다면, 공급망 내 협상력에도 변화가 생길 수 있음. 

현재는 공급자(메모리,엔비디아) 우위 시장인데, 구조가 역전되며 가격 인하 압박이 전가될 가능성도 고려해야 함.

8. 금 가격 상승과 시장 레짐 변화

최근 금 가격이 다시 뛰는 게 경기침체 레짐을 반영하는 건지, 유동성 개선에 대한 기대를 반영하는 건지는 정확히 알기 어려움.

다만 크립토가 상대적으로 버티는 가운데 골드가 하락쐐기 패턴을 상방 돌파했다는 점에서, 시장이 후자의 가능성을 기대하고 있는 게 아닐까 생각함.

9. 에너지발 인플레이션과 증시 전망

여전히 가장 큰 변수는 에너지발 인플레이션이라고 생각함.

유가 상승에 따른 물가 압력을 빠르게 잠재우지 못한다면 연준의 통화정책 전환에도 제약이 생길 수밖에 없음.

이 문제가 해결되지 않는다면 올해 4분기는 물론 내년 1분기까지도 증시가 쉬운 장세가 되기는 어렵지 않을까 생각함.

10. BofA 하트넷의 금 강세 전망

뱅오아의 마이클 하트넷은 물가상승과 경기침체 우려, 재정 불안을 근거로 금 강세를 전망하고 있음.

개인적으로도 어느 정도 동의할 수 있는 뷰라고 생각함.

특히 물가 압력이 지속되는 가운데 경기까지 둔화되고 미국의 재정 불안이 심화된다면 금에 대한 안전자산 수요가 더욱 강해질 가능성도 있음.

11. 워시, 베센트의 금리 정책과 채권 커브

최근 워시는 단기물을 관리하고 베센트는 장기물을 관리하려는 듯한 스탠스가 지속되고 있음.

워시가 단기금리를 높은 수준에서 유지하고 베센트가 장기금리 상승을 억제하려 한다면, 채권 수익률곡선에는 평탄화 압력이 발생할 수 있다고 봄.

이런 구조가 지속된다면 기업들의 자금조달 부담이 누적되면서 경기 둔화를 더욱 자극할 수 있는데, 어쩌면 의도적인 경기침체를 바라는 게 아닐까 하는 의심도 듦.

12. 경기침체를 통한 AI 산업 구조조정 가능성

여기서 음모론에 가까운 생각이 듦

의도적으로 경기침체를 유도해 자금조달 능력이 취약한 데이터센터 기업과 AI 기업들을 어려움에 빠뜨린 뒤 막대한 현금을 보유한 하이퍼스케일러들이 이 기업들을 저렴하게 인수하도록 만드는 게 아닐까 하는 의심.

결국 AI 산업 내부에서도 자본력이 부족한 기업들을 선별적으로 가지치기하고 하이퍼스케일러 중심으로 산업을 재편하려는 게 아닐까 싶기도 함.

13. 민주당의 의회 장악과 정책 레짐 변화

물론 민주당이 상하원 다수당을 확보한 만큼 기존 정책 레짐이 꺾일 가능성도 고려해야 함.

새로운 의회가 출범하는 내년 1월부터는 데이터센터 규제와 기업 세제혜택, AI 인프라 정책 등을 둘러싼 갈등이 본격화될 수 있음.

트럼프의 거부권이 존재하기에 기존 정책을 전면적으로 뒤집기는 어렵겠지만 민주당이 어느 수준까지 압박을 가할지는 지켜봐야 할 문제라고 생각함.

에너지발 인플레이션이 얼마나 빠르게 진정되는지, 금융여건이 실제로 개선되는지 민주당의 규제가 어느 수준까지 확대되는지가 향후 시장의 방향을 결정할 중요한 변수가 될 것으로 봄.

P.S 젠슨황 불륜이고 뭐고 시장을 누르고 싶어 하는 주체가 있는건 분명해 보임.

author: Plus_Ultra_715
quoted_text:
人类最后的护城河「品味」，可能也快守不住了。

一项正在进行的实验发现，在判断什么内容更能吸引人点击这件事上，Claude Opus 5.5 已经超过了约 98% 的参测者。

实验来自 Clickhunt Lab。研究人员把不同 YouTube 视频的封面和标题拿出来，让人类与 AI 分别判断，哪种组合更能吸引陌生观众，再根据平台积累的人类投票数据评估表现。

截至 11 月 7 日，能击败各模型的人类参与者比例分别是：

Claude Opus 5.5：2%
GPT-6 Astra：7%
Gemini 4 Argon：10%
Jev 1.14：22%

团队此前披露，已有 7,030 人参与测试。

当然，这并不等于 AI 已经比 98% 的人更有审美。实验衡量的是对群体点击偏好的判断，而非实际点击率，更不是创造力。

但真正值得警惕的恰恰是这一点。

过去我们常说，AI 可以生成内容，但不知道什么是好内容。人类的品味、直觉和对受众心理的理解，是创作者最后的护城河。

现在看来，至少在「什么东西更能吸引人」这个问题上，AI 已经开始摸到门道。

这对内容行业的冲击，可能比 AI 会写文章、画图片更加直接。

因为当预测注意力的能力变得廉价且人人可用，原本只有少数优秀创作者掌握的经验，就可能变成所有人的基础配置。

更讽刺的是，当所有人都越来越懂得什么东西能吸引人，互联网可能反而越来越无聊。

AI 可以学会预测人们想看什么，但谁来创造人们还不知道自己想看的东西？

这或许才是下一道真正的护城河。

text:
$ETH should be valued as a SoV rather than as a fee burning token and the numbers make his case more strongly than he did.

Over the last 12M Ethereum burned roughly $52M in fees, which is about 0.02% of a $260B mcap, while the apps built on it paid around $3.3B in fees, so the chain itself collects only a small fraction of the value created on top of it. When ETH fell 43% from its Oct 25' peak, fees fell by almost exactly the same amount. What does seem to hold the asset up is that about $42B of ETH is deployed in DeFi and another $19.8B is borrowed against it, so people are treating it as collateral they trust to stay neutral.

That makes the SoV case something you can measure on a balance sheet and it shows the real test is how much of that collateral stays when borrowing gets expensive.

h/t to @DefiLlama for the data
author: yashascore
quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
Hackers now have AI agents searching GitHub for your API keys, 24/7.

Microsoft just warned that attackers are using AI agent tools to scan public repos for secrets: company names, cloud keys, AI service keys. It's been running since August.

When an agent finds a working key, they sign straight into your cloud, pull data from your vaults and storage, and run up your AI bills. CrowdStrike says 200+ organizations have been hit since mid-October.

If a key ever touched a public repo:
- Treat it as stolen, even if you deleted the commit. Old commits and forks still have it
- Rotate it now, not later
- Turn on GitHub push protection so it blocks secrets before they're pushed: Settings > Code security
- Scan your repos with gitleaks or trufflehog

Microsoft's own advice: if your secrets were ever public, assume they've been compromised.

text:
美股休市，但市场从未停止定价：RWA的长期价值，可能被很多人低估了

我一直认为，币圈虽然充斥着投机与泡沫，但加密行业的金融创新，长期依然具备明显的竞争优势。

尤其是RWA（现实世界资产），我始终认为这是未来值得长期关注的方向之一。从17年的bch叙事开始这就是我最期待的基础建设的方向。

传统金融存在一个很明显的结构性问题：

交易所有营业时间，但风险没有。

美股周五收盘，不意味着周末不会出现重大新闻。地缘政治、企业突发事件、政策变化，都可能随时改变市场预期。

虽然纳斯达克计划于12月6日推出23小时、每周5天的交易机制，CME的股指期货也早已实现接近23小时的日常交易，但这些市场依然存在每日维护停盘和周末休市。

只要交易存在时间上的中断，消息就可能在休市期间集中积累，并在重新开盘时形成价格跳空。

而7×24小时连续交易，恰恰是加密行业长期积累的基础设施优势。

这次英伟达（NVDA）就提供了一个很有代表性的案例。

周末英伟达出现负面消息，美股现货市场处于休市状态，但币安TradFi永续合约依然保持活跃。

根据周末相关统计，成交量、持仓量双双领先，体现了币安在这次休市期间的流动性优势。

这里真正值得研究的是价格发现机制。

美股虽然休市，投资者依然可以通过衍生品表达市场预期，提前消化信息，并根据需求调整仓位或对冲风险。

虽然休市期间永续合约的价格未必等于下一次美股开盘价格，但连续的市场反馈本身就具有价值。

这也是我长期看好RWA和加密金融创新的原因。

传统金融资产正在逐步接入全天候运行的数字金融基础设施。虽然TradFi永续属于衍生品，与直接持有代币化资产存在区别，但二者都体现了传统金融与加密技术融合的趋势。

还有一个经常被大家忽略的问题：

金融基础设施的竞争，最终离不开流动性与信用。

币安依然是全球成交规模领先的中心化加密交易所。根据CoinGecko统计，2026年第三季度币安占头部CEX现货成交量的42.7%，排名第一。

流动性天然存在网络效应。更多交易者带来更多订单，吸引更多做市商与套利资金，进一步改善市场深度和成交效率。

这种规模优势，也正在向传统资产衍生品市场延伸。

当然，我认为信用同样重要。

很多人谈到CEX就认为中心化一定危险，谈到DEX就认为去中心化一定安全。

这种思维在数学和概率论上显然过于简单。
当你把资产存进CEX，本质上就承担了交易所的信用风险。
在平台负有返还资产义务的结构下，用户依赖平台履约，部分法律安排还会形成对交易所的债权。
因此评价一家交易所，理应研究其资产负债表、资产储备、风险准备金以及极端情况下的偿付能力。
上周宇宙所发生历史上最大规模的被盗事件，这个规模足以对任何金融机构构成严峻的压力测试。
但币安的快速流动性补充能力，由平台承担损失，并预留超过损失金额100%的资金。截至11月3日，官方披露受影响代币资产已有98%完成补足。
对我而言，在没发生之前我比较担心，发生之后反而更放心，就像行情的假突破信号一样。
风险管理的核心，是同时衡量风险发生的概率，以及风险发生后最终损失的概率与幅度。
同样遭遇黑客攻击，资本薄弱的平台可能直接破产，拥有充足储备和偿付能力的平台则更有条件保护用户资产。
一次成功的危机应对无法保证未来绝对安全，但愿意承担损失、具备偿付能力并实际履约的历史记录，值得纳入信用评价。
这也是为什么我始终强调，投资要尊重事实，更要尊重条件概率。

反过来问一句：

DEX难道就一定没有存款风险吗？

智能合约漏洞、预言机攻击、跨链桥风险、清算机制失效、治理权限滥用，哪个没有可能造成真实损失？
链上代码公开透明，也不意味着漏洞不存在。
更现实的问题是，一旦协议遭遇重大攻击，谁来承担损失？有没有保险机制？有没有充足的赔付资金？有没有明确的追偿主体？
不同架构的风险分布不同，不能简单按照CEX和DEX两个标签判断安全性。

在其他条件相近的情况下，我更愿意相信有真实偿付记录、充足资本和明确责任主体的平台。

当然，这种信任也需要持续通过储备证明、审计和长期履约表现来检验。

金融市场最重要的信用，最终都要通过行动来证明。

从稳定币、DeFi到RWA，再到TradFi永续合约，加密行业正在不断拓展传统金融的效率边界。

我相信，未来会有越来越多传统金融资产接入加密基础设施。真正能够提高金融系统效率的技术，自然拥有长期生命力。

币安的TradFi休市行情页面，就提供了一个直观的观察窗口。交易者可以在美股休市期间，查看相关合约的价格变化与交易活跃度。(https://t.co/D2frx048j1)
当然，全天候交易意味着风险也可能全天候存在，杠杆、资金费率和清算风险仍然需要严肃对待。

技术创新拓展了交易的边界，风险管理决定了投资者能够走多远。

美股可以休市，但市场不会停止定价。

文中NVDA数据采用指定周末统计口径，衍生品交易具有高风险，不构成投资建议。

CoinFlip 在加州运营约500台加密 ATM。调查发现，它从2021年起就没有好好核实用户身份，也没能拦截可疑交易，骗子因此能诱导用户（尤其是老年人）通过它的机器转走资产。

这是加州近期整治加密 ATM 行动中的最新一起，今年5月 DFPI 已关停运营商 Hermes Bitcoin，此前还处罚过 Coinme 等公司。

text:
Alice Huang 背后的 MegaSpeed 其实大家都认识，他们的前身是开发“弹弹堂”的第七大道（对我们有什么启发？）

- 2008 年第七大道成立，然后就做出了风靡全网的“弹弹堂”

- 2011 年开始做重度游戏“神曲”，月流水 2 亿人民币

这时候他们完成第一次阶级跃升，靠的是页游的不规范野蛮生长

- 2013 年被畅游（张朝阳的公司，天龙八部开发商）收购，创始人套现离开

- 2015 年创始团队又以 2 亿美元回购公司

- 2018 年公司在香港上市

这是他们的第二次阶级跃升，从无产阶级变成上市公司，开始了资本运作

- 2023 年第七大道海外公司更名为“MegaSpeed”，这时候 Alice Huang 加入管理层

- 2023 年成立马来西亚分公司“SpeedMatrix”做算力本地部署

这是他们的第三次阶级跃升，也是算力市场的不规范，存在跨地区套利的空间

这对我们有什么启发呢？

让我想起《孤注一掷》的台词

text:
46 亿美元，13.6 万颗英伟达 GPU。

这是新加坡 AI 云公司 Megaspeed 自 2023 年成立至 2025 年 11 月的采购规模，已使其成为东南亚最大的英伟达买家之一。

这家公司不造芯片，也不训练模型，而是采购 GPU、搭建算力集群，再出租给需要算力的企业。这就是 GPU 云服务（GPUaaS），也是 Neocloud 的生意。

彭博社披露，Megaspeed 已向阿里巴巴出租英伟达芯片。但 46 亿美元只是进口额，不是营收，更不是利润。设备部署量、利用率和合同规模仍未公开。

这门生意真正拼的是资金、电力、数据中心和长期客户。GPU 买回来就开始折旧，没有稳定订单，巨额投入也可能变成负担。

CoreWeave 已证明这门生意可以做到数十亿美元规模，但 Megaspeed 能否复制，最终要看能否让 GPU 持续运转、持续产生现金流。

AI 基建的机会，不只在造芯片，也在出租算力。

quoted_text:
明天 @Enter_Elysium 就上主网了，简单聊聊为什么这条链值得关注，以及我个人正在关注哪些项目。

（一）关注逻辑

Elysium 是 @Kinetiq_xyz 构建的一条 Hyperliquid 高性能 L2，特点是用 hyperliquid:native 作为 Gas、结算回 HyperEVM ，且吞吐量目标远高于 HyperEVM。由于 Hyperliquid 的结构和生态定位的特殊性，个人觉得不能简单地将 Elysium 归纳为又一条 EVM L2 的故事，它值得关注的理由恰恰也与 Hyperliquid 息息相关，其实可以列很多，这里主要说两点：

> hyperliquid:native 的财富效应还在，叙事也在升级，当前 HyperEVM 的应用密度/体验明显不够，生态资深用户/鲸鱼需要更好的投机与应用出口
> 构建了完整的代币生命周期：代币发行 → AMM 深度 → HyperCore Spot → Perps

主网正式上线前的 Private mainnet 以及各家 Launchpad 搭 RPC 抢跑，确实透支过一部分注意力了，但结合链上数据也恰恰说明了市场对它的预期还不错，并且整个运行逻辑并没有改变，因此个人依然会持续关注其主网上线后的表现和发展。

（二）值得关注的项目

目前大家看到最多的生态项目大概就是 Launchpad 了，据 @ElysiumEco 显示，光是 Launchpad 的数量就高达接近 40 个了。前面 Robinhood Chain 已经向大家展示了这一品类的潜力和财富效应，所以数量多个人并不意外，但毕竟注意力有限，不可能每个都关注，个人目前主要在关注下面这些项目。

> @AscendLaunch ：Elysium 上最先把流量打出来的 Launchpad 之一，创始人是 @CryptoTomYT ，11/4 解开官网密码限流做压测后贡献了不错的数据，当天交易量超 $5M 量级。更为重要的是，它在费用侧把 kinetiq:native  的回购比例拉到 80%，按照 @0xSleepinRain 的说法，这体现了生态内应用与公链代币的一致性，而 Ascend 起了一个很好的生态示范作用。

Ascend 没有自己的官方代币，但会有一个 NFT 并且还有一个生态孵化器用于支持生态项目，这决定了它更像是一个生态入口，而不仅仅只是发射台。值得一提的是，今天 Ascend 上发射的 $e/acc @eacc_coin 已经拍下了 HyperCore Spot Ticker。

> @MontraXYZ ：另一个主要 Launchpad，定位 House of launches，Private mainnet 阶段占据了最大的市场份额，超过 60% 的代币都是从 Montra 上发射出来的，日交易量在千万级别。在今天的 $e/acc 之前，Elysium 生态中的两个主要 Runner $EACCAT 和 $CHAMELEON 都是 Montra 上的。值得一提的是，Montra 提供自定义的 Launch 规则配置，包括代币如何铸造、市场如何开启、费用如何运作等，而不是单一的结构。

Montra 将发行自己的代币 $MONTRA ，并有一个空投计划，总量的 25% 将用于社区空投，主要分成五块：HYPE/KNTQ/Elysium 活跃用户、早期创作者与交易者、Top 10 token 持有者、LP、内容/推荐，目前官网已有 Airdrop 积分页。

> @quoted_xyz ：和前面两个 Launchpad 不一样的是，Quoted 专注的是「用什么来报价」。每个新代币不是简单跟 HYPE 配对，而是可以被股票、商品或杠杆仓位 quote，比如 SPY、QQQ、黄金、白银、Brent，以及现货 hyperliquid:native / kinetiq:native，跑在 Uniswap v4 上。个人觉得这条线和 Robinhood Chain 上的股票代币叙事是同构的：流动性本身变成可发行、可收费的产品形态。

更值得关注的点是它在往「Be the quote」走：可以把 Vault（含最多 8 腿的 3x 杠杆仓位组合）直接做成 quote 对，别人在上面发射/交易，你吃交易费的一部分；官方也说会把国库和后续费用换成 kinetiq:native 并在主网 Day1 做 LP。 $QUOTED 目前已在 Elysium 上线，属于少数把 TradFi×Crypto 机制先跑起来的应用。

> @Bound_Exchange ：Bound 做的是一种叫 Boundaries 的交易原语，选市场、设上下界、锁定固定赔付，哪个价先碰到就结算，没有到期日，也可以中途按报价提前平仓。本质上是把「图表上的一段路径判断」直接变成一笔可表达、可复制的仓位，介于永续深度和预测市场赔付之间。产品目前主要跑在 HyperEVM，Bio 写明即将上线  Elysium；创始人 @benny_options 也提到，HyperEVM 上 Keeper 的 Gas 成本并不便宜，Elysium 的低 Gas + 更直接的 Hyperliquid 接入为他们提供了更好的构建环境。

这种项目值得关注的地方是可以用来观察 Elysium 到底能不能真正承接这种依赖 Hyperliquid 深度、又对 Gas/延迟敏感的新原语，期待在 Elysium 主网上线后的表现。

> @eloscapeHQ ：Eloscape 的定位是 Elysium 上的 Virtual Mining /价值沉淀协议，官方 Slogan 就是 Value consolidation on Elysium。玩法大致是：每一轮（约 60 秒）把 hyperliquid:native 部署到网格上，链上随机结算，过程中挖出 $ELO；领取挖矿所得会有手续费，质押 $ELO 则参与协议收入分配。和纯 meme 发射不同，它更像是在给生态做一个持续消耗 HYPE、再把价值沉到协议代币上的资金漏斗。

目前项目还未上线，也还没有代币，看共同关注应该是个还蛮有潜力的项目，保持关注。

> @kalosfun ：定位是 Elysium 上的一站式交易终端——Meme sniping、Swap、做 LP、扫 NFT/drops，再到 Social，都想收进同一个入口。Bio 就是 Trade anything on @Enter_Elysium；官方生态页也把它归在 Launchpads + DeFi。它是 @AscendLaunch Builder Incubator 的第一个入选项目，和 Ascend 的绑定比较深，个人会把它当成「发射台之外的流量承接层」来看。

Genesis NFT（1,500 枚）已在 11/4 售罄，官方定价 $25，对应未来 $KALOS 总量约 10%，并计划 11/9 空投到钱包。主网上线后，还会有积分计划。

NFT 的话可以关注 @Elyziumaa @slymzcrew ，就不过多介绍了，感兴趣可以自己去看看。

以上就是个人的一些看法和关注的项目，打法上也相对简单，优先看有创新、能接住 HYPE 资本溢出、又能把费用/叙事回流到 KNTQ/HYPE 的相关项目，期待主网明天的上线。

最后，朋友做了一个 Elysium meme 信息聚合 & 交易小工具 @ElySignal ，如果这篇内容对你有所帮助，欢迎帮忙点点关注和参与体验，目前还在持续优化中，有任何建议也可以直接跟我提~

i forgot about this until @ScottWu46 reminded me, but back in january 2017 when we were 19, scott and i had lunch in SF

at lunch, we talked about how our IMO/IOI/math competition gang could be the next paypal mafia. i knew the competition kids were geniuses by any standard, and felt confident in time we could take the tech world by storm

fast forward nearly 10 years later, and many of our friends from that time are some of the most exciting people in AI and technology (@ScottWu46, @akshat_b, @chameleon_jeff, Jerry Ma, @randomjohnnyh, @0xShitTrader, @stevenkplus1, @thejessezhang, @vickie_ye_, @alexwei_, @demi_guo_, @d_m_ziegler, @hughbzhang, @_mohansolo, @MarkSellke, and many others i'm sure i'm forgetting)

i'm now at that age where i reminisce about everyone i grew up with, and i've known most of these people since middle school (via MATHCOUNTS!). even though we were scattered around the country, we would gchat about math problems and hang out on AoPS, then we did math/algo camps together, and then we did internships together.

very crazy to think about the degree of sheer brilliance of this group when we were just teenagers, and so special to see so many go on to leave their mark on the world.

note to parents: if your kid is on gchat all day solving math problems with some anonymous group of cross-country asian kids, (s)he may just turn out alright.

text:
美银首席策略师Michael Hartnett在最新一期周报中，将2026年中期选举定性为“AI股票集中度见顶”的历史节点，上调明年超大规模云厂商资本开支预期，预示未来现金流恶化。美银还为明年初债务上限做准备，看多黄金。

根据美银7月全球基金经理调查，七成投资者认为中期选举前美联储不会加息，八成认为民主党不会横扫，九成认为AI资本开支不会削减。而这些预期正在逐一被打破，美联储9月已经加息，民主党中期选举完成横扫，而随着多位民主党当选州长承诺暂停数据中心建设，“AI资本开支不会削减”的信念也岌岌可危。

Hartnett的市场逻辑是，云计算大厂资本开支高企，现金流急剧恶化（美银一周内将2027年超大规模云厂商资本开支从1.2万亿美元上调至1.3万亿）。债券市场期待AI资本开支放缓；科技债券将跑赢科技股，利空芯片、云计算建设端，利好AI使用方资产负债表。

芯片股方面，费城半导体指数目前跌至200日均线下方 17%，根据历史规律，优质买点一般在20%‑25%区间；英伟达、台积电ADR均跌破关键支撑价位，仍有进一步调整空间。

在宏观交易方面，美银押注黄金，警惕债务上限危机，理由是2027年2月美国或将触及41.1万亿美元债务上限，而历史上前两次债务上限博弈前三个月黄金大幅上涨，黄金从当前约4000美元起算，有望在债务上限博弈高峰期触及4500至4700美元区间。

在中期选举后，Hartnett的交易清单方向是黄金 > 石油、收益率下行、科技债券 > 科技股、消费股 > 能源股、小盘股 > 垄断股、做多欧洲、做多中国科技股。

美银对标普500是否会崩盘设定了三个衰退预警指标，分别是银行ETF（IXG）守住125美元、中小盘ETF（MDY）守住666美元、高收益债ETF（JNK）守住92美元。而MDY目前已告破，而且需要警惕的是，标普500目前距离Hartnett“全球广度法则”买入信号触发线（7323点）仅不足1%。

#观察 得克萨斯州翻蓝，对数据中心和AI题材带来更负面影响，可以预见未来项目审批放缓及监管收紧，延缓得州作为美国AI算力主要增长极的角色。

民主党人Gina Hinojosa击败共和党州长Greg Abbott，成为自1990年以来首位民主党州长。在竞选期间，她多次呼吁立刻暂停数据中心开发、取消税收优惠和补贴，并指责开发商推高居民电价以及消耗大量水资源，呼吁暂停审批，直到州议会出台优先保障得州民众利益的法案。

目前得州约占美国计划数据中心容量的26%左右，短期延迟会拖累全国2027-2028年新增算力交付。而“结束税收优惠”，以及“强制承担全部电网升级成本”政纲的落实，会显著增加资本和运营成本。

Jefferies等机构的分析师估计，禁令可能使约13.3 GW已宣布项目面临延迟或取消风险。缺环境许可的项目可能推迟12-18个月，无电力或无许可的项目会转移到路易斯安那、俄克拉荷马或其他州，甚至取消。

text:
老黄这事，大家别只当吃瓜看。🧐

表面上是出轨认错，董事会查一查。但我越看越觉得，这根本不是一个私德问题，背后的博弈，比八卦精彩多了！

先说事实：
• 老黄给员工发信，承认对妻子不忠
• 对方是 Megaspeed 前高管，美国情报部门怀疑她被中国方面招募
• 董事会成立独立委员会，请外部律师调查
• 国会三个委员会要求他11月18日去闭门汇报
• 董事会还特意强调：目前没有证据显示机密泄露

咱们看看，一个没有证据的事，为什么要闹这么大？

我的看法，有这么几层：

1️⃣ 先把人设砸了，再谈权力

你想想，私德问题最好用在哪？就是最容易让人闭嘴的地方。老黄自己都认了，那他在后面谈判的底气就没了。想扣帽子，一个“间谍风险”就够了，不需要真有证据。

2️⃣ 真正的靶子是对华芯片政策

别忘了，老黄这两年最大的诉求，就是让美国放开对中国的先进芯片出口。他一直在游说，一直在喊“中国市场不能丢”。

现在好了，一个“可能被中国情报盯上”的标签贴上去，他再去喊放开出口，谁还敢听？说什么都带着嫌疑。这一手，等于直接把他从政策谈判桌上请了下去。

3️⃣ 英伟达太大了，大到让人睡不着

• 10月市值接近5.8万亿美金
• 最近回落到5万亿以下
• 没有接班计划，也没有明显接班人
• 公司靠老黄一个人说了算

一家5万亿的公司，所有决策都压在一个人身上，华盛顿怎么可能放心？这次调查，我觉得很大概率是想把治理结构改一改，往董事会里塞更多有政界背景的人，让英伟达变得更听话。

4️⃣ 时间点也很有意思

17号英伟达就要发财报，市场正在担心AI泡沫。这个时候爆出来，情绪面、估值面都会被放大。有人想借机施压，也说得通。

那老黄接下来会怎么走？

我猜大概是这三步：
• 短期：认错+配合，把事情定性为私德问题，死死守住别往国家安全上靠
• 中期：让点权，多引入独立董事，主动接受审查，换CEO位置
• 长期：对华策略只能越来越保守，站队站得更明显

说句心里话，这件事最大的影响，不是老黄个人，而是AI产业的格局。中间地带越来越窄，英伟达被迫往美国阵营靠，中国这边只会更坚定地走国产算力的路。

当然，调查结果还没出来，目前也没有证据证明机密泄露，咱们别把阴谋论当结论。但从资本和政治的角度看，这场博弈，绝对不简单。

对我们美股投资者来说，17号英伟达财报，18日国会简报会，是两个关键节点，注意风险，控制仓位。

以上纯属个人观点，DYOR🙏

text:
加州金融保护与创新部：责令 Coinflip 补偿比特币 ATM 诈骗受害者

加州金融保护与创新部（DFPI）责令加密货币 ATM 运营商 Coinflip 向当地诈骗受害者赔偿超 480 万美元，并向监管机构支付超 35 万美元非法收取的超额费用。该命令涉及其在加州运营的约 500 台设备，并要求其停止违法行为。

调查发现，自 2021 年以来，Coinflip 未能充分识别用户，也未能有效发现、预防、报告和缓解可疑活动。相关交易还超过加州每日 1000 美元的客户限额，且存在购买前未提供书面披露、收据信息不完整等问题。

DFPI 表示，诈骗者会冒充可信机构，谎称账户或电脑存在问题，诱导受害者提取现金并通过附近的 ATM 转移资金；受害者扫描二维码购买的加密货币会被转入诈骗者钱包。监管机构指出，老年人尤其容易成为此类骗局的目标。

text:
六家 AI 巨头的组织架构背后

OpenAI：资本驱动的层级式数据生产
顶层制定目标，中间拆解任务，底层执行标注、评估、反馈和数据处理。这种模式的优势是能够建立标准化、规模化的生产流程，把复杂的模型训练需求拆解成大量可执行的工作。

Anthropic：安全治理与业务训练之间的隔阂
Anthropic 的技术路线长期重视人类反馈、偏好建模和安全训练。但安全究竟是训练体系的底层能力，还是一个独立于业务之外的审查部门？如果 Safety Team 只负责最后的审核和否决，那么它可能成为研发效率的瓶颈。如果安全约束真正进入数据采集、模型训练、评估和部署的每个环节，那么安全才是整个研发系统的一部分

Google DeepMind：研究网络与 Benchmark 驱动
DeepMind 最强的地方是研究网络，多个研究团队之间存在交叉协作。不同研究方向之间可以共享技术和资源。Benchmark 是衡量进展、连接不同研究方向的重要工具。这很符合 DeepMind 长期以来的研究导向。从 AlphaGo、AlphaFold 到 Gemini，Google DeepMind 的研究传统并不只是训练一个更大的语言模型，而是尝试把不同领域的研究方法、算法和评价体系连接起来

Meta：产品矩阵驱动的用户反馈闭环
nstagram、Facebook、WhatsApp 分别对应不同的模型或数据生产集群，底部则是大量用户。它拥有大规模、多场景、多模态的产品入口。Instagram 有图像、视频和创作者内容；Facebook 有社交关系、内容互动和社区；WhatsApp 有通讯场景。这些产品能够为 AI 产品提供完全不同的使用场景和反馈入口

xAI：极端中心化的单点驱动模式

author: bajpaiharsh244
quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

There’s a REAL software company, an open-source product, and a business model behind it.

Gadlus LLC is the parent company behind Letronna AND AILE.

✅ Letronna: An AI agent that writes code, deploys applications, manages cloud infrastructure, and pays for APIs.

✅ AILE: A live marketplace for affordable AI model access.

✅ Open-source Rust infrastructure: Over 2,300 commits on GitHub.

✅ Working desktop and terminal alpha: Real software people can download and use TODAY.

✅ Persistent cloud workers: Agents can deploy bots and applications that continue operating even after your computer shuts down.

✅ Real token utility: The published $LETRO model includes 50% of hosted-model margins allocated to future buybacks and 10% burns when LETRO is spent on credits.

Here’s the BIGGER picture:

Most AI coding agents help you BUILD software.

Letronna wants to help you BUILD, DEPLOY, HOST, and OPERATE that software autonomously.

That’s a much bigger opportunity.

One prompt becomes a working application.

That application becomes a recurring service.

Recurring services generate ongoing compute and model spending.

And that creates the potential for REAL revenue and token value capture.

This is exactly the direction I believe Agentic Finance is heading.

We’re moving from AI agents that simply answer questions to agents that actually perform work and manage their own expenses.

$LETRO is still early and needs to prove sustainable adoption, but the foundation is becoming increasingly interesting.

REAL builders. REAL products. REAL utility.

One to watch closely. 🤝

🇨🇳BREAKING: Researchers in China achieved internet transmission speeds fast enough to download 20,000 4K movies in ONE SECOND.

The team set a world record in optical fiber transmission by achieving the world’s FIRST real-time, two-way transmission over 1,000 km of hollow-core fiber.

The 1,007.48-km link carried 64 terabits per second in each direction simultaneously, equivalent to 160 movies per second in each direction at 50 GB per movie.

A signal crossed 1,000 km in just 3.43 milliseconds. Light travels through the fiber’s hollow center, cutting travel time by about 30% compared with conventional glass fiber.

This is a massive breakthrough, especially for AI data centers hundreds of kilometers apart, where latency and bandwidth between facilities directly affect the efficiency of large-model training and inference.

quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
Banks Can Move to Onchain Rails, Beyond Just Stablecoins and Tokenized Deposits

Cross River is a US bank based in New Jersey that works behind the scenes for fintech companies like Affirm, Upstart and Coinbase. Last week it announced, together with Offchain (the company behind Arbitrum), that loan it makes will also be issued as a token on the Arbitrum One blockchain at the moment the loan is created.

Here is why that is different.

1/ Today, when a loan gets tokenized, the loan already exists in the bank's own systems, gets bundled with other loans, and a token is created at the end to represent the bundle. The token is a copy of a record that lives somewhere else.

2/ Cross River flips this. The token is the loan record from the start, so who funded it, who owns it, and what the borrower has repaid are all written in one place. No one has to reconcile the bank's books, the investor's books and the token afterwards.

3/ What does not change is the regulated part. Cross River is still the lender, it still does the underwriting and compliance checks the same way, and borrowers still use the same app they use today. They will never see a wallet or a blockchain.

4/ What changes is what happens after the loan is made. Investors can buy loans one by one as they are created instead of waiting for a batch, they can buy in smaller amounts, and funds that already operate onchain, including investors outside the US, can buy directly.

The takeaway for banks is that the first onchain products were payments (stablecoins) and deposits (tokenized deposits) however this shows a bank can put its core lending product onchain too, while keeping every regulated function exactly where it is.

This is ultimately a distribution strategy, and great move from Cross River when most are just focused on stablecoins and tokenized deposits.

*Interesting announcement from @GillesGade

text:
I agree! Lots of pareto improvements.

Top few I see are:

1. DC available chain (current PQ roadmap) only has a few hundred validators in the hot path of each slot. Consensus time ~= log(validator count), so going from 30k vals -> 500 is plausibly a 2x speed boost.
2. Erasure coded P2P improves expected propagation time of big objects with no downside except some code complexity (which is manageable, esp given that this is not consensus code)
3. Few-slot finality. PQ sig aggregation is able to handle a message from every validator per round, and even at very conservative params (eg. ~5 rounds of aggregation, 1m validators) current math/simulations imply finality in under a minute (compare: 2.5 epochs = 16 min avg finality today)

So effectively, significant efficiency gains are part of the (currently understood) PQ security roadmap "for free"

text:
gonna take a shot in the dark here (barely woke up) and say that maybe assets become SoV/money not when they have certain fixed properties, but when they become the best version of themselves

Think portfolio optimisation. You want to hold a basket of assets so risk isn’t concentrated (very simplified). Given an existing basket, if I’m a contender as an asset, should I aim to look more like every other asset in the basket? I would argue no, and I would argue I should also aim to be the best in my category. The more novel the category, the better, because my risk vector points away from those already in the basket.

So what does it mean for ETH? Well it’s the native asset of a network that has PoS and is fully programmable. These are sensible choices for a network whose aim is to offer maximum security and maximum utility! And it’s possible that we’re simply cursed to deliver the best settlement layer the world has ever had, and that even if we do succeed, it’s still only a necessary condition for ETH to succeed.

text:
ZEROBASE WEEKLY 11.2-11.8

ZBT remained under selling pressure during November 2–8, declining from approximately $0.070 to $0.059–$0.061 by the weekend. The token traded between $0.0585 and $0.0704, with brief stabilization attempts failing to sustain a recovery. Weekly trading volume totaled approximately $17.7 million, averaging $2.5 million daily.

The cryptocurrency market faced another difficult week as political uncertainty, institutional outflows, and macroeconomic developments weighed on sentiment. Total market capitalization declined from approximately $2.61 trillion toward $2.5 trillion, while Bitcoin dominance remained near 60%. Most major altcoins recorded weekly losses.

Bitcoin started around $77,000–$78,000 and briefly climbed above $80,000 on November 4, reaching $81,000 before reversing. Selling pressure pushed BTC below $76,000 and toward $73,700 on Sunday, its weakest levels since August.

Ethereum followed a similar pattern, rising toward $2,445 during the midweek rebound before retreating. Selling accelerated on November 5, pushing ETH toward $2,230, with weakness continuing through the weekend. Both assets struggled to sustain gains amid market uncertainty.

The November 3 U.S. midterm election saw Democrats secure both chambers of Congress, raising questions about digital asset regulation and market structure legislation. While several crypto-supported candidates won, high-profile defeats highlighted the limits of political campaign spending.

Security concerns persisted following the October 29 Binance breach involving approximately $6.34 billion in unauthorized transfers. On November 3, Binance reported that $2.85 billion had been frozen or intercepted, with 98% of impacted token assets replenished as of October 31. Investigations remained ongoing.

The breach renewed scrutiny of exchange custody and counterparty risks. On November 7, Binance announced CFO Kaiser Ng's departure and Justin Yek's appointment. Although described as planned, the transition attracted attention amid continued security concerns.

Institutional ETF flows remained negative. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $1.28 billion in net outflows during November 2–6, with BlackRock's IBIT accounting for significant redemptions. Spot Ethereum ETFs also saw approximately $365 million in weekly withdrawals.

Macroeconomic conditions added pressure. The November 6 U.S. employment report showed October payrolls rising by 165,000, above expectations of 65,000, while unemployment declined to 4.1%. Treasury yields and the dollar strengthened, with December Fed rate increase expectations approaching 78%.

U.S. equities declined despite Friday's partial rebound. The S&P 500 closed at 7,376.86, down 2.7% weekly, while the Nasdaq fell 3.4% to 24,579.42. Technology stocks faced pressure from valuation concerns, regulatory uncertainty, and elevated capital spending.

Across crypto markets, ETF outflows, political uncertainty, and security concerns constrained recovery attempts. Bitcoin's inability to maintain $80,000 reinforced resistance, while the Fear & Greed Index declined toward 28, indicating cautious sentiment.

The week ended with Bitcoin testing two-month lows, Ethereum reversing its recovery, and institutional flows remaining negative. Attention now shifts to the November 10 U.S. inflation report, regulatory developments, and the Binance investigation. Sustained recovery will depend on improved liquidity, stabilized ETF flows, and easing selling pressure.

text:
PLEASE STOP FUCKING WITH ETHEREUM WITHOUT ASKING THE PEOPLE WHO BUILD ON IT: FIVE REASONS I AM TIRED

[feat. Wildcat Labs, a company that is filled with Ethereum die-hards and works exclusively on code that has originated over a billion dollars of economic activity for the chain, but these are my opinions not that of Labs itself etc]

---

REASON ONE: Our entire market deployment flow breaks on day one of Glamsterdam

Wildcat's core product involves a borrower creating a market that they've specified the way that they determine is best for them. That includes the core market itself (interest rate, underlying asset, debt token name), and a separate configuration (through hooks) granting access to the market and its functions (i.e. who can deposit, can debt be transferred, are withdrawal requests subject to a fixed-term tenor and so on).

In our currently deployed, immutable V2 code, what used to be a single transaction bundling those things together goes from 8.6M gas to ~62-71M, which means we can't fit it into a 60M block (don't you dare 'but ackshually' me, I am coming back to this).

Nothing in our contracts changed: the chain reprices bytecode deposits by 7.65x underneath already-audited code. We only have a workaround because our factory happens to expose the two halves separately, so we need to boot out an SDK and frontend release, plus pray folk are using a wallet that will sign a 35M gas field.

Every borrower's first market to date used a call that will no longer fit in a block as-is (I said I'm coming back to it).

The reason I am starting to... express opinions, is that this is the second time in a year that the execution layer has changed what a deployed contract costs to use (EIP-7825's cap in Fusaka, now state gas), and each time the burden of discovering it lands on us, the teams developing applications that drive economic activity on the chain, and we have to do it by replaying our own history on a testnet.

[This is going to be a long post. I am Not Pleased.]

---

REASON TWO: We are relying on social consensus for any hope of relief

The repricing aspect is consensus: at the fork, every validator must enforce it. The gas limit - the thing that would make a ~70M transaction possible post-Glamsterdam - is a validator-set preference with no mainnet schedule.

Sepolia was handed 200M, and things look fine over there. Hoodi had its 200M yeeted out the airlock the day the fork was postponed. So, the testnet that "proves" the fork works runs with over three times the headroom of mainnet, but the fork's own design assumes a headroom that nobody has committed to.

For a protocol that needs to tell institutional borrowers what a market costs to open, Wildcat's honest answer after Glamsterdam has to be "it depends on a social campaign to change validator config files," and that isn't a dependency that a credit product should carry. We are engineers, not lobbyists.

It also means Wildcat's capacity planning is hostage to the same ACD calls that are currently stalled on a security review of the very EIP that created the problem. 

You know what, Ameen, you are a core dev now. Why not.

---

REASON THREE: As-is, Safe App deployments of mainnet Wildcat markets fail after the fork

Safes are the default custody mechanism for exactly the borrowers Wildcat wants, and just over a third of V2 markets (29 of 82) were deployed via one.

Under EIP-8037, the GAS opcode no longer reports the reservoir, so a Safe's execution check (GS010) can never be satisfied for a transaction that needs more than the execution cap.

On either deploy entrypoint: the core market itself or its hooks.

Historical Wildcat Safe deployments set safeTxGas to zero and survive. The Safe App and safe-apps-provider path set it from the estimate... and die. :)

We can patch our own route (send safeTxGas 0, which our testnet branch already does), and we will. What nobody owns is the default: every Safe App on Ethereum that lets the provider fill safeTxGas from an estimate above ~16.4M dies in the same way.

This is not Wildcat's bug, nor is it Safe's in any useful sense.

It is a consensus change that silently invalidates a safety check in the most widely deployed smart-contract wallet on Ethereum, with no deprecation path, and as of today nobody owns fixing it. Building on a platform where our users' wallets can be broken by a gas-accounting EIP is something that every single protocol team should be screaming things that would get us put on trial in The Hague about.

---

REASON FOUR: Every single part of the tooling stack currently assumes tx.gas stops before the reservoir

Fusaka taught Ethereum developers that a transaction cannot exceed 16.78M, and so tooling calcified around that number because... why wouldn't it? It's not even a year old yet!

As it stands, geth's default 50M RPC cap can't estimate the combined deploy of a Wildcat V2 market, and public nodes cap eth_call the same way.

Even our own release ceremony prices contract deployments statically at 200 gas per byte against the 1,530 already live on Sepolia (our simulation gate catches it, the planner doesn't).

Glamsterdam now says the gas field can be 4.29 billion, with the part above 16.78M living in a reservoir that neither GAS nor most estimators nor any wallet UI understands yet.

When our V2.5 audit is done and it's time for us to deploy the necessary factories, the install is sixteen transactions and about six blocks' worth of gas, at most one big creation per block, and every wallet and integrator that Wildcat touches has to re-learn gas at the same time.

With no shared reference implementation.

None of this is Wildcat's code, all of it is Wildcat's outage, and the execution layer will have shipped two contradictory gas models in consecutive forks.

Masterful gambit.

[and this last one's just me being me about my most hated and well-known bugbear]

---

REASON FIVE: Code bytes are now 96 percent of what one of our markets costs to deploy, but the spec is still moving

I have spent coming up ten years - near enough since its introduction - begging for the death of EIP-170, and I genuinely don't know why I dared to believe that anything except a monkey's paw would answer me.

At 1,530 gas per byte, the cost of deploying a V2.5 market (when it launches) is almost entirely the price of copying 23 KB of bytecode into state. A lender’s first deposit to a Wildcat market costs about 3x the gas it would pre-Glamsterdam, because every fresh storage slot went from 22,100 gas to 110,020.

EIP-7954's promised 64 KB contracts are capped in practice at about 38 KB by a 60M block, so the one concession to builders in this fork - the one I have been asking for since my age first started leading with a 3 - is muted on mainnet until the aforementioned social campaign gets the gas limit bumped to 200M. Which we have to take on faith right now.

Meanwhile, the refill and reservoir semantics of EIP-8037 are under review, Hoodi is unscheduled and mainnet has no date, which means that Wildcat Labs just paid six figures to get Wildcat V2.5 into external audit against gas semantics that may change before it ships.

The cost - and the apparent lesson - of being an early, careful team on Ethereum is that you run the risk of needing to audit twice: once against the chain you deploy to, and once against the chain it becomes.

---

WHAT WE ARE DOING ABOUT THIS: Upcoming SDK and frontend releases will, defensively and until we can safely revert to type, split market creation into two transactions and send safeTxGas 0 on the Safe App route. Existing markets will keep running. Lenders will be affected in cost only: first touches (first deposit, opening a withdrawal request, first approval) about 2-3x, everything else 1.1-1.6x. What we cannot do is make a 65M transaction fit in a 60M block.

That part is on you lot, the social layer.

Further to the above, Wildcat Labs will happily send an invoice for an audit rebate to anyone willing to provide it if we end up having to re-check things for V2.5 once semantics are finalised.

Mind you, we'd provide an EOA, as we're a bit wary of anything contract-based right now.

Enjoy your Sundays.

Now you know.

text:
Vitalik declaring Ether as a memetic store of value is a consequence of the path he started on years ago. I spelled this out at the start of the year. 

It actually has a close parallel to Bitcoin. Originally conceived to be a payments system, the governance gridlock eventually drove out all those who wanted to make it more practically useful. The end result is that only those in the community who are ok with the gridlock stay. And the only application that we know of that doesn't require much active development is a memetic store of value.
author: dankrad
quoted_text:
This is a good post.

Not because I agree with it, directionally I disagree with a lot. But Vitalik is finally telling people what he actually believes, and an indication on how he intends to run the Ethereum Foundation. This creates transparency for those around him, and means those who disagree can now evaluate if this is the right place for them. Long overdue.

I think it is worth understanding what this strategy means for Ethereum, and I might write something about it in the future :)

In short: The only major asset that really benefits from this extreme version of self-sovereignty and trustlessness that he describes is Ether. I fear that the fully executed version of this strategy is going to result in Ethereum just becoming another version of Bitcoin "digital gold" (technically an improvement, but IMO tiny in terms of what crypto can actually do for the world).

I don't know if Vitalik actually cares that much about Ether, though -- I think he thinks more about other applications, e.g. social and identity systems. I am highly critical of basing Ethereum's strategy on those, because none of them have anything close to PMF and there are good reasons to believe that's going to be extremely hard.

(And yeah, I do have a suggestion for an alternative strategy for Ethereum: Get as much valuable economic activity on L1 as possible. I think that would be ultimately the better strategy for Ethereum being a core building block of a more transparent and inclusive financial system)

老黄的出轨大瓜背后，其实藏着一个近50亿美元的“跨境算力租赁”大棋。

今天大家都在讨论黄仁勋的这个桃色新闻可能对 $NVDA 股价的影响，但事件中女方 Alice Huang 曾担任高管的新加坡企业 Megaspeed 更值得深挖。

据《海峡时报》等媒体溯源，Megaspeed 的前身其实是中国游戏公司第七大道（7Road）的新加坡海外实体。

- 2023 年 3 月，公司更名并将股权转入 Alice Huang 控制的 BVI 公司；
-2023 年 11 月，股权再次转给一家新加坡空壳公司，Alice 随即辞去董事。
-巧合的是，在这场转让完成仅数日后，Megaspeed 就被正式列为“英伟达云合作伙伴”。

而在成为合作伙伴之后，据 Bloomberg 及贸易数据平台 ImportGenius 的追踪：

该公司及其马来西亚关联实体在2-3年内，花费 48 亿美元，购买十多万张包含 H100、H200 在内的英伟达顶配 GPU，并将它们密集部署在马来西亚和印尼的数据中心里。

随后，Megaspeed 走通了当前 AI 供应链中最核心的商业模式：

第三国远程算力租赁。

在物理上，这些显卡合法合规地留在东南亚机房；但在网络端，它们产生的庞大算力，正通过云服务远程租给需求方；

据纽约时报报道，Megaspeed 持续为其主要客户阿里巴巴提供云服务，并且其在马来西亚的关联实体也与阿里巴巴存在相关的业务与财务往来。

目前，这一动向已引来美国商务部和新加坡当局的调查，不过英伟达坚称此前已做过核查，未发现设备被违规转运。

这种模式下，芯片没有过境但算力已经出海；想起之前国内的 token 出海，形成了一种微妙的对比。

在不断加码的物理禁运与庞大的算力需求之间，资本和技术总在寻找那条最有效的流动路径。

从币安孵化营的 8 个项目之一，到自己的代币登上纳斯达克，@injective 用了八年。

11 月 5 日，Canary Capital 发行的 ethereum:0xe28b3b32b6c345a34ff64674606124dd5aceca30 质押 ETF（INJC）登陆纳斯达克。曾经那个想绕开传统金融体系的年轻团队，如今把自己的代币送进了传统金融市场。

2018 年，19 岁的 Eric Chen @ericinjective 和团队挤在纽约一间仅 7 平米的小屋里，拿着币安孵化营的 50 万美元，在熊市中寻找第一个用户。

当时他们想解决的只是一个问题：如何让链上交易不再被抢跑。

八年后，Injective 的故事已经完全变了。

它不再只是一条去中心化交易公链，而是开始把贝莱德基金、加拿大房贷、跨国贸易应收账款、股票和稳定币搬上链，甚至自己注册成为 SEC 认可的转让代理。

从反对金融中间商，到亲自进入华尔街的金融基础设施体系。

最有意思的是，Eric Chen 似乎从来没打算只做一条加密公链。

八年时间，Injective 从一个解决交易公平性问题的协议，变成了试图连接华尔街、链上金融与 AI Agent 的金融基础设施。

屠龙少年最终穿上了华尔街的西装，但他想做的，可能是把整座华尔街搬上链。

text:
币安「UID 撞号」引发全网大辩论，请看双方辩手的主要观点👇

背景：用户 @1ts_hodlkitty 想把资金从币安主站转到币安泰国站，在主站直接输入 UID 完成转账，转出 11,398.77 USDT 后钱进入主站另一用户账户。

正方：更强调用户核对责任

一辩 @heyibinance | XHunt全球排名：181
核心观点：币安主站与泰国、土耳其、美国等本地法币站因历史合规原因完全独立开发，账号体系不共享，不支持跨站 UID 转账（也从未支持过）。主站内 UID 唯一，不存在撞号。用户跨站时直接在主站输入 UID，属于操作失误；平台已有二次确认（展示头像、昵称等），用户未仔细核对。事发后已第一时间冻结资金并持续联系收款方，但对方不活跃，且平台依法无法直接从他人账户强制划转。于情个人会补贴用户损失，同时将在币安支付转账增加三次确认。欢迎社区提出产品改进建议。

二辩 土澳大狮兄 @BroLeon | XHunt全球排名：905
核心观点：币安 UID 转账需要确认对方头像、UID 对应昵称、面部识别等多个环节，流程没啥问题。用户转错钱自己怎么可能完全没有责任呢？理解惯性思维，但不能完全赖币安头上。币安愿意垫钱补偿可以理解，但用户必须承认自己疏忽大意。自己的钱自己更该重视，转钱出去都该核对三遍。

三辩 熬鹰资本 @thankUcrypto | XHunt全球排名：1473
核心观点：币安 UID 转账会展示头像、昵称，大额转给陌生账户还需要再次输入 UID，不能跳过用户是否认真核对。反对「按闹分配」，不能因为公开投诉就改变资金处理原则。

四辩 jiayi 加一 @mscryptojiayi（前币安员工） | XHunt全球排名：1878
核心观点：类比王者荣耀国服与海外服，你知道不同服务器对应不同 ID，却默认跨站用 UID 能直接转，且两次强制确认都不看，这是自己资产自己不小心。自己资产自己小心，不能靠事后闹就指望平台赔偿。换其他交易所未必有人理你。

五辩 Ron @Ron521520 | XHunt全球排名：20717
核心观点：主站与本地站本就是独立系统，UID 不通用是公开信息。个人补贴可以做，但不能变成默认责任，否则口子一开后续会有更多人把粗心甩给平台。建议在 UID 输入时增加实时站点识别+强制提醒，而非单纯堆确认次数。

六辩 jack_hu @jackhu_bangzhu | XHunt全球排名：90154
核心观点：何一说是跨 App 转泰区误把 UID 当地址，不是撞号；钱已冻，还要加第三道确认。主站、泰区账不共享——像不同所同名币，界面一家，清算各走各的。冻得住资金，冻不住手滑。你内转最后核 UID 还是地址？

反方：更强调平台防错机制

一辩 @star_okx | XHunt全球排名：236
核心观点：同一品牌下的不同站点，UID 应做到全局唯一；否则就不该允许仅凭 UID 进行跨站内部转账。同一串数字在不同站点可能对应不同账户，容易造成收款识别错误。产品设计应在底层减少用户犯错空间，而不是把责任主要推给用户核对。好的产品不该给用户留下「同品牌却不同账号体系」的认知陷阱。

二辩 Sea @Sea_Bitcoin | XHunt全球排名：1663
核心观点：好产品应不给用户留下犯错空间，只加确认是治标不治本。用户在同一品牌下操作时，天然会默认 UID 是全局唯一的，这是合理预期。如果不同站点的 UID 数字可以重复，却仍允许直接输入 UID 转账，确认页再多一层也只是增加操作成本，无法从根本上消除误转风险。建议从底层让 UID 全局唯一，或者在输入阶段就强制识别站点并拦截不兼容转账。OKX 确认页信息也偏少，但币安作为头部平台更应该把防错做在前面。

三辩 很大很大的橙子 @0xVeryBigOrange | XHunt全球排名：1676
核心观点：同一品牌下 UID 应全局唯一，否则跨站转账不能只凭数字放行。用户看到的是「币安」，不会细究主站和泰国站是独立法人、独立账号体系。这种品牌一致性与技术隔离之间的矛盾，本应由产品设计来消化，而不是让普通用户在转账时自己去判断「这个 UID 属于哪个站点」。建议加字母前缀（如 TH-、TR-）区分站点，并在误转发生后考虑先行垫付，再与收款方协商，而不是让用户长时间等待不活跃账户的回复。

四辩 Crypto攻城狮 @gcsbtc | XHunt全球排名：3593
核心观点：主站与本地站账户不互通，用户在主站误输 UID 导致转错，这是事实。确认页信息不足，是产品可以改进的地方。何一愿意个人补贴并改进产品，这个态度值得肯定，但补贴是事后补救，不是产品设计的替代方案。建议在 UID 输入框实时校验站点归属，并在确认页明确标注「此 UID 属于主站 / 泰国站，是否支持互转」，把歧义消灭在交易前，而不是依赖用户自己去记住复杂的站点规则。

五辩 $trong @StrongHedge | XHunt全球排名：15819
核心观点：平台面对产品失误时推责用户，这不只是一次误转，也是信任问题。二次确认点了还是转错，说明确认流程本身信息不足（没有明确展示「目标站点」或「是否支持跨站」）。当产品设计让「同品牌不同站点」的 UID 存在碰撞可能时，把全部责任推给用户「没仔细看」，会让用户觉得平台在逃避产品层面的问题。一次误转可以协商，但反复出现类似情况会侵蚀用户对平台的信任。

六辩 孙 Sun ⚡💵 @hashcoin0 | XHunt全球排名：35760
核心观点：UID 还能撞号？难怪币安能被盗 60 多亿。钱好像转到欧盟用户账号里了，币安还被欧盟清退了。八个月了愣是对用户不管不顾，眼看舆论对自己不利了才开始掏钱平事。要不是社区帮忙维权，人家这些钱就流产了。祖传的回滚绝技不能给用户服务，产品底层设计本就不该给用户留这么大的犯错空间。历史问题累积到现在，用户对「平台是否真正把用户资产安全放在第一位」已经产生怀疑，这次 UID 事件只是把这个信任缺口再次放大。

写在最后，感觉双方都有责任。
币安可以通过 UID 设计机制更好的规避这种情况（全局唯一或强制站点识别），用户二次确认应该再次核对，同时先转小额测试。产品防错和用户谨慎都不可偏废。

Taiwanese semiconductor analyst Andrew Lu’s take on the recent scandal involving Jensen Huang:

Why the US Seized on the Scandal to Draw Its Sword: Three Strategic Objectives

The purpose of this scandal is by no means to expose an affair. It is to force through three critical objectives that had made no headway in the tech war between the US and China because Jensen Huang opposed them.

The first cut: Completely destroy the legitimacy of Jensen Huang's lobbying against sanctions in Washington

Over the past two years, the loudest and most influential business leader in Silicon Valley opposing a total ban on chip exports to China has been Jensen Huang. He has told the White House the same thing all along: "Cede the Chinese market to Huawei, and the only one that ends up dead is the American tech industry."

But the moment US intelligence labels the woman named as Huang's affair partner "a spy working for China's Ministry of State Security who sought to steer the US toward easing its chip controls," every bit of lobbying he has done for looser controls takes on an entirely different political meaning. It becomes a national security matter, raising the possibility that a foreign spy used a secret relationship to exert influence.

Huang can no longer say a single word in defense of the Chinese market before Congress or the White House. If he does, he will be branded as someone who "fell for an intelligence operation and still hasn't come to his senses."

The second cut: Reverse the H200 export approvals for China and sever the link between Chinese shell companies and Southeast Asian smuggling networks

Look at the timing of the two reports.

On November 8, the very day the Jensen Huang scandal broke, The New York Times published an investigation for which its reporters went in person to dozens of Chinese companies that the US Commerce Department had approved to handle Nvidia's H200 chips. New Matrix in Beijing was one of them. According to the report, the registered addresses of companies approved to buy the chips turned out to be empty "ghost offices," and some of the companies had close ties to entities on US sanctions lists and to firms under contract with the Chinese military.

One exposé says Nvidia's CEO was having an affair with a female spy from Megaspeed, the Singapore company that handled the chip smuggling. The other says the Chinese companies Commerce approved to buy H200s are nothing but shell companies trading on behalf of the Chinese military. The aim of these two reports is clear. They are meant to pressure the Trump administration and the Commerce Department into fully revoking or freezing H200 export approvals for China and, going further, to force a sweeping overhaul of the loophole that let chips be diverted through data centers run by third parties in Singapore and elsewhere in Southeast Asia.

The third cut: Put Nvidia on a national security leash through congressional oversight and an independent investigation

As the world's largest company by market cap and the dominant force in AI, Nvidia has until now enjoyed broad autonomy in how it runs its business. But in the wake of this incident, the three congressional committees responsible for China, foreign affairs, and intelligence have begun examining Nvidia's internal security measures directly. They have even pressured Nvidia's board into forming an independent investigation committee to look into the company's own founder and CEO.

In effect, Washington's national security establishment has planted a watchdog right inside Nvidia's board. From now on, the goal is to make sure that everything, down to where each and every one of Nvidia's high performance chips ends up, conforms strictly to US national security strategy. It also means there is no more room for skirting the edge of the rules or releasing chips with specs specially tailored to regulatory thresholds.

Conclusion

"The scandal was a detonator set off right on cue. The real goal was to plug the holes chips were leaking through."

Jensen Huang made the fatal mistake of letting his guard down in his private life and personal relationships. In the end, he fell into a honey trap, the textbook tactic of intelligence warfare, and was compromised. America's national security and intelligence agencies ruthlessly exploited the weakness his private life had exposed. As a result, they solved three thorny problems in a single stroke: Nvidia's lobbying at the White House to ease restrictions on China, the flow of H200 chips into Chinese shell companies, and smuggling routed through Singapore.

The closed congressional hearing set for November 18 will be the decisive turning point at which the US moves in earnest to tighten its sanctions on China's AI compute even further.

author: gmgnjordan
quoted_text:
Several hundred orders. That's the total count of AI-agent orders DoorDash has processed since the feature launched, not per quarter, the entire run, according to Tony Xu on the Oct 29 earnings call. DoorDash did 993 million orders last quarter alone.

Uber's number is smaller. Balaji Krishnamurthy told analysts on Nov 4 that during a week with roughly 320 million total trips and Eats orders combined, agents booked four rides and about 500 Eats orders. His words: "very, very early and very limited traction."

Amazon won't even give a count. Andy Jassy said outside agents aren't meaningfully showing up in the numbers yet. The one agent doing real volume is Amazon's own, Alexa for Shopping: 400 million customers in the last year, interactions up 570%. The traction is happening inside the walled garden, not through ChatGPT or Claude placing orders on someone else's app.

Eric Seufert called the whole category a collective hallucination this week, and the earnings calls back him up more than the demo videos do. Every one of these companies has shipped agent-facing infrastructure in 2026. None of them are seeing agent-driven revenue that clears a rounding error.

Four rides out of 320 million trips is the real adoption number right now, whatever the keynote slides claim. I'd bet that gap closes slowly, in paid pilots and negotiated integrations, not in a single quarter where agents suddenly show up in the P&L.

适合挂机，假如你想买机票，交代一句，盯着这个机票，降到 X 就通知我，它就把监控挂在 Box 上跑，手机等消息就行，电脑和手机都不用醒着。

最重要，如果人在外面只有手机，突然要处理个文件只有电脑能开， 手机浏览器打开它，就是一台现成的电脑。

至于配置方面，
Ubuntu 系统，2 核 CPU、约 4G 内存、20G 硬盘。没有显卡，配置也不大，把它给 Muse 当备用机用用也不错。

text:
One night in June of 2024, in a Taipei bar, a Chinese businesswoman named Alice Huang made a bet with some technology executives that she could get Jensen Huang, the C.E.O. of Nvidia, to come meet them. After midnight, he showed up, wearing his black leather jacket, and joined the group for some whiskey drinks. (One of the executives who was there told the story to The New York Times.)

Alice Huang, who is not related to the Nvidia C.E.O., was a top executive at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed. In the three months after the meeting Megaspeed bought a billion dollars' worth of Nvidia technology. In the next nine months, it bought another billion dollars' worth.

On paper, this was all legal. Megaspeed built data centers in Malaysia and then rented the computing power to Chinese companies, mostly Alibaba. The U.S. bans selling its most advanced A.I. chips to China, but it's O.K. to rent the computing power to Chinese companies in a neighboring country.

But in late 2024, a U.S. Commerce Department official visited Megaspeed's Malaysian data center and found Nvidia chips still in their boxes. Investigators began to suspect that some of the chips were being moved on into China.

And then, as the Times revealed this past October, things got worse. US intelligence had concluded that Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset, reporting to China, and that she developed a close personal relationship with Jensen Huang.

President Trump was briefed about a year ago and decided not to do anything. The Times reported that he didn't want to risk Nvidia chip sales, which are helping drive the stock market. Jensen Huang was never told about the intelligence finding.

Nvidia says that it's the C.E.O.'s job to meet with customers, that Megaspeed got no secrets, and that the company found nothing wrong in its investigation into the smuggling allegations. Jensen Huang has said that Nvidia can account for all of Megaspeed's chips.

Ultimately, stopping the chips from going to China came down to two judgments. One was Nvidia's word about its customer. The other was a president weighing an intelligence finding against trade with China and an economy that Nvidia sales are helping boost. In a case like this, American export controls are only as good as those two decisions.

text:
6月初就知道黄仁勋和Alice Huang的瓜了，这在算力圈也不是啥大的秘密。

整个故事挺唏嘘，不过可以明确的一点是，老黄是个好人，保全了女方，至少她现在在很安全的地方，自己承担了责任。

Alice Huang的老公是其前合伙人。

Alice Huang之前所在的 Megaspeed  算是中国算力圈的黄埔军校，里面的人后来分散到了各个地方。

Megaspeed前身是游戏公司第七大道，背后股东主要是各大游戏公司，包括《传奇》的运营方世纪华通。

Megaspeed的操作路径，是比较常见的手法，把东南亚当跳板。

以新加坡主体，向英伟达合规下单，拿到配额，Megaspeed对于自己和英伟达的良好合作关系也从来不藏着掖着，直接在官网挂上了英伟达支持。

设备运到马来西亚、印尼自建数据中心落地，对外宣称算力本地自用、对外出租。

这些芯片运送到Megaspeed于2024年初在马来西亚设立的子公司Speedmatrix。

后来，美方核查时发现一个巨大疑点，马来西亚机房内大量服务器原封不动、未拆箱，没有上电部署痕迹。

Speedmatrix注册地址在吉隆坡郊外，但是现场却无人办公。

Megaspeed以后，美国也开始封堵“用大客户身份+东南亚数据中心外壳”模型，以及传统的NCP身份不再是100%阿暖。

所以，我看着B300现货从半年前还是几百万一路跳涨到现在2000万，一切都是连锁反应。

但无论如何，中国的算力还是会继续发展。

多年后回看，说不定这就是改变中国乃至全球AI算力发展的历史性事件。

有幸吃瓜。

text:
gonna take a shot in the dark here (barely woke up) and say that maybe assets become SoV/money not when they have certain fixed properties, but when they become the best version of themselves

Think portfolio optimisation. You want to hold a basket of assets so risk isn’t concentrated (very simplified). Given an existing basket, if I’m a contender as an asset, should I aim to look more like every other asset in the basket? I would argue no, and I would argue I should also aim to be the best in my category. The more novel the category, the better, because my risk vector points away from those already in the basket.

So what does it mean for ETH? Well it’s the native asset of a network that has PoS and is fully programmable. These are sensible choices for a network whose aim is to offer maximum security and maximum utility! And it’s possible that we’re simply cursed to deliver the best settlement layer the world has ever had, and that even if we do succeed, it’s still only a necessary condition for ETH to succeed.

text:
币安最近真的有点水逆啊

前脚刚经历重大安全事件，后脚又来了个「UID撞号」风波。宇宙所最近也是接连被考验。

因为我自己之前也在交易所工作过，所以看待这类事件的角度可能会有些不同。

我更关注的是，当危机发生时，一家交易所的「响应速度」「解决问题的能力」，以及CEO和发言人有没有「责任心和担当」。

毕竟在Crypto这个行业，「信任是最昂贵、也是最脆弱的资产」。

尤其是涉及用户资金安全的问题，一旦信任出现裂痕，想要重新建立，可比解决一次技术故障难得多。

而这几次事件中，一姐和币安团队的处理方式，确实有不少值得我学习的地方。

先说这次UID事件。

简单来说，一位用户想把币安Global的资产转到自己的币安泰国账户，却误用了泰国站的UID进行主站站内转账。由于两个平台的账号系统独立，这个数字恰好对应主站另一位用户，导致资金误转。

从一姐的回应来看，她本人和4位员工一直在跟进，第一时间协助冻结资金，并持续联系收款方协商。

更让我佩服的是，虽然事件尚未完全解决，一姐就已经主动表示「愿意自掏腰包补贴用户的损失」。

其实这件事确实存在用户自身的操作失误，但她并没有简单地把责任推回给用户，而是一边厘清问题，一边尽力提供解决方案。

这种「既讲原则、又愿意主动承担」的危机处理方式，确实很值得学习。

当然，站在交易所产品运营的角度，我觉得这次事件也有值得优化的地方。

看到不少人建议，给不同地区币安的UID统一增加国家前缀，以避免重复。

但我个人觉得，这个方案未必那么容易落地。

毕竟Binance Global与各地本地平台独立运营，涉及不同的主体、技术架构和合规要求。想统一修改UID体系，可能需要多方协调，并不是简单增加两个字母就能解决。

相比之下，我更倾向于「加强用户教育，以及在转账过程中设置更加醒目的风险提醒」。

比如用户输入UID时，明确弹出：

⚠️「当前UID转账仅适用于Binance Global站内账户。币安泰国、美国、土耳其等本地平台均使用独立账号系统，UID并不互通。如需跨平台转账，请使用对应平台的充值地址或二维码。」

最好让用户主动勾选确认，而不是把提醒藏在一行不起眼的小字里。

毕竟多一个清楚的提示，就可能帮助用户避免一次不必要的资金损失。

值得肯定的是，一姐也在积极收集用户反馈，探讨如何优化产品机制。

再回到币安最近遇到的几次风波。

上次安全事件，币安迅速公开回应，承诺承担相关用户损失，并协调各方资源追踪和冻结资产。

这次UID事件，一姐亲自参与跟进，积极协调，甚至愿意个人出资为用户提供保障。

虽然两次事件性质不同，但其中体现出来的「危机响应能力、责任意识以及沟通方式」，都很值得行业从业者借鉴。

「好的危机公关，从来不是把问题解释得多漂亮，而是真正让用户看到：有人在负责，有人在解决，问题也在推动改变。」

当然，最终资金能否追回、产品优化能否落地，还是要看后续结果。

但经历过这么多市场周期，CZ和一姐在应对危机上的经验与执行力，确实让我理解为什么币安能够长期保持行业头部地位。

「真正的宇宙所，不是永远不出问题，而是遇到问题时，有能力解决，有担当承担，也有胸襟不断改进。」

希望币安继续完善产品、安全与风控体系，也相信整个Crypto行业会在不断修正和迭代中走得更远。💛
author: ppisabeauty
quoted_text:
每个人在币安都只会有一个UID，且是独立的，并不存在撞号。我理解你的感受，从联系我开始到现在，全程我和4个员工跟踪了前因后果。
我简单描述一下背景：您把币安的钱转到币安（泰国），正常这属于跨站转账，需要用地址或者二维码，但你在转账过程中在币安直接输入UID转账，虽然我们有二次确认环节，但你没有仔细看。你发现转错后，直接找了我。我本人和4个人的团队一直在协助，第一时间帮忙冻结了这笔钱，但因为这个收到钱的持仓用户并不活跃，我们也在反复联系对方，但对方没有响应。我们做了应该做的，甚至设身处地考虑你打错了钱会着急，所以尽可能帮忙。
对方并不是犯罪，是您打错币，如果对方坚持不退只能我们客服介入谈判。你着急，我们建议让你通过报警执法介入，我们再协助沟通。但你在泰国报警，您在您希望收款的泰国报警要求币安主站把另外一个国家的币安用户的资产直接划拨给你，这不符合执法流程，报警应该在你希望找的用户国家所在地而不是泰国。
之前处理过很多打错币的情况，大额打错几千万美金，也是我们及时拦住帮忙追的，而且当时用户坚持不退，也是我们协助谈判，最后到双方能接受的范围和解。
我理解你的难处，团队也一直在跟踪进展，得到的就是这篇长文，我们会继续联系另外一个用户协商，但你打错币这事儿，在泰国报警确实帮不上忙，那是你的钱想去没去成的目的地。
最后提醒大家，币安土耳其，币安泰国，币安美国等本地法币交易平台是独立平台，并不共享账号系统，日常转账提币时请仔细检查地址和UID。

Taiwanese semiconductor analyst Andrew Lu’s take on the recent scandal involving Jensen Huang:

Why the US Seized on the Scandal to Draw Its Sword: Three Strategic Objectives

The purpose of this scandal is by no means to expose an affair. It is to force through three critical objectives that had made no headway in the tech war between the US and China because Jensen Huang opposed them.

The first cut: Completely destroy the legitimacy of Jensen Huang's lobbying against sanctions in Washington

Over the past two years, the loudest and most influential business leader in Silicon Valley opposing a total ban on chip exports to China has been Jensen Huang. He has told the White House the same thing all along: "Cede the Chinese market to Huawei, and the only one that ends up dead is the American tech industry."

But the moment US intelligence labels the woman named as Huang's affair partner "a spy working for China's Ministry of State Security who sought to steer the US toward easing its chip controls," every bit of lobbying he has done for looser controls takes on an entirely different political meaning. It becomes a national security matter, raising the possibility that a foreign spy used a secret relationship to exert influence.

Huang can no longer say a single word in defense of the Chinese market before Congress or the White House. If he does, he will be branded as someone who "fell for an intelligence operation and still hasn't come to his senses."

The second cut: Reverse the H200 export approvals for China and sever the link between Chinese shell companies and Southeast Asian smuggling networks

Look at the timing of the two reports.

On November 8, the very day the Jensen Huang scandal broke, The New York Times published an investigation for which its reporters went in person to dozens of Chinese companies that the US Commerce Department had approved to handle Nvidia's H200 chips. New Matrix in Beijing was one of them. According to the report, the registered addresses of companies approved to buy the chips turned out to be empty "ghost offices," and some of the companies had close ties to entities on US sanctions lists and to firms under contract with the Chinese military.

One exposé says Nvidia's CEO was having an affair with a female spy from Megaspeed, the Singapore company that handled the chip smuggling. The other says the Chinese companies Commerce approved to buy H200s are nothing but shell companies trading on behalf of the Chinese military. The aim of these two reports is clear. They are meant to pressure the Trump administration and the Commerce Department into fully revoking or freezing H200 export approvals for China and, going further, to force a sweeping overhaul of the loophole that let chips be diverted through data centers run by third parties in Singapore and elsewhere in Southeast Asia.

The third cut: Put Nvidia on a national security leash through congressional oversight and an independent investigation

As the world's largest company by market cap and the dominant force in AI, Nvidia has until now enjoyed broad autonomy in how it runs its business. But in the wake of this incident, the three congressional committees responsible for China, foreign affairs, and intelligence have begun examining Nvidia's internal security measures directly. They have even pressured Nvidia's board into forming an independent investigation committee to look into the company's own founder and CEO.

In effect, Washington's national security establishment has planted a watchdog right inside Nvidia's board. From now on, the goal is to make sure that everything, down to where each and every one of Nvidia's high performance chips ends up, conforms strictly to US national security strategy. It also means there is no more room for skirting the edge of the rules or releasing chips with specs specially tailored to regulatory thresholds.

Conclusion

"The scandal was a detonator set off right on cue. The real goal was to plug the holes chips were leaking through."

Jensen Huang made the fatal mistake of letting his guard down in his private life and personal relationships. In the end, he fell into a honey trap, the textbook tactic of intelligence warfare, and was compromised. America's national security and intelligence agencies ruthlessly exploited the weakness his private life had exposed. As a result, they solved three thorny problems in a single stroke: Nvidia's lobbying at the White House to ease restrictions on China, the flow of H200 chips into Chinese shell companies, and smuggling routed through Singapore.

The closed congressional hearing set for November 18 will be the decisive turning point at which the US moves in earnest to tighten its sanctions on China's AI compute even further.

币圈吹了整整三年的“消灭助记词神话”，在今天彻底沦为了一场血腥的笑话。

几个小时前，链上安全圈拉响了最高级别的红色警报：
为海量 Web3 钱包提供“谷歌/苹果一键登录”的底层基础设施 Web3Auth，突发私钥泄露级严重事故。

首当其冲被穿透的，是 Cosmos 生态龙头钱包 Keplr。

黑客已经开始在受影响的地址上发起疯狂盗币。
Keplr 官方紧急切断所有社交登录入口，全网各大链上验证节点和项目方一片大乱。

极度荒诞的一幕在链上赤裸裸地上演：

那些自以为走在时代前沿、贪图省事用 Google 和 Apple 账号一键建钱包的散户，账户私钥被扒得一干二净，沦为案板上的鱼肉；
反而是那些被嘲笑“操作落后、冥顽不灵”、坚持拿纸笔手抄 12 个助记词、死守冷钱包的老韭菜，在这场灾难里毫发未伤。

为了省下抄写助记词的 30 秒，代价是把自己的全部身家，双手奉送给第三方中心化数据库。

现在的链上战场已经变成了一场生死竞速。
Web3Auth 联合 Keplr 正连夜在 Celestia、Injective、dYdX、Osmosis、Akash 等 10 条公链以及 8 条 EVM 链上，疯狂用白帽程序把被盗边缘的资产转移到紧急恢复钱包，硬生生跟黑客抢跑。

Polygon 首席安全官 Mudit Gupta 更是公开发出最冰冷的警告：
“只要你用社交账号登过 Keplr，现在立刻马上把钱转走！更可怕的是，天知道全网还有多少钱包和 dApp，也在背后接了这家服务商。”

Not Your Keys, Not Your Coins。
你以为一键登录是去中心化的技术进步，其实你只是自作聪明地，把钱存进了一家没有任何安保的地下钱庄。
