Frontier performance at a fraction of the compute.

Today at @i14labs we’re launching Sugar Glider, our new family of LLM architectures!

Join the waitlist for early access: https://t.co/IT5IReDmvT

Sugar Glider delivers a new Pareto frontier: extreme memory and compute efficiency whilst maintaining frontier performance, even for large models (tested up to ~1T params).

O(1) per token inference → ✅

Fixed size KV cache → ✅

Frontier long-context retrieval quality → ✅

1 billion token long context retrieval → ☑️**
(**100% -> single needle @ 1B-token context, 90.5% multikey 1 @ 1B-token context.)

How did we do it? Turns out a few decades in the trenches of human memory and language model research is a pretty handy starting point to solve the “intelligence vs efficiency vs memory” conundrum.

... and just for something extra, we’ve been converting some of the most powerful and popular open-weight models to O(1) inference and fixed memory, with each conversion taking just hours :)

quoted_text:
随着一连串事件的发生，我不禁思考起来

作为圈内体量最大且影响力最高的交易所 
每次出现问题为什么总是围绕着外部原因展开？

回看历史：

2018 两次被拉盘，2019 被盗 7000 BTC，都是用户被钓鱼的问题

同年 KYC 照片流出是 FUD，真有也是第三方供应商的问题

2021 狗狗币提现停 17 天虽然只有币安一家中招，但这是狗狗币钱包的问题

2023 BUSD 被叫停，虽然名字叫 Binance USD，但这是 Paxos 的问题

1011 是做市商的问题，不是自己模式设计有问题 
赔钱是自愿的，不是义务 

1030 是黑客的问题，又或者是AI发展太快，反正不是自己的问题 

这次 UID 转错是用户没仔细核对的问题，不是主站和泰国站 UID 重号的问题

我当然理解，交易所不可能完全避免事故，也不认为所有问题都应该由币安独自承担

但我始终觉得，解释事故发生的原因，与承担平台应有的责任，是两件可以同时成立的事情

黑客可以是直接攻击者，第三方可以存在技术问题，用户也可能操作失误

可这些解释并不能自动回答另一个问题：

平台的安全机制、产品设计和风险控制，是否还有本可以做得更好的地方？

或许有些问题放在其他交易所身上根本算不上什么大问题
但因为你是币安，这些问题才会被无限放大

作为加密行业最具影响力的交易所之一
币安享受着行业头部地位带来的流量、资源与话语权

自然也需要承担与之相匹配的责任，接受更高标准的审视
外界对币安的要求更苛刻，并不一定是刻意针对
而是大家对行业头部平台本身就有着更高的期待

当一家交易所已经站在行业金字塔的顶端，衡量它的标准就不应该仅仅是有没有犯错，还应该包括它有没有能力把每一个细节做到更好

行业地位决定了你的影响力，也决定了你应该承担的责任

text:
Stumbled across an incredible LA Times article from 1996 - "The Dirty Secret About the Net" 

It was written about the nascent consumer Internet, but you could replace "web" with "agents" and get a perfect mirror of the current discourse

The author's predictions (he was the paper's tech editor): 

- The time for startups had passed, and Microsoft would own the Internet market (Google was founded two years later) 
- It would take more than a decade for the Internet to become a consumer phenomenon, if it ever did (it took <5 years)
- Privacy and security concerns + complicated setup meant that the web would only appeal to high income, highly educated coastal elites
- Infrastructure was "groaning under the weight of the huge traffic increases" - this would be very slow to fix, and would significantly limit adoption
- Online shopping showed "few signs of taking off" - even if payment issues were solved, retail shopping was too entertaining for users to default to the Internet
- Making money would be near-impossible - consumers would not pay subscriptions, and the Internet's reach was not enough to generate real advertising revenue

My favorite one-liner: "Many new businesses, like the huge online bookstore Amazon, will find a niche." 

...as well as the fact that the author's prior piece was "The Fall of Apple Computer"

text:
Unfortunately, we’re winding down @veildotcash.

From today, deposits are disabled. We’ll keep the frontend and relayer running until 21 December 2026. After that, withdrawals will still be possible through the CLI.

I haven’t taken this decision lightly. After two years of building something I’m passionate about, I’ve had to accept that the version of privacy I want to build isn’t scaling.

We’ve had periods of strong usage, but it was never sustained. With Veil, privacy depends on usage. As that declines, the privacy becomes weaker. Over the last few months, the protocol hasn’t been delivering the core value I set out to provide.

Although we didn’t solve what I set out to do, I’m extremely proud I tried to tackle what is still to this day the hardest problem in crypto. Privacy.

Going from a 9–5 to being a crypto founder has been one of the most enjoyable and rewarding things I’ve ever done. I feel lucky to have had the opportunity, which makes this a difficult call to make.

I want to thank Base, the Coinbase team and everyone who held, used or supported Veil for helping me work on it for the last two years. Ultimately, I feel I’ve fallen short of what I set out to do.

The wind down also means our support for the VEIL token ends today, including staking rewards and LP incentives. Treasury tokens will be burned.

Finally, I’m not going anywhere. I’m still bullish on crypto, Ethereum and Base, but I’d be lying if I said I knew what I was building next. Veil has had my full focus until now. Whatever comes next, I want to believe in it as much as I believed in this.

text:
New security feature: Withdrawal address allowlisting

You can now lock withdrawals from your deposit wallet to addresses you’ve approved. Adding a new address requires email verification and a 48-hour time lock, and you can cancel it from the email if it wasn’t you. That means even if someone gets into your session or you sign a bad transaction, they can’t drain funds or transfer your positions to an address you don’t control. I highly recommend enabling it if you are on the latest wallet version.

Turn it on in Settings → Account. Passkey support is coming soon to strengthen security further.

For non-deposit wallet users, we are developing a migration tool to help you move everything to the new wallet type. If you don't want to wait, you can open a new account to access this feature immediately.

We are also working on adding more advanced built-in security protection, without requiring you to enable anything on your deposit wallet - will also be live soon.

quoted_text:
Hot take: it’s gonna take 10+ years for AI to diffuse through most enterprises.

Accelerationists argue “things will be different this time” and “AI will fully diffuse wayyy faster,” but the more time I spend in the guts of big companies, the more I think their view shows a fundamental misunderstanding of corporate bureaucracy and inertia.

An enterprise’s ability to metabolize raw intelligence is limited by the slowest step of what I call the Corporate SDLC. 

It goes something like this…

1. A senior sponsor (CEO, CAIO, CIO, CFO) decides it’s in their best interest to champion AI transformation. 
2. Orgwide and function-specific AI audits are done in order to map problems/opportunities to key goals.
3. AI roadmap is built based on the org readiness of initiatives uncovered during the audit. Readiness includes: ROI case, data hygiene, data access, cultural openness, define champion, process/product understanding, pilot construct & go/no go criteria, security/legal considerations.
4. Leg work (inclusive of actual work & internal politicking) done to get first initiative to pilot readiness. 
5. Build process done by internal FDEs or external partner. Includes connecting to data sources, setting up agent-based access control, doing all necessary agent infra, harness engineering, embedding business logic, setting up evals, etc. 
6. Set up pilot with proper benchmarks and change management.
7. Make scale, cut (return to step 3), or change (return to step 5) decision on pilot.
8. Complete production readiness checklist. 
9. Additional FDE & enablement work as needed. 
10. Agent deployed to production. 
11. Ongoing maintenance and progressive permissioning to the agent as it proves itself. 

If you thought optimizing & agentifying a traditional software development life cycle was cumbersome, buckle up for the enterprise version. 

There are literally thousands of ways that the corporate SDLC can be interrupted and slowed.

Stakeholder that initially agrees to initiative gets cold feet upon employee push back.
Audits with full workflow inventory and KPI base lining takes a quarter.
Data is nowhere near semantic ready for agents.
Senior sponsor finds a new job.
Access gateway doesn’t exist.

The potential friction list is endless. 

This is why the diffusion gap (distance between raw intelligence & enterprise results) is massive & only growing and why we’re in inning 1 of a decadeslong transformation arc. 

Btw, if you want help closing the diffusion gap and driving ai transformation in your company, head to tenex[.]co.

text:
The OP was deleted but I found it a really good post to share some thoughts on and discuss.

> "the happiest partners in my office are all men with stay at home wives, all the others are miserable psychos"

Hmm, from my POV this probably works well when the SAH partner is at least competent and productive enough, effective at home-making including and critically early child development(implementing our shared and agreed values and protocols as a way of life), and it works phenomenally well when she shows high competency on the socio-economic aspect: excelling at the relationships and opportunities across social groups, clubs, orgs, and committees of interest like PTA, kids’ sports and recreation, philanthropy, community development, and so on.

Like yeah, making sure the home is the best home it can be is already a big win. On top of that, extending our influence, security, and even practical reach into the society right around us makes for a bigger win which I’ll very much appreciate and work more towards enabling.

Coming back from work and finding out that my lady was the reason a cancer-research fundraiser succeeded, or that new study materials got delivered to the school, or something along those lines would be a real admirable and desirable outcome that I’d love to see more and more, especially when I can enable her to do so. To me, that’s some of what characterises a homemaker/SAH life partner.

My grandad was a businessman, and my grandmother held a lot of the family’s influence, especially in politics. So much so that she apparently became a political force of nature in her community, and I think my grandad was lucky for that.

A lot has changed since their time in terms of how society, dating, and life + family-building are done, and a lot of what the OP kinda signals at some of that, so there's definitely a much broader discussion worth having. Will probably add more thoughts on this in the comments later.

1/x

“Practical principles to counter a modern-day coup/psyop/struggle session”

1) Own what you did but fiercely resist accommodating the mob, resist owning half-truths or actions/behaviors you didn’t do.

2) The op is not about your past actions, it’s about your enemies and this event as their opportunity

3) No matter how bad it gets, nothing is as bad as it seems. 

4) Find the enemies at the very root of the op and find every creative problem-solving tool at your disposal to neutralize them.

5) People will throw their grandmother under the bus if they believe doing so will protect their reputation. They can become highly useful idiots in the op. Their power and access must be fiercely and quickly cut off.

6) Do not hesitate in cutting off anyone you suspect of disloyalty.

7) Build a team of close and loyal patriots and have one of them run a dedicated, well-resourced war room to put the rebellion to rest. 

8) Use your patriots and regular meditation to buoy your psychological resistance to the op. 

9) Your enemies aren’t as smart or hard working as you. Outsmart and outwork them as a way of life until the op is over.

10) Think about the op as if it were in the past. What are the difficult things you procrastinated on or avoided that would have stopped the op? Do them.

11) Never be ashamed of the op. Business as usual. Continue on with optimism and joy in your everyday work and its mission.

12) Download telegram and use it as your messaging application for all sensitive communications.

text:
It’s abundantly clear that the U.S. intel community not only knew about all of this for a long time but also most likely briefed Jensen and used him to gather intel on China’s efforts to evade sanctions. 

Supporting evidence for this theory is that the media has had images and videos of them together for a very long time and Trump and Marco Rubio were briefed on this a full year ago. Additionally, Trump not only met with Jensen several times after he even allowed him to travel on Air Force One to a state dinner in China. There is no shot whatsoever the secret service or the intel community would have allowed someone who was that compromised to be this close to the president even if there was the smallest chance that he could be relaying information to foreign actors. 

The most likely scenario is that Jensen was notified and briefed on the threat before and the intel community thought it was more advantageous to use the opportunity for counter espionage and potential sabotage. The U.S. has a history of doing operations like this, if you take a look at stuxnet, the virus designed to sabotage Iran’s nuclear reactors by targeting their industrial controllers, it took the Iranians over a year to figure out they were being sabotaged and that was with backing of the entire state resources and its engineering talent. 

With GPUs it’s harder to discover these bugs, in fact it could take forever to figure out. A bit flip here and there, a small math mistake here, intermittent thermal throttling, bad telemetry reports etc. you would be flying blind for a looooong time and there are even ways to build in anti reverse engineering measures if a card was pulled out on a bench to be tested. 

That being said I think the Chinese eventually got wise to this and with the change in the house and senate they thought it was the opportune time to let the cat out the bag. It’s telling that Jensen will be testifying to the house in a closed door meeting. Sadly he still needs to claim he was “cheating” to the public as admitting to working with the intelligence community to sabotage a foreign country would be 10x worse for diplomatic relations and for Nvidia. 

Even though I’m not his biggest fan, if what I think it’s true you can’t call Jensen anything other than a real American patriot. It must be very hard to sacrifice your public image and your families peace for the country.

text:
Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan on why institutions are only now coming around to $BTC

"Old fact from early days of Bitwise, we've been doing this since 2017, is that our average client allocates to us after 8 meetings."

"If you count from when the ETFs launched, which was like two and a half-ish years ago, if you did a meeting every quarter after they launched, you're just sort of now getting to the point that you're accepting of Bitcoin."

"That number of meetings is what it takes to normalize Bitcoin. There are other great firms doing it. Fidelity and BlackRock and VanEck and Franklin."

"No one just sees it for the first time and accepts it. They see it and they study it. Central banks probably do one meeting a year, but after 8 years, they're going to get there too."

"This sort of rule of eight is sort of how these institutions get onboarded into crypto. I think it's as simple as just the passage of time."

text:
Thought I’d start with what I’ve observed over the years.. For many years researchers (I was one of them) kept being told by a vocal part of the community that gas should be turned way up and to hell with small nodes. We did hear scaling demand from app devs, at least that they were considering deploying away from L1 because they did not imagine their scaling needs could be met.

It took a while (too long) to internalise that scaling was desirable, particularly given the L2-centric roadmap that considered more or less that activity should be offloaded from the L1 and towards L2s. If app devs go there, that’s a feature! Clearly this thinking has been heavily updated, more towards apps should go wherever they’d best leverage the platform they’re building on, either L1 or L2s.

Then somewhere around March 2025 we sat down more properly and I think that was the first seeds of a clearer scaling roadmap for Ethereum. L2s were in favour too, scaling was useful to them from the blob perspective, but many would also highlight a strong L1 being a better value proposition for them.

Repricings like the ones Glamsterdam intends to do were discussed iirc. They’re not a strange researchy solution in my view, when you look at how to prevent DoS attacks like Shanghai, it’s clear that getting the price right is the first step.

But here it’s more about the long-term load. I don’t think it’s right to say we’re overindexing on historical precedent, the NFT reference was perhaps a bit unhappy. afaict (chart attached below!), state creation is distributed fairly equally over time, and scales linearly with the gas used (the bigger the blocks, roughly proportionally more state).

So then there’s a couple points.

1. Yes state creation increases 5x, bytecode increases 7.65x, but gas limit increases 3.33x, meaning relatively speaking, state creation gets 50% more expensive, and bytecode 2.3x. Not trivial! But some of the state operations besides creation benefit from the block-access list feature that ships with Glamsterdam too. And then future, deeper updates like partitioned binary tree continue to push state access costs down again. Not state creation, afaik, but for bytecode, nodes already don’t keep duplicated code around so proposals like SETCODEFROM can stop charging for it.

2. Then there is the issue of contracts breaking because they have made specific assumptions about the cost of state operations. This is where the line has been that such expectations were misplaced, Ethereum had done such changes in the past etc. I agree with this, and to be clear as a supporter of quick slots, block time is another such parameter that I think we should be allowed to update. But of course it’s a bit of a rollercoaster that transactions were capped at 16.7M gas in Fusaka and now they could be consuming more gas with the reservoir, so this is a legitimate expectation that is now broken shortly after being introduced. It’s mostly a tooling impact more than a contract impact, but still.

3. And then there is the issue of contracts breaking beyond what most would consider legitimate. This was surfaced in reviews and audits, sadly it seems that it wasn’t addressed until late, with pcaversaccio shining a light on these issues that triggered the heightened attention. Most of the attention is on that now, and all known findings are expected to be published by early next week.

Any of the three above could be controversial. On net, I think
1. is neutral-ish, it simply tries to make the best of the limited resources of the network, and state is the resource that doesn’t scale as well as the others, until deeper changes like expiry (if that's ever a thing.. that also has DX implications).
2. has precedents, but it caught more people by surprise than it should have imo.
3. is an issue, and there’s possibly a judgement call to make regarding how to move forward here, I’ll not opine on it until I see more of the findings.

I don’t think this addresses the point about sentiment around the fork. I’m sad that it is this low. From my perspective everyone is clear about building better loops between core protocol and builders, even pointing at the contract size increase contained in Glamsterdam as proof we were finally listening.. but the mark was missed here and the reaction is legitimate.

I’m hopeful that this week and the next will bring a lot more clarity and structure to the discussion. We have a post coming tomorrow (Tuesday) laying out some of these steps.

Fully expect that it won’t clear up every disagreement, and it’s not about explaining away the sentiment of experienced devs either. I talked about Ross’s piece here https://t.co/aqSXdFzW7N because I found it well-balanced, and it led me to consider how the fork would be perceived if the developer outreach had been earlier and stronger. It’s possible that it wouldn’t have changed the core disagreement.

For the future, the only way I see here is to be clear about what expectations are, also something briefly discussed here https://t.co/uLlyHtoThx I’ve seen versions of this around and I expect we’d want to push something like this once the current crisis is resolved.

text:
卧槽，特朗普现在最大的软肋可能是两个华人😂😎

民主党中期选举大胜后，一场针对特朗普家族的调查风暴正在酝酿。

我看了下，民主党未来两年准备重点调查的方向，大概涉及以下8个领域：

1.特朗普家族生意：WLFI加密货币、房地产、1789 Capital投资、中东主权基金。
2.爱泼斯坦案：政府有没有故意隐瞒关键证据。
3.移民执法：ICE暴力执法、非法拘捕及资金滥用。
4.司法部：是否利用司法权力打击政治对手，以及争议性总统特赦。
5.马斯克：旗下公司与美国政府的合同及利益往来。
6.白宫工程：宴会厅私人捐款、政府工程及矿产交易。
7.国防军事：伊朗战争、军事决策和国防部履职。
8.医药保险：药厂、医疗保险及政府药价协议中的利益冲突。

民主党现在的思路很清楚，先调查，不急着弹劾。毕竟弹劾定罪需要参议院三分之二支持，难度极高，但国会调查可以持续传唤证人、索取文件、举行公开听证，这也在为2028年的总统大选作准备。

我分析来分析去，发现最容易率先找到突破口的，可能就是特朗普家族的加密货币生意。

因为其他调查很多还停留在寻找证据的阶段，而加密这边已经有人打官司、有人追资金、有人正式要求交文件了。

而帮民主党撕开这道口子的，可能就是孙哥和大表哥。

先说孙哥：

2024年11月，孙哥拿出3000万美元支持特朗普家族的WLFI项目，后来累计投资达到7500万美元，一度被奉为座上宾。

2026年3月，孙哥此前面临的SEC诉讼迎来和解，旗下公司支付1000万美元罚款，SEC撤销对孙哥个人的相关指控。

结果才过一个多月，孙哥就跟特朗普家族彻底翻脸了！

原来孙哥持有的WLFI代币早在2025年9月就遭到冻结，无法正常转让和出售。

到了今年4月，孙哥直接把WLFI告上美国法庭，要求解冻代币，恢复自己的资产处置权。

高潮发生在11月3日，也就是美国中期选举当天。

孙哥帖子链接：https://t.co/DumKywpRTG

孙哥突然向法院申请制裁WLFI及其律师，指控对方在诉讼中隐瞒阿联酋股东身份。

WLFI最初披露的公司身份只有美国佛罗里达州，后来又修改文件，承认股权链条涉及22个成员以及阿联酋，并以涉及外国股东为由挑战美国联邦法院的管辖权。

而此前曝光的另一笔交易显示，阿联酋国家安全顾问塔赫农支持的投资实体，曾以5亿美元取得WLFI约49%的股权。

这下事情就大了。

孙哥原本只想拿回自己的币，现在却把特朗普家族与中东资本的股权关系拉进了司法程序。

如果诉讼继续涉及股东身份、协议及相关资金往来，民主党调查特朗普家族海外商业利益时，就多了一条现成的取证线索。

再说大表哥：

2023年，币安因反洗钱等违规问题与美国政府达成43亿美元和解，大表哥认罪并在2024年服刑约4个月。

到了2025年，事情发生了戏剧性变化。

5月，阿联酋投资机构MGX选择使用特朗普家族WLFI发行的20亿美元USD1稳定币，完成对币安的投资。

这笔交易的商业价值非常直接：USD1的发行方可以通过稳定币储备资产获得利息收入。20亿美元的资金规模，对刚起步的USD1来说是极其重要的业务。

同年10月23日，特朗普正式特赦大表哥。

一边是中东资本通过USD1投资币安，一边是特朗普家族的稳定币业务受益，随后大表哥获得总统特赦。

几件事本身都有公开记录，民主党自然会追问其中有没有不当利益交换。

麻烦还没结束。

2026年2月，美国民主党参议员Blumenthal针对币安启动调查，质疑该平台涉及约17亿美元与伊朗关联实体及俄罗斯影子船队有关的可疑资金流转。

币安明确否认有关违规指控，但民主党已经把这个问题与大表哥的特赦、特朗普家族的加密业务联系起来审查。

现在最有意思的事情发生了。

11月5日，Blumenthal正式向WLFI、币安等机构发出通知，要求最迟在2027年1月4日前提交相关资料，否则考虑采取进一步措施。

这就形成了两条线：

孙哥在法庭上追查WLFI股权与阿联酋资本。

民主党在国会追查USD1资金流、币安合规以及大表哥的特赦。

两条线最后都指向同一个问题：

特朗普家族到底从这些交易中获得了多少商业利益，这些利益与美国政府的决策之间有没有不当关联？

PS：写到最后不得不服孙哥的政治敏感性有多强，孙哥只花了1000万美金搞定了美国，而大表哥花了40多亿美金搞定了美国。
author: oragnes
quoted_text:
昨晚，我的律师向法院提出动议，请求制裁世界自由金融(World Liberty Financial) @worldlibertyfi。理由是：它在我起诉它好几个月之后，才披露自己是阿联酋 🇦🇪 公民。

先给刚关注这场纠纷的朋友介绍一下：我是 World Liberty 最早、也是最大的投资人之一。2024 年 11 月，我和 World Liberty 签了代币购买协议，同意购买 3,000 万美元的WLFI代币，后来又把总投资增加到 4,500 万美元。

今年 4 月，我起诉了 World Liberty，指控这家公司用欺诈手段诱使我投资，之后又非法冻结了我的代币。

根据我的代币购买协议，我有权选择在加州的联邦法院或州法院提起诉讼。

我选了联邦法院。

像我这样的案子，只有在双方来自不同地方时，联邦法院才能审理。像我这样的外国原告，可以在联邦法院起诉美国被告，但一般不能在那里起诉外国被告。在这个问题上，像 World Liberty 这样的公司，会被视为拥有它每一个所有者的公民身份。所以只要有一个所有者是外国人，这家公司就算外国公司。

换句话说，只要 World Liberty 和它的所有者全都是美国人，我的案子就可以由联邦法院审理。

按照联邦法院的规则，World Liberty 必须在案件一开始就提交一份披露声明，列明它的每一个所有者，以及他们各自是哪里的公民。World Liberty 的披露声明只列了一个实体，就是 World Liberty 自己，公民身份只写了佛罗里达州。它的律师还签字证明，不知道还有其他需要披露的人。

随后，World Liberty 申请强制仲裁，想把我的案子从公开法庭转到秘密的仲裁程序中。

我反对这项申请。我的律师为此花了好几个月、几十万美元。在 8 月的一次听证会上，法院表示，它并不认为我的诉求都应该交付仲裁。法院裁定，我的部分诉求留在公开法庭审理，部分交付仲裁，并命令双方协商，拟定一份协议，划分哪些诉求留在法庭、哪些交付仲裁。

不到一周，World Liberty 突然"更正"了它的披露声明。之前它的所有权链条上只列了一个成员，现在列了 22 个，公民身份也变成了佛罗里达州、特拉华州、波多黎各和阿联酋。

World Liberty 现在说，联邦法院对我的案子没有管辖权，因为它有阿联酋公民身份，这样原告和被告双方就都有外国当事人。

这其中的讽刺显而易见。World Liberty 的"金皮书"宣称："World Liberty Financial 在设计上就不是在离岸注册的"，是"一家美国的、纳税的公司，致力于把 DeFi 带回它真正的家：美国"。它承诺打造一个"总部在美国的去中心化平台"，建立在"自由、隐私和交易自由的美国理念"之上，把不经中介的私人交易称为"美国的核心价值"，还夸口说："World Liberty Financial 不回避美国，而是拥抱美国，让它成为未来的全球加密之都。"

卖代币的时候，World Liberty 是骄傲的美国公司 🇺🇸。直到它需要想办法逃离美国联邦法庭的时候，才"发现"了自己的阿联酋 🇦🇪 血统。

World Liberty 想必一直都知道自己的所有者是谁。它的律师却声称，他们是在提交最初的披露声明之后，才得知公司有阿联酋公民身份。

正如我的动议所说，如果这是真的，那么要么是 World Liberty 的律师没有尽到应有的核查义务，要么是 World Liberty 没有对自己的律师说实话。我们问他们这是怎么回事，World Liberty 拒绝回答。

代币持有人有权知道，他们投资的项目对公众、对法院说的是不是真话。我提出这项动议，是要追究 World Liberty 及其律师的责任，因为我认为他们向法院提交了误导性的披露声明。我也要确保 World Liberty 耍手段的代价由他们自己承担，而不是由我承担。

联邦法院对这项制裁动议作出裁决后，我会在加州州法院重新起诉 World Liberty。

我会继续为这个社区应得的透明度而战。

text:
Thought I’d start with what I’ve observed over the years.. For many years researchers (I was one of them) kept being told by a vocal part of the community that gas should be turned way up and to hell with small nodes. We did hear scaling demand from app devs, at least that they were considering deploying away from L1 because they did not imagine their scaling needs could be met.

It took a while (too long) to internalise that scaling was desirable, particularly given the L2-centric roadmap that considered more or less that activity should be offloaded from the L1 and towards L2s. If app devs go there, that’s a feature! Clearly this thinking has been heavily updated, more towards apps should go wherever they’d best leverage the platform they’re building on, either L1 or L2s.

Then somewhere around March 2025 we sat down more properly and I think that was the first seeds of a clearer scaling roadmap for Ethereum. L2s were in favour too, scaling was useful to them from the blob perspective, but many would also highlight a strong L1 being a better value proposition for them.

Repricings like the ones Glamsterdam intends to do were discussed iirc. They’re not a strange researchy solution in my view, when you look at how to prevent DoS attacks like Shanghai, it’s clear that getting the price right is the first step.

But here it’s more about the long-term load. I don’t think it’s right to say we’re overindexing on historical precedent, the NFT reference was perhaps a bit unhappy. afaict (chart attached below!), state creation is distributed fairly equally over time, and scales linearly with the gas used (the bigger the blocks, roughly proportionally more state).

So then there’s a couple points.

1. Yes state creation increases 5x, bytecode increases 7.65x, but gas limit increases 3.33x, meaning relatively speaking, state creation gets 50% more expensive, and bytecode 2.3x. Not trivial! But some of the state operations besides creation benefit from the block-access list feature that ships with Glamsterdam too. And then future, deeper updates like partitioned binary tree continue to push state access costs down again. Not state creation, afaik, but for bytecode, nodes already don’t keep duplicated code around so proposals like SETCODEFROM can stop charging for it.

2. Then there is the issue of contracts breaking because they have made specific assumptions about the cost of state operations. This is where the line has been that such expectations were misplaced, Ethereum had done such changes in the past etc. I agree with this, and to be clear as a supporter of quick slots, block time is another such parameter that I think we should be allowed to update. But of course it’s a bit of a rollercoaster that transactions were capped at 16.7M gas in Fusaka and now they could be consuming more gas with the reservoir, so this is a legitimate expectation that is now broken shortly after being introduced. It’s mostly a tooling impact more than a contract impact, but still.

3. And then there is the issue of contracts breaking beyond what most would consider legitimate. This was surfaced in reviews and audits, sadly it seems that it wasn’t addressed until late, with pcaversaccio shining a light on these issues that triggered the heightened attention. Most of the attention is on that now, and all known findings are expected to be published by early next week.

Any of the three above could be controversial. On net, I think
1. is neutral-ish, it simply tries to make the best of the limited resources of the network, and state is the resource that doesn’t scale as well as the others, until deeper changes like expiry (if that's ever a thing.. that also has DX implications).
2. has precedents, but it caught more people by surprise than it should have imo.
3. is an issue, and there’s possibly a judgement call to make regarding how to move forward here, I’ll not opine on it until I see more of the findings.

I don’t think this addresses the point about sentiment around the fork. I’m sad that it is this low. From my perspective everyone is clear about building better loops between core protocol and builders, even pointing at the contract size increase contained in Glamsterdam as proof we were finally listening.. but the mark was missed here and the reaction is legitimate.

I’m hopeful that this week and the next will bring a lot more clarity and structure to the discussion. We have a post coming tomorrow (Tuesday) laying out some of these steps.

Fully expect that it won’t clear up every disagreement, and it’s not about explaining away the sentiment of experienced devs either. I talked about Ross’s piece here https://t.co/aqSXdFzW7N because I found it well-balanced, and it led me to consider how the fork would be perceived if the developer outreach had been earlier and stronger. It’s possible that it wouldn’t have changed the core disagreement.

For the future, the only way I see here is to be clear about what expectations are, also something briefly discussed here https://t.co/uLlyHtoThx I’ve seen versions of this around and I expect we’d want to push something like this once the current crisis is resolved.

以太坊基金会前员工Nixo把以太坊基金会和Vitalik告了。

原因竟然是：

基金会今年发了个内部《Mandate》（使命文件），

里面有一段搞怪的“Source Seppuku License”（源码切腹许可证），

写着如果没守住承诺，就要“用剑自杀”。

还配了动漫风插图（winking 二次元女孩 + 黄猫）。 

员工被要求表态支持这个文件，不支持就等于自己辞职。

很多人觉得这个“切腹”说法很离谱、不合适，Nixo 组织了联署反对，

同时她刚跟公司说自己得了癌症，没多久就被开了。 

律师 Gabriel Shapiro的看法是：

•  这个 Mandate 其实是以太坊挺重要的一个文化节点，要求员工对齐使命本身没问题。

•  “切腹”那句明显是艺术/夸张表达，不是真让人自杀，正常人不会字面理解。

有些人故意抠字眼，可能从一开始就想留证据打官司。

•  起诉书里还提到她私自录音 Vitalik（没经同意）再公开，这事本身就很脏。

•  公司给了她一整年约 19.5 万美元的遣散费，已经很厚道了。

•  这种案子因为有“切腹”“二次元/Milady 风格”这些猎奇元素，

陪审团容易被表面故事带节奏，结果不好说。

text:
OpenAI 给 dot 加了个功能：同一个 dot 可以连上你的好几台电脑，每个任务由你指定用哪一台。

dot 是 OpenAI 9 月底在 DevDay 上发布的常驻 AI 助理，住在云端，有自己的云电脑和浏览器。你关了电脑它照样干活，在 ChatGPT、Slack、Teams 里都能给它发消息。

之前连上一台自己的电脑，dot 就能用这台电脑上的文件、代码和软件。现在能连多台，就可以把活派到一台专门的机器上，不占你手上这台。

【能干什么】

OpenAI 开发者账号举了三个例子：

• 做 iOS App：让 dot 在第二台 Mac 的 Xcode 里测一处改动，把效果截图发给你。

• 复现 Bug：让 dot 在你的笔记本和一台装着旧版 SDK 的机器上跑同一个测试，对比两边结果，你日常用的环境不用动。

• 测界面：让 dot 在第二台电脑上把一套操作流程点一遍，记下哪一步出错。你的屏幕和鼠标照常归你，可以同时修 Bug。

在连上的电脑上，dot 会新建 Codex 或 ChatGPT Work 的本地任务，也能接着做那台电脑上已有的 Codex 任务。任务在云端统一管，用的是那台电脑上的文件和工具。

每个线程一次只用一台电脑。想让几台电脑各干各的，就让 dot 每台开一个线程。已经开始的任务，不会因为你换了选中的电脑跟着搬过去。

【谁能用、怎么连】

dot 正逐步向 ChatGPT Pro 各档和 Business Premium 用户开放。Pro 用户要年满 18 岁，欧洲经济区、英国、瑞士暂时用不了。Enterprise、Edu、Healthcare 目前要管理员开通，11 月 18 日起默认打开，除非企业选择关闭。

跟 dot 聊天不占 ChatGPT 的用量额度，它派给 Codex、Work 的任务照常算这两个产品的额度。

连电脑的步骤：在要连的那台电脑上打开 ChatGPT 应用，进入 dot 的资料页，在“Computers”下找到这台电脑，点“Allow”，再点“Allow access”确认。连第二台，就到第二台电脑上再做一遍。

连上后一直有效，但 dot 用它的时候，那台电脑得联网、ChatGPT 应用得开着。显示“Offline”只是暂时用不了，要彻底断开得点“Revoke access”。这个授权和把电脑连到 Codex、开启 Work Sync 是分开的，光开那两个，dot 碰不到你的电脑。

【跟 Claude Duet、Grok Bot 比】

Anthropic 对标 dot 的产品是 Claude Duet，10 月 21 日发布，研究预览版，美国 Pro、Max、Ultra 用户排队试用。Duet 也有自己的云端虚拟机和浏览器，你的笔记本和手机关着它也能干活，靠的是 6000 多个连接器和插件。

Duet 的官方介绍里没提连接你自己的电脑，dot 之前就能连一台，这次变成多台。官方还说 Duet 暂时没法让你看它的浏览器；dot 可以打开它的云电脑看，点“Take over”自己接手。

想让 Claude 用你电脑上的东西，目前得走 Claude Code：它的项目功能（Projects，公测，面向 Pro、Max、Ultra）可以让某个任务通过远程控制（Remote Control）跑在你电脑的文件夹里，不过围绕的是代码仓库。

xAI 的 Grok Bot 在连本地电脑这件事上跟 dot 最像：所有 Bot 共用一台云电脑，你允许后也能在你的电脑上执行命令，每台连上的电脑单独设置，默认每条命令都要你批准。它还能让云电脑的网络流量从你的电脑走，网站看到的是你电脑的 IP，遇到屏蔽云服务器的网站更好办。dot 遇到这种网站，办法是到你连上的电脑上另开一个本地任务，云浏览器里的登录状态不会带过去。

原推文：https://t.co/Dj62PyW64N

text:
Brazil exposed the question every front-running F1 team must answer: how much of your pace survives when the conditions change?

Paddock Signal analysis 🇧🇷

Norris won, Mercedes secured the constructors’ title, Red Bull put both cars on the podium and Ferrari left with six points. The most revealing part was how differently their races developed through the wet, dry and wet-again phases.

McLaren: a win built across the transitions

Norris lost ground at the start, then recovered to win by 14.602 seconds. Antonelli’s spin handed him the lead, but protecting that advantage through further tyre changes and returning rain still required execution.

McLaren’s own report identifies a useful detail: Norris had enough margin to monitor Verstappen’s pace on fresh softs before choosing his second stop. That gave the pit wall information as well as breathing room.

Our reading: the value of building a lead in changeable weather extends beyond the stopwatch. It can give a team more freedom to react to evidence rather than commit under pressure.

There is a limit to the conclusion. McLaren says its upgrades helped and the low temperatures suited the car. One excellent Sunday does not establish that it now has the fastest package everywhere.

Mercedes: champions with an unresolved problem

P4 and P5 secured the title, but both drivers reported balance concerns during the race. Andrew Shovlin said the team needed to understand the unusual behaviour. Russell also acknowledged his pit-exit mistake.

Those details matter. It would be premature to diagnose a specific mechanical failure or attribute every lost position to the same cause. Driver errors and an unsettled car can both contribute, and the available statements do not quantify their separate costs.

Wolff was already asking why Mercedes underperformed and what to improve for Las Vegas and 2027. That is the right engineering question to carry away from a championship celebration: which weaknesses remained even in a title-winning season?

Red Bull: recovery pace needs context

Verstappen’s P21-to-P2 drive was exceptional. He said the opening intermediate stint was particularly strong, but that the balance changed afterwards and he could not close on Norris once he reached second.

Hadjar’s podium added another important result. Still, the evidence supports a powerful recovery, not a claim that Verstappen would certainly have won from a better grid position. Starting further forward would have changed traffic, strategy and the race itself.

Ferrari: investigate the whole stint

Hamilton gained 11 places on the opening lap, then struggled as his rear tyres deteriorated. Leclerc described a severe lack of grip and difficulty bringing his tyres up to temperature early on. Both found more pace at other stages.

That combination deserves more attention than another argument about a single radio message. Ferrari needs to establish why useful performance was so difficult to sustain as conditions evolved.

Hamilton’s late spin and Leclerc’s contact with Lawson also carried consequences. Recognising the car’s limitations does not erase the drivers’ mistakes; recognising those mistakes does not explain the entire performance deficit.

Our takeaway

Brazil offers a strong case for judging performance across a complete race, including the difficult laps immediately around tyre changes. A quick stint is valuable only if the team can convert it into a result.

For the remaining races, watch whether McLaren can repeat this execution in different conditions, whether Mercedes resolves its balance questions, and whether Ferrari can make its pace more consistent.

Which team leaves Brazil with the most useful lesson for 2027?

#F1 #BrazilGP

Sources: F1 race report and post-race interviews; McLaren race report.

text:
what really sets elysium apart from every other l2 is native hypercore access through precompiles

hevm has them too but slow blocks, top-of-book-only reads and delayed order writes with no execution guarantee meant they never got used to their full potential. papertrade is one of the few protocols that actually built its core around them

on elysium a contract will be able to read live hypercore state every single hypercore block. full-depth orderbooks, oracle, mark and spot prices, and the balances and positions of any account on hl. it will also be able to send orders to the hypercore books in ~100ms while users keep custody of their funds

so while everyone is fighting over what the next cashcat on elysium will be i think the thing worth watching is what actually makes this chain different: composability with hypercore

none of this is live yet. it ships in an upgrade expected in about four weeks. when it does i hope to see serious builders put it to work. the design space is huge and could give us genuinely new defi/perps primitives

i have a few fun ideas in mind, will talk about them later. until then let the tourists leave and let's wait patiently for the precompiles

Was bored last night so hit up a local izakaya here in Seoul. Pretty good food (7/10), decent ambience, but not much in the way of stimulating conversation. Had a few beers to compensate.

Stumbled out around 3am, fairly inebriated but in excellent spirits. Unfortunately, in my relaxed state, I somehow managed to walk straight into a group of girls from Singapore???. Literally. Apologised profusely, which apparently was enough to establish some sort of international friendship.

One thing led to another, and before I knew it, I'd been adopted by the group and was being escorted to a karaoke bar. Not entirely sure how this happened, but they seemed convinced I was exactly what their evening had been missing. I wasn't about to argue.

Several questionable renditions of early 2000s pop classics later, we were all getting along famously. One of the girls took a particular interest in me, which I initially attributed to my devastating charisma and surprisingly competent rendition of When Doves Cry.

Things were going swimmingly until she leaned over, looked me straight in the eyes and asked, rather seductively, "Do you have a laptop?"
Odd question, I thought, but who am I to judge Singaporean flirting customs?
"Of course," I replied.
She smiled. "Can I borrow it for a few minutes?"

Anyway, fast forward a couple of hours and she's now sitting in my hotel room furiously typing away on my laptop while speaking Mandarin to her brother??? on the phone. Not entirely sure what line of work she's in, but she seems rather stressed about getting a few emails out ASAP.

So she's over there attending to what I assume is some fairly urgent family business, while I'm sitting on the edge of the bed taking 10x leveraged long positions on Zcash.

Neither of us has asked too many questions. I think that's important in any healthy relationship.

Quite nice, really. Two ambitious young professionals supporting each other in the moment.

Let's see what tomorrow brings.

- Sent from my pump fun app.

author: DavidOndrej1
quoted_text:
Anthropic has released Claude Fable 5.2, taking the #1 spot on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 at 65, led by gains in science, knowledge, and coding

At max effort it scores 65, 5 points ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon (high, 60) and 6 ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 59). Gains are driven by scientific reasoning, knowledge and FrontierCode 2.0, and roughly matching Opus 5.5 on AA-Briefcase and Terminal-Bench 4.0.

Priced at $8/$40 per 1M input/output tokens, a 20% reduction from Fable 5.1, Claude Fable 5.2 averages a Cost per Task of $26.5 with max effort, a ~2.6x increase compared to Opus 5.5 (max, $10.0) and ~2x compared to Fable 5.1 (max, $12.99)

Key takeaways:

➤ Claude Fable 5.2 leads 5 of the 9 evaluations in the Intelligence Index: At max effort, Fable 5.2 scores 65, ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon (high, 60), Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 59) and GPT-6 Astra (max, 57), and ~15 points above Claude Fable 5.1 (max, 49). It sets the highest scores on HLE-Diamond (80%, previous best 69% from Gemini 4 Carbon), AA-Omniscience v1.1 (67, previous best 54 from Gemini 4 Carbon), Terminal-Bench-Science (73%, previous best 65% from Gemini 4 Carbon), CritPt v2 hard subset (77%, previous best 72% from GPT-6 Astra) and FrontierCode 2.0 (49%, previous best 46% from Claude Opus 5.5)

➤ Less progress in agentic knowledge work and terminal coding: Claude Fable 5.2 improves on Fable 5.1 across capabilities, but sometimes only to Opus 5.5 levels. It reaches 1785 Elo on AA-Briefcase, within the confidence interval of Opus 5.5 (1800) and just behind Claude Sonnet 5.5 (1813). On GDP.pdf it reaches 24% all-pass against 26% for Opus 5.5. On Terminal-Bench 4.0 it scores 60%, level with Opus 5.5 and behind Kimi K3.1 Pro (67%), Gemini 4 Carbon (65%) and Sonnet 5.5 (64%). AutomationBench-AA is an exception, at 76% against 70% for Opus 5.5, narrowly behind Gemini 4 Carbon, 78%

➤ Lower efforts still take leading positions: With high and xhigh effort, Claude Fable 5.2 scores 62, ahead of every other model at any effort, using 98k output tokens per task against 173k for Opus 5.5 (max). At max effort Fable 5.2 costs ~2.6x more than Opus 5.5, but at lower effort settings it can outperform Opus 5.5 at lower cost per task

Other model details:

➤ Context window: 1 million tokens with image and text input

➤ Pricing: $8/$40 per 1M input/output tokens; cache writes $10 with 5-minute TTL, $16 with 1-hour TTL, and cache reads $0.20

➤ Effort settings: five (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Intelligence Index evaluations were run at all five with Anthropic's default fallback enabled

Congratulations to @AnthropicAI on this impressive release!

very crazy to think about the degree of sheer brilliance of this group when we were just teenagers, and so special to see so many go on to leave their mark on the world.

An initial $39 million will help unlock five projects in neighborhoods across our city. SoMa, the Mission, Bayview-Hunters Point, Potrero Hill, and downtown will all see transformational projects finish sooner, bringing more welcoming public spaces to residents across San Francisco. 

As Mayor, one of my top priorities is making San Francisco a city where families can put down roots and build their futures. Earlier this year, we launched our Family Opportunity Agenda—a citywide effort to bring down the cost of living and expand economic mobility for San Francisco families. 
 
We're building more housing, protecting tenants, expanding access to affordable childcare, and keeping public transportation safe, reliable, and affordable. We're also investing in the public spaces families rely on every day. 

Our parks are an essential part of what makes San Francisco such a special place to raise a family. Our recreation programs provide exceptional and affordable opportunities for San Francisco families. With this investment, we're bringing those opportunities to more neighborhoods across our city, expanding access to recreation, and making our parks even better for the families who use them. 

San Francisco has created enormous opportunity for the people who have built their businesses here. And with that success comes a responsibility to give back to the city that helped make it possible. text:
人类最强模型 Claude Fable 5.2 和 Mythos 5.2 发布。
几乎所有能力都超过了 Opus 5.5 。
这是人类目前最前沿的大模型，没有之一。

一句话简单总结：
人类目前最强模型，价格下降20%，速度提升30%，编程办公不在话下，生物医药和机器人都能搞定。

这是核心信息的快速笔记：
1. 虽然更为智能了，但模型的安全对齐方面，比以往模型都要好或持平（可能使用了他们研究里所说的讲故事对齐法）
2. 几乎所有能力都超过 Opus 5.5，而且沟通风格更加清晰明了
3. 生成速度相比上一代的 5.1 快了 30%
4. 在 FrontierCode 2.0 测试中，Fable 5.2 High 就能打平 Opus 5.5 Max，但每任务成本只要一半。需要注意的是 Fable 5.2 在  Xhigh 时得分最高，比 Max 都高。思考努力程度并非越高越好。
5. 基因疗法可以通过一种称为衣壳的蛋白质外壳进行递送。Mythos 5.2 发现了一种预测整个衣壳结构的新方法。它准确地模拟了其尝试的 34 个衣壳中的 28 个。生物学家可以使用它来更快、更便宜地设计衣壳。
6. 由 1,000 个 Fable 5.2 Agents 组成的团队在 30 小时内完全形式化了费马大定理，将证明翻译成一种计算机可以逐步检查的语言。在相同的设置下，Opus 5.5 在 18 小时内仅完成了 26%，并且在 30 小时后几乎没有取得更多进展。
7. Mythos 5.2 在控制物理机器人方面展现了显著提升的技能，即使是在它从未明确接受过训练的任务上。（和 Astra 一样具备了机器人方面的泛化能力，在其他模型上暂未观察到）在 RoboDojo 上，这是一个带有模拟双臂机器人的基准测试，它超越了其他模型以及大多数专为控制机器人而构建的 AI 系统。
8. 官方建议是，大多数 Coding 和知识任务，建议使用 Opus 5.5 起手，把最具雄心、开放式的技术工作交给 Mythos 和 Fable。
9. 价格方面，8 美元输入，40 美元输出，较之前的 10 美元和 50 美元下降了 20%。

这两个模型是同一个模型的不同版本，Fable 定位更为大众，Mythos 则开放了生物等安全领域。

My name is Dave. I go by The Carnoustie Caddie.

I'm a 5th generation Carnoustie man. This town, the course and the people are in my DNA.

I adore this golf course. I've been carrying bags here since I was 14 years old, and I spend my life working on it and writing about it.

At the beginning of the year I published my first book, The Carnoustie Caddie: How the Course Really Plays.

It's a hole-by-hole guide to the Championship Course, written from a caddie's perspective. Every hole, every bunker, the strategy, the history and the little things I've learned from carrying bags here.

It's been wonderful seeing people from all over the world buying and enjoying it. Something I never imagined when I started writing.

But it's not just the golf I write about. It's the stories, the characters, the named bunkers, the great moments in Open history and the everyday people who travel from all over the world to fulfil their dreams.

Carnoustie is a masterpiece of golf architecture, shaped by some of the greatest architects in the history of the game. Golf's toughest test.

And what a history.

Ben Hogan in 1953. Gary Player hitting what he called the greatest shot of his life in 1968. And a certain Frenchman standing in the Barry Burn with his shoes and socks off in 1999. 🤣

Carnoustie produces drama like nowhere else.

And in 2029, The Open is coming home for the ninth time.

The greatest players in the world are coming back to take on this magnificent course, and I'll be here to share the stories, the history and the inside track as we build towards it.

So if you love golf, give me a follow and a share.

I'll show you why I believe Carnoustie is the greatest golf course in the world.

2029. This caddie cannot wait.

Tell me your favourite Open moments.  

#carnoustie #theOpen #carnoustiecaddie

text:
@HyperliquidX's IOC speed-bump mechanism has a flaw. Normally designed to protect makers in the interests of a more liquid market, it breaks down in periods of high activity. When blocks become full, pending modifies and cancels queue up for later blocks, so their latency increases. However, IOCs behave as though they have a separate blockspace dedicated for them, and their latency barely budges. You can see this in the lower left chart, showing latency of different order types during 19 activity bursts. 

The result is that under relatively modest load (25-30k tps), IOC + 8 bps (priority fee) orders can pick off resting liquidity before it has a chance to get out the way. Meanwhile, under higher load (35-40k tps), even IOCs without any priority fee can pick off resting liquidity. 

This, in my opinion, is antithetical to the ethos and design of the ALO and cancel prioritization mechanism and needs investigation by the team. It exists to reduce toxicity from HFT takers, and is breaking down precisely when most needed. 

It may also be exploitable. If IOCs really are insulated from the congestion affecting cancels and modifies, a malicious user could spam orders, delaying makers’ cancels while their own IOCs go through, and taking the liquidity left stale.

One single example that occurred on AVAX today caused 1.3M$ of volume to be adversely selected for a total loss of ~13k$ over the subsequent 10 seconds. This affected us materially. Faced with such episodes of adverse selection, spreads and liquidity are undoubtedly worse than they could be otherwise.

Would appreciate if anyone with a contact at HL could share this with the team.

text:
韩国半导体市场对美股 AI 和半导体的参考价值 — — 杠杆 ETF 的再平衡

早在六月我就聊过韩国新推出的三星和海力士的杠杆 ETF 为了维持杠杆比例，可能合计卖出了约 60 亿美元的相关股票。

原因是这些杠杆 ETF 需要维持每日的目标杠杆倍数。当标的股票下跌，基金净资产也会跟着下降，基金就需要减少持有的股票或其他市场敞口。跌幅越大，需要调整的规模也可能越大。如果这些交易集中在收盘前，市场上的买盘又不够，就可能进一步放大当天的跌幅。

而目前美股同样有追踪大盘指数、半导体板块和单只科技股的杠杆 ETF。市场上涨时，这些产品为了维持杠杆可能需要增加敞口，市场下跌时，则可能需要减少敞口。

举个简单的例子，一只两倍做多 ETF，假设净资产是 100 美元，对应 200 美元的市场敞口。如果标的下跌 10%，敞口会降到 180 美元，而基金净资产降到 80 美元。为了重新回到两倍杠杆，基金需要把敞口调整到 160 美元，也就是再减少 20 美元的敞口。

所以在市场下跌幅度较大时，除了投资者主动卖出，杠杆 ETF 也可能因为每日调整仓位而增加卖盘。如果卖盘集中出现，市场的买盘实力又不足够大，就可能会加剧下跌，或者是加剧振幅。

说人话就是当初在韩国因为杠杆而导致下跌时候加速下跌的情况现在很有可能在美国股市也会出现。美股股市散户投资者也在追求高收入和大量的采用杠杆 ETF ，这在市场下跌的环境中就会加速下跌。

韩国半导体市场就是最好的例子。

一个 @Gate ，交易更多市场
author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
杠杆资金正在押注美股半导体板块反弹

高盛的数据显示，美国上市的杠杆 ETF 单日净流入 33 亿美元，反向 ETF 净流出 22 亿美元。

ETFIQ 的独立估算显示，11月5日半导体三倍做多 ETF SOXL 净流入约 37 亿美元，三倍做空 ETF SOXS 净流出约 14 亿美元。纳指三倍做多 ETF TQQQ 也净流入约 3.79 亿美元。

大量资金选择进入这类产品，说明有一部分资金愿意承担更高风险，通过杠杆放大对半导体上涨的敞口，而且最空的资金在降低，说明市场普遍看好接下来半导体板块的反弹。

韩国市场今年就出现过类似的杠杆资金集中。韩国 5月 推出的三星和海力士的两倍做多 ETF，从 5月27日到 6月19日，散户累计净买入约 8.2 万亿韩元。

这类产品需要每天调整敞口，来维持目标杠杆倍数。上涨时可能增加买入，下跌时也可能减少敞口。韩国市场随后出现大幅调整，最初由基本面担忧和板块轮动引发，杠杆 ETF 随后放大了跌势。

所以杠杆资金不仅是放大了购买力。为了维持杠杆而进行的交易，也可能让市场的涨跌幅度变得更大。尤其是韩国市场目前的结局就是一旦出现下跌行情，杠杆会加速整个行业的下跌。

quoted_text:
Moods won't be your ordinary @opensea reveal. There are a couple of layers & ways you can play it.

🤙 METADATA 🤙
– Type is permanent. It has your typical rarity structure (Cosmic, Gold, Beef, etcc) that you come to expect from GVC. This dimension never changes.
– Moods also carry their first Expression (happy, sad, stoked, etc). These also have rarity, but they change dynamically 1x per day.

So effectively, you'll get a new reveal every day across the entire collection.

🤙 EXPRESSIONS 🤙
There are two optional ways to play the Expression layer. Think of it as a collector game.

– You can freeze a Mood to lock its expression (hold 100K $STOKED in its wallet). Each expression has a different rarity and "freeze cap" that controls the universal # possible. Some will have a cap of 10, some 20... others only 1-of-1. First come, first serve. Once the cap is reached no more can be frozen. 

– You can stone a Mood to permanently transform it (burn 1M $STOKED). This turns your Mood into a 1/1. Only 1 can exist per expression, first come first serve.

We like to use the Pokemon analogy a lot. There's a set of expressions loaded up in the pool to chase, and that set can dynamically expand over time. Giga rare expressions might remain undiscovered for a while (like a shiny green Onix), some as rare as 1 in 10,000.

Who knows what you might find! 👀

More Moods = more reveals each day, and more chances to find a grail or something ya love.

🤙 SNIPING 🤙
During most reveals, you just check what your hold and hawk what's listed on @opensea.

The big change here is the Anvil pool with @ClutchMarkets.

There are currently 1,239 Moods in the vault.

Those can all be freely sniped at reveal, both tomorrow and every day afterwards, using $STOKED (385K per snipe). Flip side, you can swap a Mood you're not vibing w/ back for $STOKED (315K) and use that to snipe something you like more.

Unlocks a whole new dimension of mobility, liquidity, and potential for collectors.

Happy hunting.

text:
Vitalik 号召将 ETH 的定位，从手续费销毁驱动的价值捕获 (应用链)，转变为价值储存 (SoV)

这也意味着，在 Vitalik 来看，过去几年的 Web3 叙事已经宣布失败。Web3 叙事包括 DAO, NFT, GameFi, SocialFi, DID, 元宇宙, X-to-Earn, CreatorFi 等应用场景，它们很多以 ETH 定价，并且在高 gas 情况下会销毁掉大量 ETH，使 ETH 进入通缩状态

实际上，这两年 ETH 一直处于净增发状态：2025 全年销毁/新增发行的比例为 9.50%，2026 年初至今销毁比例为 2.38%，最近 30 天约为 3.2%

相比其它智能合约公链，ETH 确实在安全、去中心化、抗审查方面有明显优势：这也是为什么它一直是全球黑客赖以生存的公链。但一旦定位于「价值存储」，ETH 就需要跟 BTC 直接竞争，为什么不买 BTC 而是 ETH 呢？

现在白银占黄金市值的 10.34%，而 ETH / BTC 市值之比为 16.49%。考虑到 Ethereum 在智能合约上相比 Bitcoin 有独特价值，二者市值之比长期在 10-20% 之间摇摆倒也合理
author: Sea_Bitcoin
quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

quoted_text:
The Islamic Republic denies negotiations are taking place and demands America’s surrender as the United States briefs the Gang of Eight on Iran and moves a third aircraft carrier toward the region.

Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Islamic Republic’s Supreme National Security Council, dismissed reports of advancing negotiations as “FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks.”

He claimed the war had already “wrecked the US government,” described the United States as a “desperate gambler” and demanded that it “surrender” to the regime’s seven conditions and accept a “West Asian NEW ORDER.”

This directly contradicts claims that productive, reciprocal negotiations are underway.

The Islamic Republic is not proposing talks in which both sides negotiate toward compromise. It demands that the United States surrender much of its leverage before meaningful negotiations begin or the Strait of Hormuz fully reopens.

The regime’s reported conditions include:

▪️ Ending hostilities on every front, including against Iran-backed forces.
▪️ Lifting the American naval blockade.
▪️ Removing sanctions, including restrictions on oil exports.
▪️ Releasing billions in frozen Iranian assets.
▪️ Reducing the American military presence in the region.
▪️ Paying compensation for wartime damage.
▪️ Accepting the regime’s preferred security arrangements for the Strait of Hormuz.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he had “no progress to report,” that talks had not been productive and that the Islamic Republic’s demands were “outrageous,” “ridiculous” and unrealistic.

As diplomacy stalls, the United States is preparing military options.

CIA Director John Ratcliffe and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton reportedly delivered a highly classified Iran briefing to the Gang of Eight—the congressional leaders notified about America’s most sensitive intelligence and covert activities.

The previous comparable Iran briefing reportedly occurred four days before the major US-Israeli strikes that opened the current war in February.

This does not prove another attack has been authorized. The briefing could concern the regime’s intentions, covert operations or military contingencies if diplomacy fails.

But the timing is significant.

Two American aircraft carriers are already operating in the region. The USS Theodore Roosevelt and its strike group are now heading toward the theatre.

It may ultimately replace another carrier, but the overlap could temporarily give the United States three carrier strike groups, substantially expanding its airpower, surveillance and strike capacity.

The broader military posture includes approximately 50,000 American personnel, additional warships and strengthened missile defences.

The United States has also formed Task Force Iron Gate to restrict the Islamic Republic’s remaining land and Caspian supply routes while the naval blockade continues cutting its maritime revenues.

The picture is increasingly stark:

▪️ The Islamic Republic says reports of negotiations are fake.
▪️ The regime demands American concessions before talks begin.
▪️ Rubio says those demands make a breakthrough unrealistic.
▪️ America’s most senior congressional leaders are receiving classified Iran briefings.
▪️ A third carrier is moving toward the region.

Diplomacy has not formally ended, and Qatar continues mediating. But the Islamic Republic’s position is hardening while American military preparations accelerate.

The last time the United States combined a highly sensitive congressional briefing with expanding strike power around Iran, major combat followed within days.

That does not make another attack inevitable, but it strongly suggests the United States is preparing for the possibility that diplomacy has failed.

author: joemccann
quoted_text:
This is going to sound silly, but one of the heuristics that has become a core signal for me and my team over the years is a simple observation: “Vol is alive when it is, well, volatile.”

Without giving away the details around surface reactions and term structure shifts, the idea is straightforward. When vol can explode higher and then cave in just as quickly, repeatedly within compressed time frames, that behavior reinforces our view that volatility is clustering at higher levels and builds our conviction that it can move higher still.

You turn your head one moment, and vol explodes. You turn your head the next, and it gives back practically the entire move. You look again, and it’s above the highs of the recent run.

Those violent reversals can look like noise, but to us, the way vol responds carries information.

These are exactly the kinds of reactions a long vol guy wants to see and a short vol guy hates to see. It’s like the fire that you can’t put out with a bucket of water, and it slowly keeps getting larger and larger.

author: TrungTPhan
quoted_text:
I've changed how I work over the last few weeks.

I now have one lead agent for each area of focus, running all the time, and a chief of staff agent that oversees them. Each lead manages its own sub-agents that write code, test it, chase reviews, and coordinate with team members.

Everything I need to decide or review comes into one prioritized queue, a simple local web app. Each product review includes screenshots and a video demo of the feature. I clear the queue in batches, mostly by voice and keyboard shortcuts. The leads also bring back ideas I hadn't considered.

Working from one queue, instead of switching between dozens of chats, has cut a lot of mental overhead. The system keeps learning my preferences and distilling my judgment into a "Brian brain," so its recommendations and first drafts get better before they reach me. The goal is fewer corrections per change.

Every change still goes through the same human review and security checks. It is eliminating tasks, not human judgment.

What an exciting time to push the frontier of productivity, especially as we build the economy for agents (agentic finance). We should all keep pushing in this direction.

text:
70% of this rant was good but I have to strongly disagree with this take floating around all week that CT is dead. CT is not dead or dying

1) CT is the information hub of crypto industry. It’s the MarketWatch, the CNBC and WSJ, wallstreetbets and town square of the industry. There is no alternative, and that makes it not comparable to fintwit

2) There have always been alternative platforms for social trading in crypto: Telegram last cycle, Discord cycle before that. None of them meant the death of CT (not tg’s arguement but this was the argument of a lot of takes on this)

3) Currently social trading apps are the strongest they’ve ever been but this is a recent meta, and importantly, almost everyone with influence is being paid to post and trade there. We’ve seen this many times before, never this successful for sure, but also never killed CT. Callout rewards have existed for less than 3 months

4) Surprised more people haven’t talked about this, but the one company who could be competitive with crypto social trading apps on day 1, and possibly even pull the rug out of under them on market share, is X itself. If X decided to compete in crypto social trading, I think the crypto-native apps likely survive, possibly pivot to more data and crypto-native experience like current terminals. I find this possibility of X competing in the future more likely than CT dying 

5) If CT does die and social crypto moves to these social trading platforms, the onchain industry will permanently shrink and become more niche. I do not expect this to happen and it hasn’t been the trend 

6) In 2018 there were 50-100 big accounts left on CT, in 2023 we had months where basically nobody was here besides the true believer die hards. This current bear market has genuinely an order of magnitude more people sticking around. CT is more active than it’s ever been with comparable market conditions. And when people want to discuss high level ideas and metas, even non-CT native Fortnite kids, then come to X to discuss them. People who never tweeted during the bull run are now reply guying on X

7) Sure every American knows about crypto, but you go and talk to people and barely anyone understands it, most hate it or think it’s worthless with no value to the tech. This technology is not going away like some trendy brand. There is fundamental value, tokenization is happening, the global markets are embracing stablecoins and blockchains. Many people will never understand crypto tech, but the bulk of the functional adoption curve (people using the tech regardless of if they know they are) is still ahead. Crypto x AI implications and importance are still in their infancy of exploration and discovery. AI will never use cash, and will prefer open blockchains to walled institutions 

8) Possibly we never see the celebrity engagement in onchain markets we’ve seen in past cycle, but if anything that would be a sign of maturity. IMO the entire concept of celebrities and the culture of celebrity worship is plummeting. Not to zero, but I think we’re entering an era where culture and fame is fragmented, and nobody gives a fuck if you’re famous 

Have thoughts about the geeks, MOPs, sociopaths topic for another post. Mostly agree with that part, if anything I think it’s even worse than described, but optimistic how things play out long term

CT is not dead. Crypto is not dead. Crypto is never cool during bear markets but the tech makes the coolest markets of the future most likely to be on, if not only possible on, public blockchains

“Practical principles to counter a modern-day coup/psyop/struggle session”

1) Own what you did but fiercely resist accommodating the mob, resist owning half-truths or actions/behaviors you didn’t do.

2) The op is not about your past actions, it’s about your enemies and this event as their opportunity

3) No matter how bad it gets, nothing is as bad as it seems. 

4) Find the enemies at the very root of the op and find every creative problem-solving tool at your disposal to neutralize them.

5) People will throw their grandmother under the bus if they believe doing so will protect their reputation. They can become highly useful idiots in the op. Their power and access must be fiercely and quickly cut off.

6) Do not hesitate in cutting off anyone you suspect of disloyalty.

7) Build a team of close and loyal patriots and have one of them run a dedicated, well-resourced war room to put the rebellion to rest. 

8) Use your patriots and regular meditation to buoy your psychological resistance to the op. 

9) Your enemies aren’t as smart or hard working as you. Outsmart and outwork them as a way of life until the op is over.

10) Think about the op as if it were in the past. What are the difficult things you procrastinated on or avoided that would have stopped the op? Do them.

11) Never be ashamed of the op. Business as usual. Continue on with optimism and joy in your everyday work and its mission.

12) Download telegram and use it as your messaging application for all sensitive communications.

text:
Thought I’d start with what I’ve observed over the years.. For many years researchers (I was one of them) kept being told by a vocal part of the community that gas should be turned way up and to hell with small nodes. We did hear scaling demand from app devs, at least that they were considering deploying away from L1 because they did not imagine their scaling needs could be met.

It took a while (too long) to internalise that scaling was desirable, particularly given the L2-centric roadmap that considered more or less that activity should be offloaded from the L1 and towards L2s. If app devs go there, that’s a feature! Clearly this thinking has been heavily updated, more towards apps should go wherever they’d best leverage the platform they’re building on, either L1 or L2s.

Then somewhere around March 2025 we sat down more properly and I think that was the first seeds of a clearer scaling roadmap for Ethereum. L2s were in favour too, scaling was useful to them from the blob perspective, but many would also highlight a strong L1 being a better value proposition for them.

Repricings like the ones Glamsterdam intends to do were discussed iirc. They’re not a strange researchy solution in my view, when you look at how to prevent DoS attacks like Shanghai, it’s clear that getting the price right is the first step.

But here it’s more about the long-term load. I don’t think it’s right to say we’re overindexing on historical precedent, the NFT reference was perhaps a bit unhappy. afaict (chart attached below!), state creation is distributed fairly equally over time, and scales linearly with the gas used (the bigger the blocks, roughly proportionally more state).

So then there’s a couple points.

1. Yes state creation increases 5x, bytecode increases 7.65x, but gas limit increases 3.33x, meaning relatively speaking, state creation gets 50% more expensive, and bytecode 2.3x. Not trivial! But some of the state operations besides creation benefit from the block-access list feature that ships with Glamsterdam too. And then future, deeper updates like partitioned binary tree continue to push state access costs down again. Not state creation, afaik, but for bytecode, nodes already don’t keep duplicated code around so proposals like SETCODEFROM can stop charging for it.

2. Then there is the issue of contracts breaking because they have made specific assumptions about the cost of state operations. This is where the line has been that such expectations were misplaced, Ethereum had done such changes in the past etc. I agree with this, and to be clear as a supporter of quick slots, block time is another such parameter that I think we should be allowed to update. But of course it’s a bit of a rollercoaster that transactions were capped at 16.7M gas in Fusaka and now they could be consuming more gas with the reservoir, so this is a legitimate expectation that is now broken shortly after being introduced. It’s mostly a tooling impact more than a contract impact, but still.

3. And then there is the issue of contracts breaking beyond what most would consider legitimate. This was surfaced in reviews and audits, sadly it seems that it wasn’t addressed until late, with pcaversaccio shining a light on these issues that triggered the heightened attention. Most of the attention is on that now, and all known findings are expected to be published by early next week.

Any of the three above could be controversial. On net, I think
1. is neutral-ish, it simply tries to make the best of the limited resources of the network, and state is the resource that doesn’t scale as well as the others, until deeper changes like expiry (if that's ever a thing.. that also has DX implications).
2. has precedents, but it caught more people by surprise than it should have imo.
3. is an issue, and there’s possibly a judgement call to make regarding how to move forward here, I’ll not opine on it until I see more of the findings.

I don’t think this addresses the point about sentiment around the fork. I’m sad that it is this low. From my perspective everyone is clear about building better loops between core protocol and builders, even pointing at the contract size increase contained in Glamsterdam as proof we were finally listening.. but the mark was missed here and the reaction is legitimate.

I’m hopeful that this week and the next will bring a lot more clarity and structure to the discussion. We have a post coming tomorrow (Tuesday) laying out some of these steps.

Fully expect that it won’t clear up every disagreement, and it’s not about explaining away the sentiment of experienced devs either. I talked about Ross’s piece here https://t.co/aqSXdFzW7N because I found it well-balanced, and it led me to consider how the fork would be perceived if the developer outreach had been earlier and stronger. It’s possible that it wouldn’t have changed the core disagreement.

For the future, the only way I see here is to be clear about what expectations are, also something briefly discussed here https://t.co/uLlyHtoThx I’ve seen versions of this around and I expect we’d want to push something like this once the current crisis is resolved.

text:
Jensen is irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership.

In 5G, the US had to play defense against China’s Huawei. In AI, it’s the opposite. NVIDIA leads, and now China is trying to end its reliance on NVIDIA.

Jensen laid the foundation for modern AI 20 years ago. By the time the world realized what AI was, the entire ecosystem was already built on NVIDIA.

And this goes beyond just hardware. In 2006, NVIDIA put CUDA software on regular gaming cards so they could do more than graphics. Investors called it a mistake, until AlexNet proved it was the future.

Competitors might clone hardware, but they can’t just replace 20 years of code, tools and developer knowledge.

The board’s investigation must establish the facts. And as it does, we should remember what Jensen has built.

As he put it, America should have “the first, the most, and the best.” Few people have done more to make that true.

Most of the technology we argue about today stands on ideas that are older than the products built on them:

1976 — public-key cryptography: two strangers can agree on a secret over an open channel.
1985 — zero-knowledge proofs: you can prove a claim without revealing why it's true.
2008 — the Bitcoin whitepaper: nine pages that let strangers agree on a ledger.

Every product on your screen started as a paper somebody had to explain first.

Thank you to everyone who writes them 💜

text:
Interesting product for anyone watching the tokenized stock / RWA space: @metricxyz

Metric uses a propAMM, a provisioned automated market maker, that anchors pool prices to external oracle feeds, including Chainlink data streams, rather than letting the pool discover price on its own

For crypto-native assets that don’t have an obvious off-chain price, that wouldn't work because there is no price to follow. There is only the onchain price. But for tokenized stocks and RWAs that already have a real-world price - Nvidia, Apple, an ETF, etc it makes a lot of sense.

The second cool thing they are building is active pools, which is how metric manages liquidity around that oracle price rather than spreading it across a full price curve

Before going public with the launch, the team reported over $10 billion in cumulative trading volume built in stealth across the Robinhood chain and Ethereum.

Worth watching given where the tokenized stock market is heading post-SEC innovation exemption.

text:
Elysium 泼个冷水,这波新链掘金的几个真相大家不太愿意说

Elysium 主网日的欢呼声太响了,到处都是"下一个 Base""百倍财富密码"。我今天也在玩,但想讲几句反向的真话。

第一,"Day 1 就有基建"这件事不代表成功,代表"车头提前布局到位"。Elysium 公开主网前几周,各个发射台、聚合器、Meme 龙头就已经悄悄部署好了。

这些早期部署者绝大多数是圈内老科学家和项目方团队,不是普通散户。所以今天普通人看到的"繁荣",本质是别人提前搭好的台子。你以为自己是第一波冲进去的,实际上你是接盘的第十波。

第二,HYPE 系的"富人属性"是双刃剑。Hyperliquid 用户平均消费能力强这件事,对生态起势是好事,但对 Meme 玩法是坏事。

富人玩 Meme 的方式是大仓位+短持有,一波涨幅就出,不会像 Solana 散户那样为信仰持币。这意味着 Elysium Meme 的波动会很剧烈,拿不住的概率远大于拿得住。

第三,六家发射台内战意味着"没有真正的赢家"。Volta、Ascend、Kleos、Montra、ElysPump、Boxa 每家都想做头部,真实情况是流量会被稀释到每家都只能吃到一块。

这种格局下,所有平台币的天花板都不会太高。想象 $VOLTA 能复刻 $PONS 从几百万到几亿的朋友,这个前提条件(独家平台)不成立。

CA 参考: $EACC、 $VOLTA、 $A/ACC 等已在前面提到,自行核对。

第四," $A/ACC 24 小时涨 1442%"是个什么信号。这种一天涨 14 倍的标的,背后一定是极小市值+极少筹码+机器人操盘。它不是"下一个百倍梗币"的起点,是"一次性脉冲"的典型特征。追这种盘的散户,99% 最后是亏钱出。

第五,所有 KOL 包括我今天写的这些内容,都要分层解读。真正拿到位置的人不会告诉你 CA,会悄悄撤。喊得最响的 KOL 往往是最想让你接盘的那批。所以记住一个原则:看 KOL 的仓位动向,不看他的观点。

说这些不是看空 Elysium,这条链确实有东西,我自己也在玩。我想讲的是"参与这波的正确姿势"是小仓位、快进快出、重视基础设施、不信百倍神话。

基础设施层面讲一句:用 BG 钱包这种 Day 1 原生支持的工具是真能省很多精力,零手续费活动期间还能省很多钱。

这不是因为我推它,是因为新链玩家最该把精力花在交易判断上,而不是折腾 RPC 和钱包配置上。

工具用对了,操作效率就上去了,这才是真正能影响 PnL 的东西。

@Support @nikitabier — urgent technical follow-up on the unresolved Search/Indexing defect, PSDM-864499 / PSDM-904563.

Verification — Nov 10, 2026, 08:10:04–08:15:17 JST:

The persistent hashtag Latest search discrepancy has been reproduced AGAIN, but this time with an important CHANGE in the observed behavior.

Previously, hashtag Latest repeatedly returned "No results".

Today, hashtag Latest returns OLDER posts from Oct 30 and Oct 29, while omitting my NEWER Nov 10 post.

This change makes the discrepancy particularly clear.

CURRENT POST TESTED:

Published by @senou_higura on Nov 10 at 07:02 JST.

https://t.co/c4veiZjAd1

Hashtag: #JapaneseBeauty5

Approximately 68–73 minutes after publication, the following results were documented.

OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:

01 — from:senou_higura → Latest

Captured at 08:10:04 JST.

The new Nov 10 post is PRESENT.

02 — #JapaneseBeauty5 → Top

Captured at 08:11:18 JST.

The same Nov 10 post is PRESENT.

An older matching post from Oct 31 is also displayed.

03 — #JapaneseBeauty5 → Latest

Captured at 08:12:17 JST, viewed from @senou_higura.

X displays older posts dated Oct 30 and Oct 29.

However, the NEWER Nov 10 post is MISSING.

04 — #JapaneseBeauty5 → Latest

Captured at 08:13:46 JST, viewed from @moneyqueen_m.

The same pattern is reproduced: older posts are displayed, but the Nov 10 post is missing.

05 — #JapaneseBeauty5 → Latest

Captured at 08:15:17 JST, viewed from @higura_pc.

The same omission is reproduced again.

All three viewing accounts are separately logged-in accounts under my control.

THE CRITICAL NEW FINDING:

Hashtag Latest is no longer returning an entirely empty result set.

It is retrieving some matching posts, but the displayed results begin with posts from Oct 30, followed by Oct 29.

My Nov 10 post, which is demonstrably retrievable through both from: Latest and hashtag Top, is not displayed ahead of those older posts.

Furthermore, hashtag Top retrieves another matching post dated Oct 31, which is also newer than the Oct 30 and Oct 29 posts shown in Latest.

This is NOT simply a case of an empty search query.

The Latest search is returning results, but the expected newer matching posts are absent from the displayed chronological results.

THIS IS AN IMPORTANT CHANGE, NOT A CONFIRMED RESOLUTION.

On Oct 27–30 and Nov 4–6, I repeatedly documented hashtag Latest returning "No results" despite matching posts being available in Top.

Today, older matching results have reappeared, but newer posts are still omitted.

I cannot determine whether this reflects partial indexing recovery, stale search results, filtering, or another retrieval problem.

That is precisely why a technical investigation is necessary.

THE ISSUE HAS NOW PERSISTED FOR 13 WEEKS.

I first documented this general failure pattern on Aug 11, 2026.

Today marks exactly 91 DAYS since that initial documented failure.

Throughout this period, I have submitted repeated, timestamped evidence involving different hashtags, publication dates, and viewing accounts.

Despite these reports, I have received no confirmed technical resolution and no confirmation that Search/Indexing Engineering has actually examined the evidence.

Premium Support previously closed PSDM-904563 without resolving the reported behavior.

THIS IS NOT A REQUEST TO INCREASE REACH, ENGAGEMENT, PROMOTION, OR RECOMMENDATION RANKING.

I am reporting a reproducible inconsistency in X's search results.

PLEASE PROVIDE SPECIFIC ANSWERS:

1. What is the current status of PSDM-864499? Has the earlier PSDM-904563 case history been associated with it?

2. Has the engineering team responsible for Search/Indexing actually received and reviewed the evidence? Please confirm the technical escalation status.

3. Why does hashtag Latest retrieve older posts from Oct 30 and Oct 29 while omitting newer matching posts that are accessible through hashtag Top?

4. Does the change from "No results" to older-only results indicate a change in indexing, retrieval, filtering, or another search mechanism?

5. If this behavior is intentional, please identify the applicable rule or documentation. If it is a malfunction, please confirm that it has been recorded for investigation.

EVIDENCE ATTACHED IN ORDER:

01 — from: Latest: Nov 10 post present

02 — Hashtag Top: Nov 10 and Oct 31 posts present

03 — Hashtag Latest: older Oct 30/29 posts visible; newer Nov 10 post missing

04 — Separate viewing account: same omission reproduced

Additional evidence from @higura_pc (screenshot 05) is retained and available upon request.

After 91 days of documented discrepancies, generic explanations about the For You algorithm, engagement, or improving reach are not sufficient.

The specific change observed today deserves a technical explanation.

Please provide a substantive status update, confirm whether this evidence has reached the responsible engineering team, or identify an official support channel capable of investigating this issue.

Thank you.

quoted_text:
L2BEAT is now ETHBEAT, and one of the core ideas behind our mandate is disintermediation. Why does it matter?

Because disintermediation is still one of the most effective ways to protect individual freedom. Intermediaries concentrate power, which makes that power easier to abuse and also creates single points of failure that can affect millions of people.

The recent collapse of Ueno Bank in Paraguay showed this: ~3M people, about 60% of the country's adults, were locked out of their savings, wages and pensions overnight. And that is just the latest example. Before it, we've seen custodians misuse or freeze customer funds, banks turn deposits into equity, data holders expose users to governments and scammers, and more.

Ethereum's value lies in its decentralization, together with the CROPS properties (censorship resistance, open source, privacy, and security), which create a more durable form of stability when other systems come under pressure. Anyone can verify the chain using consumer hardware, independently built clients and open specifications.

ETHBEAT's mandate is to help ensure that the applications and infrastructure built on Ethereum actually forward those properties to users, rather than recreating the same intermediary dependencies we've been trying to reduce in the first place.

Read the full mandate here: https://t.co/eXKdDQFx02
