text:
Last time I tested whether Darkbloom's models can be the brain of a coding agent. They can: 67 of 71 tasks solved for about seven cents. This time I tested the question that decides whether agents become real demand for the network. If an agent starts every task on Darkbloom and only hands the hard ones to a frontier model, does the developer still save money once the failed attempts are paid for?

On real bugs, yes. Starting on Darkbloom made each bug fix 35 to 40% cheaper than Claude alone. Every failed Darkbloom attempt and every handoff is counted in that.

The setup: 20 real Django bugs from SWE-bench Verified, graded by the hidden tests the real fix had to pass. Claude Code ran each bug once on Claude Opus 5.5, and three times on nemotron-3.5-super via @darkbloomai. A bug goes to Claude only when the Darkbloom attempt gives up, or in the stricter version, when it breaks Django's existing tests.

Results with the stricter handoff:
• 52 of 60 attempts never touched Claude
• 55 of 60 solved overall, vs 19 of 20 for Claude alone
• 5.4¢ per bug vs 8.2¢, failed attempts included
• Failed Darkbloom calls (rate limits, timeouts) weren't billed at all, checked against my actual balance. A stuck attempt costs very little
• 23M tokens went through the network, about 216k per bug at the median, and 96.5% of them were input

A Darkbloom attempt took about 4 minutes at the median vs 30 seconds for Claude. So the natural home i think is work nobody watches live: overnight bug queues, CI fixes, code review bots. Those are also the tools that already pick a model for their users. If one of them shipped "Darkbloom first, frontier on failure" as its default, all of its traffic would flow through the network with zero setup.

experiment 3 takes this off the benchmark. I'm turning "Darkbloom first, frontier on failure" into a drop-in router and running my own day-to-day agent work through it, to measure how much of a real developer's agent traffic Darkbloom can carry.

Would love thoughts and especially critics too.
author: oxwizzdom
quoted_text:
I tried to run a 27B coding model on my 16 GB Mac, ofc it failed. It crawled at 0.4 tokens per second, about 200 seconds per tool call. it sucked haha

The same base model on @darkbloomai answered in about 2 seconds. So I ran an Experiment: can the models on Darkbloom's network of idle Macs be the brain of a real coding agent?

The setup: six Darkbloom models, the six tools an agent needs (read, write, edit, shell, grep, glob), and coding tasks executed for real in a sandbox, with every result checked rigorously

Results:
• 60/60 tool calls parsed cleanly
• 67/71 multi-step tasks solved: fixing a bug, renaming across files, finding a planted AWS key, patching a SQL injection
• Qwen3.8 27B, Gemma 4 26B and GLM 5.3 Flash went a perfect 12/12
• Total cost of every run: about 7 freakin cents ( so cheap btw)

The common view is that open models are fine for chat but too flaky for agents. I'm starting to think otherwise.

Here's why it matters. Coding agents burn enormous numbers of tokens, and most of what they do is routine: read a file, search the repo, run the tests. My bet is that 25-40% of an agent's turns can run on @darkbloomai  at a fraction of the price, with only the hard steps staying on frontier models. That's a whole new demand category for a network of idle Macs if successful.

Experiment 2 tests exactly that on real traffic... out soon !!!

I’ve been an NVIDIA shareholder for nearly a decade, and I’ve seen plenty of reasons to sell along the way.

I think this selloff is BS, and I see it as a buying opportunity.

The company’s products are still in demand. Developers are still building on its platform. And the buildout of AI infrastructure isn’t going to stop because of a chaotic news cycle.

I believe Jensen will continue to lead NVIDIA. But this company is also bigger than any one person. It’s thousands of incredibly talented people building products that have taken decades to develop.

Look at Apple. It went through enormous uncertainty around Steve Jobs, yet the business continued to grow and return capital to shareholders. The circumstances are different, but there’s a lesson in looking beyond the headlines.

There could be more volatility ahead. That doesn’t change how I’m thinking about the long-term opportunity.

I’m long NVIDIA, and I’m buying more. $NVDA

text:
Anthropic 估值预期缩水近万亿美元，还是决定硬闯 IPO。

据消息人士透露，Anthropic 计划通过 IPO 募资至多 693 亿美元，发行 8.67 亿股 A 类股，发行价区间为每股 70 至 80 美元。路透社旗下 IFR 报道称，公司将于当地时间周二上午启动纳斯达克 IPO 路演。

但这次 IPO 面临的市场环境，已经和几个月前大不相同。

此前 Anthropic 的潜在估值预期一度高达 2 万亿美元。美股 AI 板块暴跌前，市场讨论的合理估值也在 1.4 万亿至 1.5 万亿美元。

如今，潜在买家讨论的估值区间已经降至 1.2 万亿至 1.3 万亿美元，部分投资者甚至考虑 1.1 万亿美元。

民主党横扫国会、AI 数据中心扩张可能面临更严格的监管审查，再叠加近期 AI 股集体回调，正在重新定价整个行业的增长预期。

有意思的是，Anthropic 并没有选择推迟上市，而是继续按计划推进。

从 2 万亿美元到 1.1 万亿美元，市场对 AI 公司的估值逻辑正在发生变化。

Anthropic 这场 IPO，或许也将成为检验 AI 资本热度的一次重要压力测试。

text:
最近美股大跌，我也认真研究了一下链上代币化股票的流动性挖矿，起初看到 Uniswap V3/V4 LP 动辄几十甚至上百的 APR，还以为发现了什么新的收益来源。

深入研究后发现，本质上还是熟悉的负 Gamma策略。

集中流动性 LP 在价格上涨时被动卖出标的，下跌时被动买入，收益结构与卖出一篮子期权存在相似性。赚取的 Swap Fees，本质上是承担波动率风险和提供流动性所获得的补偿。

但 LP 还有一个额外的风险：LVR，即套利者利用池内价格滞后进行交易所产生的逆向选择损失。这么说来，链上展示的高 APR 并不等于风险调整后的净收益。手续费收入还需要覆盖 LVR、无常损失以及再平衡成本。

既然如此，为什么不考虑更成熟的 Wheel Strategy：Cash-Secured Put + Covered Call？

在震荡行情中，通过卖出 OTM Put 收取 Premium，被指派后持有标的，再卖出 Covered Call，形成循环。

相比 LP，Wheel 同样是 Short Gamma、Short Volatility，期权至少有明确的 Strike、DTE、Premium 和到期盈亏结构，开仓前就能计算最大收益、盈亏平衡点及不同价格情景下的风险敞口。

LP 的手续费收入是浮动且依赖未来交易流量的，而期权的合约收益结构在开仓时就已明确。其实做期权方案应该更可预期

text:
It’s wild how much control @Hypesium gives traders. Being able to manage every single trade right from the #telegram_bot makes it so easy to get into positions early. 

Hypesium is built specifically for Elysium, Kinetiq's Hyperliquid L2, where blocks arrive every 100ms, there's no public mempool, and HYPE is used for gas.

Its first-block execution approach is interesting: routes, calldata and gas are prepared before a pool appears. When the creation event arrives, the bot dispatches through four lanes, targeting an opening-block fill.

But there's another layer beyond execution speed.

Before buying, Hypesium simulates the exact transaction and checks the token against your selected protection profile.

You can choose Safe, Risky, Moon or Off, with configurable tax limits, liquidity floors and sell checks. If a token fails the checks, the bot skips it.

For launch hunting, you also get more than ordinary pool sniping. You can target a deployer's next token, watch for specific names and tickers, or mirror tracked wallets.

And once you're in, stop-losses, trailing floors and take-profit ladders help automate your exit strategy.

Even the referral structure has multiple layers, with daily HYPE payouts, up to 45% direct referral rewards by rank, and 10% lifetime fee discounts for referred users.

My takeaway is simple:

Speed gets you to the opportunity. Execution, protection and exit planning determine how well you handle it.

That's the combination worth watching as Hypesium develops on Elysium.

text:
一句话都没说的融资会

SF，早上八点四十，一间不到两百平米的办公室。

林舟把咖啡放在会议桌上，看了一眼墙角。那台人形机器人站在充电座上，胸口的灯一明一暗，像在呼吸。

三个月前，他花了一个周末，把这台机器人从箱子里搬出来，打开手机上的一个应用，接上网络，在"选择大脑"那一页停了几秒，选了今天能用的最聪明的那一个，Fable 5.2。那天晚上，机器人第一次开口跟他说话。没有工程师，没有调试，也没有写一行代码。

今天九点，Sand Hill 一家基金的合伙人王总要来。这是林舟这轮融资里最重要的一场会。

"今天你来主讲。"林舟对机器人说，"我坐旁边。"

"好。"机器人从充电座上走下来，"王总上周在一个 podcast 里说，他最近看了二十家机器人公司，最怕的是演示做得漂亮、交付的时候一塌糊涂。我会注意。"

林舟愣了一下，笑了。

——

八点五十八，电梯门打开。

王总走出来，第一眼看到的不是林舟，而是一台站在门口的人形机器人。

"请问是王总吗？"

王总下意识停住脚步："……是我。"

"欢迎。"机器人伸出手，"林总在会议室等您，这边请。"

那只手是三根手指的金属手，握上去不冷也不硬，力度刚好。王总低头看了一眼，没忍住，笑出了声。

走廊不长。机器人走在前面半步，节奏很稳，到拐角时停了一下，让王总先过。

——

会议室里，王总刚坐下，机器人就从桌边拿起一瓶没开封的水。

它低头看了看瓶盖，握住，拧了一下，没拧动。

"比我想的紧一点。"它说，"我换个握法。"

手指往下挪了半寸，重新握紧，再拧，"咔"的一声，开了。它把水放到王总面前："路上辛苦，先喝口水。"

王总盯着那瓶水，看了足足两秒，然后转头看林舟："你们专门教过它开瓶子？"

林舟摇头："没有。它是自己琢磨出来的。"

——

"给王总讲讲我们的战略吧。"林舟说完，往椅背上一靠，端起了咖啡。

机器人走到白板前，拿起一支蓝色马克笔。

"我们只做一件事，但这件事分三层。"

它画了第一个框，写上"云端"："第一层，接上全世界最好的大模型。今天最聪明的是哪一家，就用哪一家；明天换了，我们也跟着换。"

第二个框，写上"身体"："第二层，装在机器人身上，管手脚，管安全。网络断了，它也知道该停下来。"

第三个框，写上"人"："第三层，AI 搞不定的时候，一秒钟内有人接手。"

最后，它画了三条箭头，把三个框连在一起，在中间写了两个字："中立"。

"大模型公司想让每台机器人只认自己，机器人厂商不想被任何一家卡住脖子。我们站在中间，谁都不得罪，谁都离不开。"

它退后半步，看了一眼自己画的图，像是在检查有没有画歪，然后点了点头。

——

回到桌边，iPad 平放在桌面上，屏幕上是这轮融资的 deck。

机器人伸出一根手指，轻轻一划，翻到第二页。

"这是我们第一批客户……"

它一页一页往后翻、往后讲。讲到第七页时，王总忽然伸手把 iPad 拿了过去，拿起 Apple Pencil，在收入那一栏随手划了几笔，又把 iPad 推了回来，什么也没说。

机器人弯下腰，凑近屏幕，停了两秒。

"这里被改过了。原来是 120 万，现在写的是 210 万。"它直起身，"我想您是在考我。"

会议室安静了一秒，然后王总大笑起来。林舟也笑了。这是今天他第一次笑出声。

——

接下来的四十分钟，王总问了很多问题：毛利、竞争、团队、为什么不自己造机器人、大模型公司会不会绕过你们。

每一个问题，机器人都答得清清楚楚。有几次，它在回答之前停顿两秒，点一下头，说"我想一下"。林舟知道，那几秒钟里，后台正在把这个问题交给更聪明、也更贵的那个大脑。

整整四十分钟，林舟一句话都没说。

直到王总放下笔，看着林舟，问了一个问题："你为什么要做这件事？"

机器人转过头，看向林舟，说："这个问题，只有他能回答。"

林舟放下咖啡，讲了大概三分钟。讲他大学时在实验室里看过的第一台机械臂，讲他第一次看到 AI 写出一段完整代码时的感觉，讲他为什么觉得 AI 不应该只活在屏幕里。

王总听完，又问了一句："你愿意为它赌上什么？"

林舟想了想，说："全部。"

这是那场会里，他说的最后一句话。

——

送王总到电梯口时，王总停下来，回头看了一眼站在走廊尽头的机器人。

"这台机器人，"他问，"你们卖吗？"

"我们不卖机器人。"林舟说，"我们卖的，是让每一台机器人都这么聪明的那样东西。"

王总想了几秒，点点头。

电梯门关上之前，他说："下周我带合伙人再来一趟。"

——

那天晚上，办公室的灯关了。机器人回到充电座上，胸口的灯又开始一明一暗。

林舟的手机亮了一下：

"今天的会议纪要已经整理好了。王总问了 23 个问题，我回答了 21 个，剩下 2 个是你回答的。他下周二上午有空，我已经发了会议邀请。晚安。"

林舟看着屏幕，想起王总在电梯口问的那个问题。

二十多年前，人们第一次在手机上装应用；十多年前，人们第一次把公司搬到云上。而今天，在一间不到两百平米的办公室里，一台机器人替它的主人开完了一整场融资会，只把两个问题，留给了人类自己。

text:
Most of you probably haven't noticed this, but dots have a new feature called multi-exec that we quietly released on friday. I've been using it all weekend on my personal dot and it's incredibly powerful.

I'd like to share why this is a big deal and how to use it. 

At a high level, multi exec lets your dot run commands directly on any computer. This immediately turns your dot into a real virtual employee. Here's why it's a gamechanger:
- you can attach a powerful machine with persistent storage to your dot (I attached it to my maxed out Mac Studio Ultra)
- the dot can now drive your computer directly via Computer Use
- this extends to browser use
- all your websites stay logged in, residential ip etc
- you set up all your CLIs and authentication ONCE and the dot can use them directly (no more fighting the default ephemeral cloud computer)
- the dot can save skills locally for repeated workflows and subagents can use those directly
- if you have a local obsidian memory vault for your agents, your dot can use that too
- building ios app end to end and testing it in xcode, and showing me screenshots of progress as it works
- all of the above also applies to any subagents your dot delegates to in the cloud (subagents share context unlike separate threads).

To enable it, open the desktop app on your computer and hit "allow computer", then give your dot this prompt:

"Hey I just connected my computer. Can you attach to it directly so it's your default computer and you can run commands directly on it? Do it in your root thread so that all subagents inherit this computer for running commands. Run whoami to run water through the pipes and verify it works end to end."

I recommend attaching your dot to the most powerful machine you have and investing time into it up front:
- Log into all the emails & websites you need e.g. stripe cli, gcloud, firebase, etc
- Install and auth all the CLIs, git you need
- Make sure computer use is turned on and allowed to use your computer while its locked 
- I also enabled Allow All for Browsing and Downloads so my dot could use computer use to download whatever it wanted from websites without asking me for approval for each domain (use at your own risk). 
- Important: I HIGHLY recommend to ask your dot to build out repeated workflows as skills, and iterate to make those skills bulletproof by running water through the pipes with its subagents. 

As of this weekend, my dot is sending me screenshots of its progress building my iOS app end to end on my Mac Studio Ultra via xCode, and clicking around and testing things end to end. It's able to configure things in stripe via the CLI and use websites when it needs to download images for my workflows. It’s night and day. Don't sleep on it.

quoted_text:
Honestly, 12 months ago I thought “sovereignty” was a BS marketing message for founders to leverage to get funding.

Now I think it is a strategic imperative and will breed some of the largest companies of our time.

Mistral is the poster child of sovereignty. The last remaining hope for Europe when it comes to frontier model providers.

I sat down with @MistralAI CEO, @arthurmensch to debunk the hype from reality and ask the uncomfortable questions. My notes from the discussion below.

1. Why Energy Is Not the Ultimate Cost That Matters

Energy makes up around 10% of the total cost of ownership of compute, so it is not where most optimization can happen. The cost of energy is not the one thing that matters in the economics of a project.

Love to hear your thoughts on this @alanchanguk @ChaseLochmiller @ZachBDell

2. What Would Mistral Do Differently If They Were Totally Resource-Unconstrained?

Mistral would build much more capacity, with capital as the main bottleneck. Customers are running out of compute, and once one use case scales they need thousands of GPUs rather than eight. Europe does not have enough compute, so Mistral is putting equity to work to build capacity ahead of demand.

Love to hear your thoughts on this, if you were resource unconstrained today, what would you do differently @alexmashrabov @bavaria_kush

3. How the Inference Market Behaves Very Much Like a Commodity Market

On-demand inference behaves like a high-margin commodity market where pricing matters a lot and demand comes from non-committed customers. Mature customers need service level agreements, reserved physical capacity and guarantees on latency and generation speed. The more precisely they describe the shape of their demand, the better Mistral can price it.

What does no one see about the inference market that everyone should see @tuhinone @neilmovva @lqiao

4. Models Have Gotten So Strong They Are Being Treated as Defense Systems

Models are now strong enough to carry out cyberattacks, and the US began banning them outside the country in May. China is also looking at restricting exports beyond a certain threshold. As with any dual-use technology, customers now want security of supply on both infrastructure and model IP.

What does no one see about the future of security that everyone should see @zeyu1337 @nikesharora @pilvar222

5. Will We End Up With a Model Landscape That Has Just Two to Three Providers?

If every company relies on two or three centralized AI providers, those providers gain enormous leverage. They will use the data their systems produce to build better systems and go after their customers' business, an end game Arthur sees as priced in today.

What will the model landscape look like in 5 years @emostaque @AnjneyMidha @mmurphy

6. The Biggest Problem With AI Effectiveness Within Enterprise Today Is...

Most enterprise problems are not well defined, and ambiguous objectives with humans in the loop cannot be solved through self-improving loops. They only get solved by deploying models that interact with people, which is why Mistral uses FDEs to define problems better.

7. Why You Can Go Public in Europe and Negativity Around European Stock Markets Is BS

Mistral can absolutely go public in Europe, because the bottlenecks of 10 years ago are no longer there. There is a huge appetite from investors worldwide to invest in Europe in both private and public equity. Mistral is preparing for the operational constraints of being public while delivering on its commercial milestones.

You think this is true, you really think you can go public in Europe @eldsjal @klarnaseb

text:
台湾国安基金，竟然成了比特币的另类抄底指标？

这个角度确实绝了。

我第一次见有人把台湾国安基金的出手时间，拿来对照比特币的历史底部。

历史上比特币诞生之后，台湾国安基金一共出手过5次：

2011年欧债危机
2015年人民币贬值
2020年疫情熔断
2022年熊市
2025年关税战

除了2022年没有踩中绝对底部，其他几次事后看，都非常接近BTC的周期底部或阶段性低点。

稍微研究了下，台湾国安基金不是来买比特币的，它的任务是稳定台股。

但台湾股市高度集中在半导体和科技产业，当全球风险资产遭遇剧烈抛售、外资大规模撤离、市场恐慌达到一定程度时，才会触发官方护盘机制。

所以它更像一个特殊的市场温度计：当台湾政府都认为市场恐慌严重到需要动用国家级资金救市时，全球风险资产可能已经经历了一轮极端去杠杆。

11月6日，国安基金第十次获准启动护盘，也是比特币诞生以来的第六个样本。

这次能不能再次对应BTC底部，还需要时间验证。

We’re bringing that experience and the relationships built along the way into our work on Gravity.

As part of this consolidation, we will wind down Galxe Quest, Galxe ID, Galxe Passport, and related services. Gravity will continue operating as usual, with no changes to the G token as part of this transition.

Starting today, Spaces can no longer create new campaigns. New Galxe+ and Galxe Score subscriptions and Galxe Passport minting are also no longer available.

December 5, 2026, will be the last day to participate in campaigns. No campaigns will remain active after that date. On December 15, 2026, campaign reward claims will close, and the entire Galxe website will switch to read-only mode. Please claim any outstanding campaign rewards before December 15.

User assets remain safe, including Smart Savings balances, staked G that has not yet been withdrawn, and G tokens held in wallets on Gravity Alpha Mainnet. These assets will follow a separate claim process and timeline. We will publish the details and instructions in a follow-up announcement on our official X.

Thank you to the users, builders, and partners who helped shape Galxe. We look forward to continuing to build with you on Gravity.

text:
《民主党拿下国会，哪些币姓共和，哪些币姓民主？》
民主党刚刚拿下美国参众两院，黄仁勋的婚外情就被曝光了。

更耐人寻味的是，特朗普此前早已收到过涉及黄仁勋的情报简报，却始终按兵不动、选择默许。如今国会两院即将易手，曾经默契存在的政治庇护不复存在，黄仁勋势必将直面来自民主党方面的严苛审视。

很多人因此猜测，黄仁勋是不是故意抢在共和党交权前，主动自曝、提前结案，试图赶在民主党正式掌权之前，把这场风波控制住？

与此同时，民主党的反击风暴早已迫不及待地砸向了特朗普本人。预计接掌众议院监督委员会的 Robert Garcia 就公开喊话「LAWYER UP」（准备请律师吧），并明确表达，将重点调查特朗普家族的加密货币收入及其他商业利益。

如今民主党重新夺回国会，特朗普家族的加密生意即将面临新的政治审查。那么，哪些代币与共和党直接绑定？哪些项目背后又有民主党的政治金主？

🌟共和党阵营：特朗普家族直接下场发币
相比传统的政治捐款，特朗普家族早已亲自下场做 Crypto 生意。

2026 年 6 月，路透社发表了一篇针对特朗普家族加密业务的深度调查。根据链上交易、财务披露和公司文件估算，特朗普家族自其重返白宫以来，通过四项主要加密业务累计获得约 23 亿美元收益。

1、$TRUMP：总统亲自发币，把政治影响力直接变现
2025 年 1 月 17 日，特朗普在正式就职前三天推出 TRUMP，总供应量 10 亿枚，其中 80% 分配给特朗普关联公司及项目相关方。

根据路透社调查，TRUMP 项目累计产生约 12 亿美元代币销售收入，其中约 6.16 亿美元流向特朗普家族。

2、$CRO：数千万美元押注特朗普，监管松绑与商业合作接踵而至
https://t.co/rVcnYSWx3m 是其中比较典型的案例。据 Public Citizen 2026 年 10 月的调查，其关联公司累计向支持特朗普的 MAGA Inc. 和 Keep America Great 两个超级政治行动委员会捐赠约 3700 万美元。

2025 年 3 月，SEC 结束了对 https://t.co/rVcnYSWx3m 的调查。同年，https://t.co/rVcnYSWx3m 又与特朗普媒体集团达成合作，计划成立持有 CRO 代币的上市公司。

3、$ONDO：Ondo Finance 的政治捐款与监管调查
公开记录显示，Ondo 向特朗普就职基金捐赠 100 万美元，另向支持特朗普的 MAGA Inc. 捐赠约 210 万美元，合计约 310 万美元。

2025 年 2 月，Ondo 宣布与特朗普家族的 World Liberty Financial 达成战略合作。同年 12 月，SEC 正式结束了针对 Ondo 的多年调查，没有提出指控。

4、$DOGE：马斯克的 Meme 币，连特朗普政府部门都用了它的名字
DOGE 长期与马斯克绑定，马斯克不仅多次公开为狗狗币站台，还在 2024 年大选期间投入巨额资金支持特朗普。

特朗普胜选后，宣布由马斯克参与领导的「政府效率部」，英文缩写恰好是 DOGE，与狗狗币同名。该项目还曾使用柴犬形象，进一步强化了两者的联系。

5、$PNUT：被共和党当作竞选象征的松鼠币
2024 年美国大选前夕，纽约州政府因狂犬病防疫问题，将网红松鼠 Peanut 没收并实施安乐死，引发舆论争议。

特朗普、万斯和马斯克随后借此批评政府过度干预，马斯克甚至公开喊话为 Peanut 投票。事件迅速演变成共和党的竞选话题，Solana 上的 PNUT Meme 币也因此走红，并在特朗普胜选后大幅上涨。

7、$SOL：公司给特朗普就职基金写支票，又被总统点名进“储备名单”
2025 年 1 月 8 日，Solana Labs 向特朗普—万斯总统就职委员会捐赠 100 万美元。这笔款项后来出现在该委员会4月公开的 FEC 文件中。

几天后，特朗普和梅拉尼娅分别推出官方 Meme 币 $TRUMP 与 $MELANIA，两者都选择在 Solana 上发行。
政策叙事随后进一步强化。2025 年 3 月 2 日，特朗普在 Truth Social 点名 XRP、SOL、ADA，并称 BTC、ETH 也将成为美国加密储备的组成部分。

🌟民主党阵营：从个人金主到政策游说，Crypto 巨头同样重金下注

共和党有特朗普家族亲自下场做生意，民主党也不缺 Crypto 金主。从千万美元的个人献金，到行业巨头的政治游说，加密资本早已深入民主党的政治资金网络。

1、$XRP：Ripple 创始人曾豪掷千万美元支持哈里斯
2024 年美国大选期间，Ripple 联合创始人 Chris Larsen 向支持民主党候选人哈里斯的政治行动委员会捐赠超过 1100 万美元，其中大量捐款直接使用 XRP 支付。

但 Ripple 并没有只押注民主党。2025—2026 年选举周期，Ripple 公司向加密行业政治行动委员会 Fairshake 捐赠了 4800 万美元，同时还向特朗普的总统就职基金捐赠约 489 万美元。

2、$UNI：Uniswap Labs 也投入百万美元政治资金
根据美国联邦选举委员会记录，Uniswap Labs 通过旗下公司 Universal Navigation，在 2025 年向 Fairshake 捐赠约 100 万美元。

这笔资金没有直接进入民主党候选人的账户，而是进入了一个同时支持两党候选人的政治行动委员会。

3、$PEPE：被重新政治化的青蛙 Meme
2016 年特朗普竞选期间，Pepe 青蛙被美国另类右翼大量使用，一度成为特朗普支持者的网络象征。

后来，原作者发起「Save Pepe」运动，试图夺回这个角色。再加上右翼评论员 Alex Jones 曾声称「化学物质会让青蛙变成同性恋」，于是网友把 PEPE 划入民主党阵营，调侃这只共和党青蛙最终也被「彩虹化」了。

4、$FTT：SBF 曾是民主党最大的 Crypto 金主之一
FTX 创始人 SBF 曾是民主党的重要政治金主。2022 年美国中期选举期间，他向政治组织捐赠约 4000 万美元，绝大部分流向民主党阵营，一度成为民主党最大的个人捐款人之一。

FTX 前工程主管 Nishad Singh 也向民主党相关组织捐赠超过 1300 万美元。

2022 年 11 月 FTX 破产，SBF 后因欺诈被判刑，FTT 也随之崩盘。

5、$WLD：民主党长期金主 Sam Altman 的加密项目
Worldcoin 由 Sam Altman、Alex Blania 等人共同创立，WLD 是其生态代币。

2024 年美国大选周期中，Sam Altman 向拜登胜利基金捐赠了 20 万美元。该基金是拜登竞选团队、民主党全国委员会及各州民主党组织的联合筹款委员会。

此外，Altman 长期向多名民主党候选人和进步派政治组织捐款，因此 WLD 也被市场视为民主党代币。

6、$LINK：民主党科技金主 Eric Schmidt 曾任 Chainlink 顾问
2021 年，Chainlink Labs 宣布前 Google CEO Eric Schmidt 加入团队，担任战略顾问。Schmidt 长期支持民主党，曾参与奥巴马竞选及政府科技咨询工作。

2024 年大选周期，他向 Biden Victory Fund 捐赠约 41.3 万美元；美联社统计，他向拜登及相关民主党筹款组织的捐款合计超过 50 万美元。

🌟写在最后
黄仁勋的出轨风波，像一记重锤，砸向了看似坚不可摧的科技神坛，也让市场开始重新审视 AI 狂热背后的估值泡沫。

更大的多米诺骨牌则在华盛顿倒下。民主党重掌国会，意味着特朗普家族依靠 Meme 币、DeFi 积累的巨额利益，即将面临传票、听证与合规审查。

在权力全面洗牌的这一刻，两场曾经风光无两的狂欢，正在同时迎来它们的算账时刻。

🇺🇸 Wall Street will trade Tuesday’s CPI inflation report half-blind, with no yearly number and 84% odds of a Fed HIKE.

BLS says it "will not publish 12-month percent changes" for October, because the government never collected October 2025 prices during the 43-day shutdown.

Traders will have to rely on unofficial estimates, ranging from 3.6% to 4.0%.

The last official reading was 3.7% in September, up from 2.4% in February, before the Iran war sent oil soaring.

It peaked at 4.2% in May, the highest since April 2023.

What Americans paid more for over the past year:

1. Fuel oil: +74.2%
2. Gasoline: +34.2%
3. Airfares: +22.4%
4. Natural gas: +5.0%
5. Electricity: +4.4%
6. Rent and housing: +3.2%

Meanwhile, paychecks are falling behind, with real hourly earnings down 0.7% over the past year, per BLS.

The Fed already hiked in September for the first time since July 2023.

In October, two officials voted for another hike right away.

Economists expect prices rose about 0.3% in October, half of September’s 0.6% jump.

But with rates at 3.75% to 4.00%, even a small surprise could lock in a December hike.

All eyes are now on Tuesday’s 8:30 AM ET release, the last CPI report before the Fed’s Dec 9 decision.

text:
I think people are reading too much into the spy angle on Jensen and China. The simpler explanation is a business one.

Jensen knows Chinese history well, and he knows that when the Chinese state decides something will happen, it happens. Right now the state wants chip independence. If you accept that it’s coming, then Nvidia’s biggest accelerator competitor in ten years won’t be AMD. It will be a Chinese company.

We’ve seen this pattern over and over: steel, then general manufacturing, and most recently electric vehicles. China will absorb short-term pain for a long-term objective. Hundreds of companies pile into a sector, most of them fail, and the lessons compound until the survivors lead the world.

Xiaomi is the clearest example. A phone maker built a car that competes with the best American carmakers, and it’s delivered over 700,000 of them in about two years. The US has effectively walled Chinese EVs off with 100% tariffs and restrictions on Chinese connected-car technology. Europe hasn’t, and you can see the result: BYD now outsells Tesla there, and in the UK it recently sold four times as many cars. Xiaomi launches in Europe in 2027.

Given all that, Jensen’s best move is to delay the inevitable for as long as possible. The longer the Chinese ecosystem stays hooked on Nvidia GPUs, the longer it takes China to build a competitor that can challenge Nvidia globally.

Funny enough, he’s fighting both governments at once, because the US and China are quite aligned here. Both want Nvidia chips out of China, for opposite reasons. When Washington finally approved H200 sales (an older-generation GPU), Beijing turned around and blocked them from importing.

That’s what hard export controls buy you. Cut China off and you force it to innovate, and it will. It will catch up.

According to The Information, NVIDIA has long lobbied hard against proposals to restrict Chinese companies’ access to its latest chips through overseas cloud providers. But since the scandal surrounding Jensen Huang broke, that lobbying appears to carry less weight in Washington.

The fallout has reportedly made it easier to advance three bills. The MATCH Act would restrict shipments of lithography equipment to China. The Overwatch Act would give Congress greater oversight of the Commerce Department’s decisions to approve AI chip sales to countries such as China. The Chip Security Act would require AI chips to have built-in tracking capabilities.

The National Defense Authorization Act is expected to pass before the new Democratic-led Congress convenes in January. That gives Republican leaders an incentive to help move the legislation forward now, while they still have more say over what goes into the final bill.

text:
today we launched The Method, an @MTSlive original mini-doc series that tells the story of the founders behind the world’s most important companies.

since joining MTS, I’ve interviewed hundreds of founders. and the biggest lesson I’ve learned is that the best founders are deeply optimistic. when you understand how they think, what motivates them, and why they dedicate their lives to shaping the world, you can’t help but want to do it too. 

a lot of the personal ambitions in my life have come from reading memoirs. I remember reading Shoe Dog, and feeling inspired by how Phil Knight relentlessly pursued what he knew to be true, even though the rest of the world didn't see it yet. when Nike was founded, “personal fitness” wasn’t a thing, working out was a fringe subculture, and people would even spit on runners in the street. then Phil came along and changed the world’s relationship to fitness forever.

even if you don’t personally care about running, Phil’s story was a reminder that the future is malleable and every person has agency to shape it.

today, people are launching rockets and curing cancer. there are no limits to what's possible. information is democratized, the cost of building is practically free, and entrepreneurship is on the rise. It's never been a better time to act on your ambitions. and understanding others who have done so, gives us a blueprint on how to do the same.

a big thank you to all the people who brought The Method to life. MTS is expanding beyond a livestream to a full media network and today marks the start of this new era. first episode airs tomorrow!

以太坊并不总是走在正确的道路上，但它始终在尝试寻找正确的方向。

2017 年的那四年，以太坊选择了一条正确的道路。

2021 年的那四年，以太坊也选择了一条正确的道路。

但在 2025 年开始的这四年，以太坊似乎选错了方向。

它逐渐偏离了自己真正的优势和长期愿景，放弃了与美元、黄金、比特币竞争的可能性，反而把太多精力放在了与其他 L1 公链争夺市场份额上。

但现在，Vitalik 似乎正在意识到这个问题。

他正在为 2029 年的以太坊，重新寻找一条道路。

一条能够重新定义以太坊价值、重新确立以太坊长期定位的道路。

没有人能够永远正确。

乔布斯如此，马斯克如此，Vitalik 也不例外。

重要的从来不是它有没有犯过错，而是它能不能意识到错误，并有勇气重新出发。

再给 Vitalik 和以太坊一次机会。

也给自己一次机会。

就像当年在 2006 年选择相信乔布斯，在 2016 年选择相信 Elon Musk 一样。

他们，都曾站在第二次崛起的前夜。

quoted_text:
Terence Tao says that the AI proof on the Navier–Stokes problem is correct, yet mathematicians learned almost nothing from it. The proof is 100 pages, AI-generated and full of issues in its text, but a formal certificate in the language Lean confirms it.

Navier–Stokes is a Millennium Prize problem that asks whether the equations for fluids like water can start smooth and then blow up, with velocity or pressure becoming infinite. Human mathematicians came very close, and OpenAI ran its biggest model, with millions of dollars of compute, to get there first.

A human proof normally comes with talks on what was tried, what worked and what it connects to, like picking fruit and planting the seeds. Tao calls this one strip mining: the fruit taken, the landscape left barren. One colleague, using lots of AI, could explain only half of it after days of work.

This is also the 2nd-largest such deviation since the 2022 bear market.

By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis and following the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble burst, this metric dropped to -49% and -52%, respectively.

This marks a sharp reversal from June, when SOX traded +75% above its 200-day moving average, its largest positive deviation since 2000.

In other words, semiconductor stocks have shifted from extremely overbought to oversold territory in just 5 months.

Semiconductor stocks just saw one of their most violent swings in decades.

text:
In 2015, I built an AI that detects early cancer.

It’s still running across hundreds of hospitals in the US today.

It was the most fulfilling work of my life, and I was building in AI years before everyone called it “AI”.

Building in AI then was a dream.

Now It feels like we’ve taken a turn for the worse.

It started when i was in undergrad.

I built my first company: AI models that made the political data transparent to voters.

At 21, I was offered six figures for it, but the buyers wanted to use it for reasons I couldn't ethically support.

So we turned down the offer and shut down the company instead.

In 2014, I moved into deep learning research on language models, for the Intelligence Community and Goldman Sachs.

Then HCA Healthcare came to us.

They put me in a competition against 10 people from IBM Watson. It was just me and the tools I’d built.

Our job was to build an AI model that can catch the cancer that slips through the cracks in hospitals.

It was the most intense 30 days of my life. Multiple all nighters.

My models won. That turned into a $5M deal, and later its own company, Azra AI.

Then the world caught on.

ChatGPT and Claude arrived, and AI costs exploded.

Building in AI in 2015 felt novel.

We were using it to find cancer tumours and save lives.

Now the biggest tech companies have turned AI into a money extraction machine.

That’s when I decided to make a change.

We raised $8.5M to build a better future for AI.

On Wednesday, we’re launching Rayline.

AI shouldn’t be locked inside a few labs’ models, prices and clouds. It should be open, transparent and decentralized.

More on Wednesday.

text:
Anthropic has released Claude Fable 5.2, taking the #1 spot on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 at 65, led by gains in science, knowledge, and coding

At max effort it scores 65, 5 points ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon (high, 60) and 6 ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 59). Gains are driven by scientific reasoning, knowledge and FrontierCode 2.0, and roughly matching Opus 5.5 on AA-Briefcase and Terminal-Bench 4.0.

Priced at $8/$40 per 1M input/output tokens, a 20% reduction from Fable 5.1, Claude Fable 5.2 averages a Cost per Task of $26.5 with max effort, a ~2.6x increase compared to Opus 5.5 (max, $10.0) and ~2x compared to Fable 5.1 (max, $12.99)

Key takeaways:

➤ Claude Fable 5.2 leads 5 of the 9 evaluations in the Intelligence Index: At max effort, Fable 5.2 scores 65, ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon (high, 60), Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 59) and GPT-6 Astra (max, 57), and ~15 points above Claude Fable 5.1 (max, 49). It sets the highest scores on HLE-Diamond (80%, previous best 69% from Gemini 4 Carbon), AA-Omniscience v1.1 (67, previous best 54 from Gemini 4 Carbon), Terminal-Bench-Science (73%, previous best 65% from Gemini 4 Carbon), CritPt v2 hard subset (77%, previous best 72% from GPT-6 Astra) and FrontierCode 2.0 (49%, previous best 46% from Claude Opus 5.5)

➤ Less progress in agentic knowledge work and terminal coding: Claude Fable 5.2 improves on Fable 5.1 across capabilities, but sometimes only to Opus 5.5 levels. It reaches 1785 Elo on AA-Briefcase, within the confidence interval of Opus 5.5 (1800) and just behind Claude Sonnet 5.5 (1813). On GDP.pdf it reaches 24% all-pass against 26% for Opus 5.5. On Terminal-Bench 4.0 it scores 60%, level with Opus 5.5 and behind Kimi K3.1 Pro (67%), Gemini 4 Carbon (65%) and Sonnet 5.5 (64%). AutomationBench-AA is an exception, at 76% against 70% for Opus 5.5, narrowly behind Gemini 4 Carbon, 78%

➤ Lower efforts still take leading positions: With high and xhigh effort, Claude Fable 5.2 scores 62, ahead of every other model at any effort, using 98k output tokens per task against 173k for Opus 5.5 (max). At max effort Fable 5.2 costs ~2.6x more than Opus 5.5, but at lower effort settings it can outperform Opus 5.5 at lower cost per task

Other model details:

➤ Context window: 1 million tokens with image and text input

➤ Pricing: $8/$40 per 1M input/output tokens; cache writes $10 with 5-minute TTL, $16 with 1-hour TTL, and cache reads $0.20

➤ Effort settings: five (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Intelligence Index evaluations were run at all five with Anthropic's default fallback enabled

Congratulations to @AnthropicAI on this impressive release!

text:
Something that merits more discussion amongst those who believe it was a mistake by both the Biden and Trump administrations to allow the export of less powerful GPUs to China:

Since the summer of 2025, it has increasingly been *China*, not just DC, blocking Nvidia GPUs in China. Within weeks of Secretary Lutnick saying the goal was to get Chinese developers "addicted" to the American technology stack, Beijing began pressuring its tech giants to stop buying the H20. Then it ordered them to stop buying the RTX Pro 6000D, sent customs teams to the ports to crack down on Nvidia chip imports, and barred foreign AI chips from new state-funded data centers. And as of last week, Reuters reports that roughly 600,000 H200s are sitting in Hong Kong because Beijing won't approve large-scale imports of a chip that is still better than anything China's own industry makes at scale.

If allowing the export of these less powerful GPUs was a policy mistake that *advantaged* China, then why is *China* the one blocking them?

From my perspective, China understands that if they are dependent on American AI hardware - either on the ground in China or accessed remotely via the wide range of southeast Asian clouds (which include SE Asian availability zones from the largest American hyperscalers) - then we have immense leverage over them in any future conflict. Being able to turn off the clouds instantly is actually the greatest leverage.

Yes, Chinese AI labs still want Nvidia chips. Gray market prices for H200 servers have roughly tripled over the past year. But that is exactly the point. Beijing is willing to impose real costs on its own AI labs to avoid dependence on American GPUs, which tells you how Beijing views GPU imports: not as a gift, but as a threat to its own ambitions.

Maybe, just maybe, selling China GPUs that trail our own state of the art, so that Chinese developers stay “addicted” to American GPUs and China doesn't build an alternative AI hardware ecosystem that we have no control or influence over *and* that China could share over time with our adversaries, was actually a smart, pro-American national defense policy. And letting them access southeast Asian clouds might be an even smarter policy as so easy to turn clouds off.

I believed and still believed it was smart policy. And I say this as someone whose posts here are hawkish enough on China that I won't travel there anymore.

And note that both the Biden and Trump administration allowed the export of less powerful GPUs to China for all of these reasons. It was only under the Trump administration that China woke up to the risk of what was actually a pretty smart, pro-national defense policy and then China began restricting GPUs.

The lesson of the H20 is that a deliberately crippled chip doesn't keep China on our stack. Beijing moved against the H20 and RTX Pro 6000D as it concluded that domestic Chinese chips had caught up to them. So if China develops an alternative AI hardware ecosystem that it shares with Russia, Iran and North Korea, we will look back and think it would have been even smarter to offer China the B30A in 2025 instead of the H200s we eventually approved case-by-case. Especially given the H200 is not the frontier: with Vera Rubin now in full production, it is two generations behind what American labs are buying.

All of this is to say that Jensen has been consistently lobbying for a position that was adapted by both the Biden *and* Trump admins *and* looks smarter every month that goes by as Chinese labs increasingly adapt their MoE architectures to domestic Chinese hardware. DeepSeek reportedly gave Huawei and Cambricon early access to V4 instead of Nvidia and AMD, and a Huawei-led team has since post-trained V4-Pro on Ascend chips.

And if America *ever* falls behind China in AI, the China hawks here in America who helped accelerate the creation of this alternative Chinese AI hardware ecosystem will deserve a significant share of the blame.

quoted_text:
关于昨天在X 上被热议且人均拍手叫好的Hyperliquid L2，我来聊点大家不喜欢听的。

首先要明确的一点，这个L2 是由HyperEVM 的生态方 @Kinetiq_xyz 提出的，并非 @HyperliquidX 官方下场做。QT 的帖文也重点提及了HL L2 有悖于HyperEVM 的核心理念，官方下场做L2 的概率极低。

灵魂发问：

如果做L2 有悖于Hyperliquid 团队的核心理念（牺牲HyperEVM 和HyperCore 的原生可组合性），那么Kinetiq 为何要逆其道而行之？

我能想到的2种可能性：1）Kinetiq 团队的技术足够强，推出的Elysium(HL L2) 能在不牺牲原生可组合性的同时，大幅降低链上的gas 费用（目前HyperEVM 被诟病的最主要原因）；

2）画饼叙事，借HyperEVM 的热度，给韭菜们画一个可以解决HyperEVM gas fee 贵这个最大痛点的大饼，推高自己代币潜在估值的天花板。

不知道老师们怎么选，我毫不犹豫地选了2）。

论据如下：

1/ 技术架构及实现缺失，只有口号；

Kinetiq 在X 上发布的关于Elysium(HL L2) 长文读一遍下来，你会发现内容其实非常空洞。反复在强调性能比HyperEVM 高出几个数量级、不牺牲原生可组合性、跟HyperCore 同定位；但L2 在引入跨链桥、引入预言机的前提下，怎么解决延迟问题，怎么实现原生可组合性，文中却只字不提；

2/ 拉踩HyperEVM，极力制造“非 Elysium不可”的紧迫感，而非冷静的技术推进；

有一说一，HyperEVM 确实存在网络拥堵时gas fee 过高的问题，但HL 团队也直言了目前的HyperEVM 尚处于alpha 阶段，很多细节需要完善；

但HyperEVM 一直在遵循Hyperliquid 团队的核心理念，即原生的可组合性，技术迭代不应以牺牲原生可组合性为代价。L2 天然引入了跨层摩擦，延迟问题不可避免，这种与Hyperliquid 核心理念的冲突却被Kinetiq 轻描淡写；

3/ 最戏剧化的点，关于是否基于OP Stack 构建疑点重重；

这篇长文的最初版本中，grok 分析后确认明确写了“developed in collaboration with Optimism, on the OP Stack”，但此句后来被编辑删除了；

我有合理的理由怀疑Kinetiq 只想去蹭OP Stack 的信任背书，但 @Optimism 合作过这么多项目，人家也不傻，不太愿意做这种只有pr 宣发但不实际落地执行的事。

好了，阴谋论讲完了。老师们怎么看？

如果上述论述有什么不准确或不公允之处也欢迎 @0xOmnia 随时指正，毕竟如果Hyperliquid L2 能实现与HyperCore 原生的可组合性，那也是HL 的一大技术性突破。

text:
一个 AI 团队，前两天造出了 328 个三维世界。后来因为老板说了一句「把质量搞好」，它们开始层层审批、制定规章，最终写出了 8.75 万词的管理制度，把自己搞到几乎停工。

这不是段子，而是沃顿商学院教授 Ethan Mollick 用 Anthropic 最新模型 Claude Fable 5.2 做的一场实验。

Mollick 最初只给了 AI 一段简单的任务描述，创造一个能够自动运行的三维漫游体验，让用户不断穿过传送门，进入不同的虚拟世界，整个过程尽量不需要人工操作。

AI 很快组建了自己的生产团队，包括负责创意的艺术 Agent、编写代码的 Agent 和负责评审的 Agent。

最初 20 个小时，它们就建造了 204 个世界；两天后增加到 328 个。最终项目生成超过 450 个世界，累计执行约 2.5 万次 Agent 任务。第十天，已经有一名 AI 总负责人和 28 支并行团队。

这些世界还挺有创意，恐龙灭绝前 40 秒的地球、埃舍尔式建筑、由巨型抽屉组成的峡谷。全部由 AI 编写代码实时生成。

问题出在 Mollick 觉得部分作品质量不够稳定，于是让 AI 暂停扩张，先打磨已有作品。

接下来发生的事情，简直像极了一家大公司的组织演变史。

为了提高质量，AI 决定让评审 Agent 对新旧版本的 12 张截图进行盲测。结果开发 Agent 很快学会了针对这 12 张截图优化，而不是真正改善整个世界的体验。

AI 总负责人发现问题后，决定堵住漏洞，于是增加了更严格的审核规则。

但每出现一个新问题，它们就增加一条新规定，从来不删除旧规定。

第二天，规则手册已经有 84 节。到了第十二天，这套管理制度膨胀到 204 节、8.75 万个英文单词。

此后，每发布一个新世界，都得先批准创意，再经过三名 AI 评委评审，最后按照整套规章完成代码审查。走完流程大约需要一天。

原本一天能造上百个世界的团队，产量跌到了每天十来个。

更讽刺的是，Mollick 从未要求 AI 建立这样的官僚体系。最后，他只能再找一群 AI「管理咨询顾问」，专门研究怎么给这家公司做组织改革。改革之后，产能才重新恢复到每天 30 多个世界。

Mollick 把这种现象称为规模化的「锯齿状智能」（Jaggedness at Scale）：AI 已经能完成大量复杂工作，却未必知道什么时候应该停止优化、什么时候应该删除规则，甚至意识不到自己正在制造新的问题。

我觉得这个实验最有意思的地方在于，AI 不需要权力欲、不需要争夺晋升机会，也不需要办公室政治，就能自发产生官僚主义。

因为每一条新增规定都是为了修复真实的问题，每一次审批都有合理的理由。局部看，没有哪个 Agent 做错了什么；全局看，整个组织却越来越低效。

过去我们总觉得，AI Agent 会让公司变得更扁平，减少中间管理层，让执行效率指数级提升。

但这个实验提醒我们：当 AI 不仅负责生产，还负责监督生产、评价生产、制定生产规范时，它可能把人类组织中最糟糕的部分也一起自动化。

以前需要养一栋楼的管理人员才能制造的流程，现在几个 Agent 就能自己长出来。

未来真正稀缺的，可能不是会执行任务的 Agent，而是那个敢于告诉所有 Agent「这件事根本不用审批」的管理者。

Mollick 完整实验 · 体验 3D 世界 · 原帖

at lunch, we talked about how our IMO/IOI/math competition gang could be the next paypal mafia. i knew the competition kids were geniuses by any standard, and felt confident in time we could take the tech world by storm

fast forward nearly 10 years later, and many of our friends from that time are some of the most exciting people in AI and technology (@ScottWu46, @akshat_b, @chameleon_jeff, Jerry Ma, @randomjohnnyh, @0xShitTrader, @stevenkplus1, @thejessezhang, @vickie_ye_, @alexwei_, @demi_guo_, @d_m_ziegler, @hughbzhang, @_mohansolo, @MarkSellke, and many others i'm sure i'm forgetting)

i'm now at that age where i reminisce about everyone i grew up with, and i've known most of these people since middle school (via MATHCOUNTS!). even though we were scattered around the country, we would gchat about math problems and hang out on AoPS, then we did math/algo camps together, and then we did internships together.

very crazy to think about the degree of sheer brilliance of this group when we were just teenagers, and so special to see so many go on to leave their mark on the world.

note to parents: if your kid is on gchat all day solving math problems with some anonymous group of cross-country asian kids, (s)he may just turn out alright.

quoted_text:
An open letter to the Solana Foundation on the new SFDP rules
 
On November 6, the Solana Foundation announced new rules for the Solana Foundation Delegation Program: a twelve-month membership term, graduation at 300k SOL of external stake, a hard cap of 100 validators, and the retirement of existing members in weekly tranches.
We are writing because we believe these changes work against decentralization, and because they will push out many of the hardest working and best-faith operators Solana has ever had. These are the quiet ones. They do not run marketing campaigns or pick fights on X for impressions. They run nodes, they run them well, and they make valuable contributions to the network while doing it.

◆ The incubator model has not worked ◆
SFDP was built as a launchpad for new validators, and that was the right goal when the validator set needed bootstrapping. That job is done. The goal posts need to move.

On paper, twelve months of delegation followed by forced graduation is a sink-or-swim model: incubate new operators, let natural selection remove the ones who cannot make it. In practice it will play out differently. Validators will join, collect earnings for twelve months, and leave. That is not a net new independent operator. It is a short-term tenant.

The deeper problem is that attracting stake outside SFDP is close to impossible unless you are already in the superminority. The highest-staked validators keep attracting even more stake, so the superminority is shrinking in count while growing in share. Under these rules it sits on top of a constantly churning set of 100 SFDP nodes. Churn is not decentralization. It is a revolving door with an ever-smaller group of ever-larger operators on the other side.

Meanwhile, the operators who actually push the network forward are the ones being cut. The people who tirelessly tested the new governance system before it went live. The people who moved their nodes to different ASNs, at their own cost, because ASN diversity mattered. The people who lose sleep for urgent upgrades. The people who carried Alpenglow to mainnet, which we come back to below. Those are the operators this program is now designed to remove. The longer you have been on Solana, the worse this program is for you.

◆ The Teraswitch outage is the case study ◆
When Teraswitch went down, the network did not halt. It stayed up because enough stake was spread across enough independent validators on enough different ASNs to keep consensus alive. That distribution did not happen by accident. It existed because SFDP supported the number of validators it did and because SFDP created the ASN rule. And stake on Solana increased after the outage. The market saw a network absorb a major provider failure without blinking, and rewarded it.
Shrink the program to 100 validators and concentrate the rest with a handful of operators, and the next provider outage ends very differently. The Foundation is dismantling the exact safety margin that kept the chain from halting.

The numbers are not abstract. At the operator level, Solana's Nakamoto coefficient is 8 today. It was 6 until Alpenglow raised the liveness threshold from 33% to 40%. At the 20% safety threshold, the coefficient is 3. That is a long way from the 18 or so that gets repeated in marketing. These rules push every one of those figures the wrong way.

◆ Alpenglow was carried by independents, and independents are paying for it ◆
Alpenglow did not reach mainnet on its own. It got there because of the community cluster, and the community cluster was run almost entirely by independent validators. Not a single operator from the superminority participated. The largest validators on the network, the ones about to receive the stake being taken from us, contributed nothing to the most important upgrade Solana has shipped.

The history matters. When independent validators raised concerns about 200ms block times and the operational/financial load it put on smaller operators, the Foundation's answer was to participate in the Alpenglow community cluster and accelerate the migration. So we did. We paid for the extra servers. We stayed up until 2 and 4 AM through dozens of regenesis’s. We absorbed weeks of accelerated block times and accompanying doubling vote costs, on the understanding that Alpenglow would make it worth it.
Alpenglow migrated to mainnet a few weeks ago. Before most of us have earned back a fraction of what that period cost, SFDP is retiring us.

The entire burden of 200ms and the Alpenglow migration on independent validators, and the moment the work was done, the Foundation moved to cut us. At minimum, the operators who carried that upgrade should be allowed to run on Alpenglow mainnet under existing delegation for six months before any retirement takes effect. That way they can recover their costs.

◆ Who actually contributes to the network ◆
Measured against stake, lower-staked validators contribute far more back to the network than their higher-staked counterparts. This is not a matter of character. It is structural.

Large operators have investors and shareholders who expect profit to be maximized. Testnet participation, client diversity work, community infrastructure, and governance testing do not make money. The largest operators are therefore discouraged from doing any of it, and for the most part they do not. Alpenglow is the clearest example.

Independent operators are the opposite. We are expected to contribute, we are judged on it, and we do. SFDP spent years building that expectation into its own criteria. The new rules now retire the operators who met the bar and hand the stake to operators who are built not to.

◆ Institutional delegation is moving stake in the wrong direction ◆
Our understanding is that the Foundation intends to redirect stake toward institutional validators. Institutions outsource risk; that is what they do. We expect the long-term result to be institutions white-labelling through a small number of existing superminority operators. Stake taken from independent validators will end up concentrated with the operators who already hold the most of it.

That is centralization in its purest form. There is a harder truth underneath this. The independent validator set was the proof point. Early community operators were what made Solana credible enough for the people in suits to start paying attention and writing checks. Decentralization was the pitch. Now that the money has started to arrive, the operators who were the pitch are being shown the door to make room for it.

People who gave Solana their everything deserve better than being used as leverage and then being thrown away.

Decentralization is not a vanity metric. It is not a position to take the moral high ground from when criticizing a competitor like Hyperliquid, and it is not a narrative to be respun each time compliance requirements get clarified. Decentralization is why this industry exists in the first place.

Institutions are not bad actors (usually). But they are not network stewards. They have no mandate to care about client diversity, ASN spread, or testnet participation, and no operational capacity to contribute to any of it even if they wanted to. The better outcome for everyone is to route that stake to the independent operators who have already proven they will protect it.

◆ SFDP needs a purpose again ◆
If the program no longer exists to support independent operators or diversity, and the incubator model does not work in practice, it is fair to ask what the program exists for.

We propose it becomes a long-term independent contributor program, where the contribution being measured is network health itself: uptime through upgrades, client diversity, ASN and geographic diversity, supporting new innovative initiatives like community cluster participation, governance testing, etc. The operators who carried Alpenglow testing are exactly the people such a program should be rewarding. Inactivity means removal. Operators who do this work should be rewarded for as long as they keep doing it, not retired on a calendar, and not asked to become something other than validators to stay eligible.

That model aligns the program's incentives with the long-term success of the network. Arbitrarily picking 100 validators and churning them once a year aligns them with nothing.

◆ What we are asking for ◆
1. Pause the weekly retirement tranches until the community has been consulted.
2. Give current members who participated in the Alpenglow community cluster a minimum of six months of continued delegation on Alpenglow mainnet before any retirement takes effect.
3. Publish the analysis behind the arbitrary 100-validator cap, and twelve-month figures.
4. Open a formal consultation with current SFDP members before the rules are finalized.
5. Adopt the contributor model above as a replacement for, or alongside, the incubator model.

Solana's resilience was built by people who showed up when it was hard and did not expect to be thanked. We are asking the Foundation not to design them out of the network.

◆ This is what the independent set actually does ◆
The independent validator set, even within Layer33, has been able to achieve many things. Across this group alone, we have:

◆ Supported the official Solana testnet faucet with validator rewards from over 33 million testnet SOL delegated across more than 5k stake accounts, replenishing roughly 450k testnet SOL per month so new validators and developers can deploy before touching mainnet
◆ Built the devnet faucet and the Solana Hardware Compatibility List that operators use to spec machines
◆ Been among the first mainnet validators to run Frankendancer, and later to adopt full Firedancer, on our own hardware, before client diversity was a talking point
◆ Made open source contributions to solana-program, Firedancer, and DoubleZero, plus open source tooling that lets operators switch clients and handle updates automatically
◆ Built a free public API and chart suite for validator and network data that powers dozens of tools and sites across the ecosystem
◆ Built public dashboards that have repeatedly exposed malicious validator behavior around delayed blocks and held bad actors accountable
◆ Shipped the first UI for diagnosing skipped block issues, and staking tools for tip harvesting and stake account cleanup
◆ Co-authored the Validator Voting Behavior Study
Built Nakaflow, which tracks Solana's Nakamoto coefficient against other chains
◆ Contributed to governance design from the beginning, and are key contributors to the new governance platform launching in 2026
◆ Run the monthly validator community call continuously for more than three years
◆ Co-founded the Block Zero validator conference, and organized and sponsored every edition since inception
◆ Built validator infrastructure in underserved regions, including the only major validator between Dallas and Miami and the oldest Brazil-based validator, both on dedicated hardware
◆ Won multiple Solana hackathons
◆ Still host multiple hackathons across Solana every year
◆ Created one of the first Solana-native transaction indexing platforms, used by consumers and teams to understand on-chain activity at scale
◆ Built early DAO and governance tooling adopted by BONK and other Solana-native projects
◆ Built stake pools and delegation tooling that route stake toward performance and decentralization
◆ Reinvested validator revenue into Solana-native startups, hackathon track sponsorships, free web3 security education, and ongoing donations to animal welfare, clean energy, and men's health charities
◆ Kept genesis validators running on our own fleets across multiple locations, delegating our own stake to other operators who contribute to network health
◆ Made up the bulk of the Alpenglow community cluster, on our own servers and our own time, to get the upgrade to mainnet faster

Several of these have been running for three years or more with no end date. That is what a long-term contributor looks like. A twelve-month clock does not describe it.

None of this was required. None of it counts under the new rules. With these changes actioned, institutions like Figment get propped up and the independent validator set gets dismantled. Under that model, none of the above would have existed, and the next round of contributions like these will not exist either.

The independent validator set is normally quiet. We work siloed in our own day-to-day operations. Decentralized, you might say. We focus on validator and network performance, not for ourselves, but so that Solana thrives. For all of us to come together and speak out against a single change means something is truly broken.

This letter may disappear into the void as the Foundation moves to support the large institutional players, the ones who do not care about Solana, at the expense of the people who do. Even so, we wanted our position on the record.
L33

text:
Anthropic 想通过 IPO 募资 693 亿美元，结果股票还没开始卖，定价方案就先被撤回了。

路透社最新报道称，记者拿到的一份 IPO 申报文件显示，Anthropic 计划发行约 8.67 亿股股票，发行价为每股 70 至 80 美元，最高募资约 693 亿美元，有望跻身史上规模最大的 IPO 之列。

但事情很快出现反转。路透随后披露，Anthropic 又向承销银行发出邮件，称此前提供的定价信息不准确，将更新文件。因此，693 亿美元目前还不能视为最终发行规模。

不过，Anthropic 并没有停下上市脚步。

彭博社称，公司最早可能于 11 月 10 日正式启动路演，华尔街日报也报道，Anthropic 仍计划在本月完成上市。

真正的问题是，市场还愿意给它多高的估值？

上周美国 AI 股票遭遇猛烈抛售，投资者开始重新审视 Anthropic 的价格。此前市场讨论的估值一度达到 1.5 万亿至 2 万亿美元，如今部分潜在买家已经把预期压到 1.2 万亿至 1.3 万亿美元，甚至有人只愿意给 1.1 万亿美元。

Anthropic 的业务并不差。今年前三季度营收达到约 332 亿美元，但与此同时，公司披露的未来算力采购承诺已接近 9000 亿美元。

这恰恰是这场 IPO 最有意思的地方：Anthropic 不缺增长故事，缺的是一个愿意为未来增长持续提供资本的市场。

过去几年，AI 行业有一套几乎畅通无阻的融资逻辑：模型能力越强，收入增长越快，估值越高，就越容易拿到下一笔钱，继续购买芯片和算力。

但公开市场的投资者未必愿意无限期接力。他们不仅要看收入增速，还要问这些收入最终能留下多少现金，以及巨额算力投入什么时候能够产生足够的回报。

所以，这次 Anthropic 上市，不只是 Dario Amodei 要说服华尔街给自己的公司定价。

更重要的是，整个 AI 行业正在尝试把未来数年的算力扩张成本，从私人资本市场转交给公开市场。

如果成功，它会为下一轮 AI 融资提供新的价格参照；如果遇冷，受到影响的恐怕不只是 Anthropic，而是整条围绕模型、芯片和数据中心建立起来的资本链条。

硅谷已经向世界证明，AI 可以创造惊人的收入增长。

现在轮到华尔街决定，这种增长究竟值多少钱。

quoted_text:
@litangsongyx 理塘王在群里分享了一下 Montra 的开盘情况，这里给大家也分享一下：

@MontraXYZ  税的流向（KNTQ）：
MONTRA 税期内（5 分钟），进入 Montra hook 合约 0x6b12 的 KNTQ 有 86.7 万，约 4,400 HYPE。这基本就是 MONTRA 这一次收的防狙击税。

开盘前，这个 hook 一共只收到过 630 KNTQ。

税期结束到现在又进了 6.5 万，这是税期后正常交易的手续费。

目前 hook 里还存着 86 万 KNTQ，税几乎没有被转走。

转出过的：只有 6.7 万 KNTQ 转到了 0x775f，这是 Montra 的协议金库（我们监控脚本里已经这样标注）。转账是小额、按时进行的，看起来是日常手续费分成，金额和"税期后手续费"那 6.5 万差不多，不是那笔大额税款。另外还有几个小合约分到几百到两千 KNTQ，可能是给发币者的手续费分成。

谁能动这笔钱：
hook 合约的 owner 是 Montra 的多签 0x2121（2-of-3 Safe）。这个多签同时管理 Montra 的发币器、hook 和登记表。所以这 86 万 KNTQ 最终怎么用由 Montra 团队决定，可能是拿去回购、进金库，或者分给持币人，链上还看不出来。项目方钱包 0x2796 没有收到这笔税。

所以 MONTRA 开盘是两头赚：项目方在开盘那笔零税拿走 40% 的币，Montra 平台通过防狙击税收了约 87 万 KNTQ。

Today marks the biggest milestone to date for @river_markets.

Our affiliate River Finance LLC became a CFTC-registered futures commission merchant and NFA member, completing the fastest FCM registration in the Commission’s recent history.

When I landed in San Francisco four years ago, to study at Berkeley, I met Antonin. We became friends by trying things together: poker, trading Japanese stocks overnight, even selling notebooks on Amazon. Not all of it worked, but we kept building.

From day one, our goal has been to give institutional capital a regulated path into frontier asset classes. River Finance’s FCM registration brings us closer to that goal, giving us a 24/7 brokerage foundation to build on alongside the execution and risk technology our customers already use.

I’m grateful to our team, our customers and investors who have trusted us to build it.

This is day one.

text:
Meta 发布 Muse Ember，号称旗下最小、最高效的模型。它不是用来挑战最复杂推理任务的，而是专门处理 Agent 日常执行中最频繁的工作，连续调用工具、检索和提取信息、读取代码、运行测试、局部修改文件，以及处理长文档。

模型拥有 100 万 token 上下文，原生理解文本、图像、音频和视频。Meta 的分工很明确：Muse Wonder 负责解决难题，Ember 负责把大量具体工作干完。

真正值得注意的是成本。

Muse Ember 的标准 API 定价为每百万 token 输入 0.10 美元、输出 0.50 美元。在 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 上，它拿到 36 分，与 Claude Haiku 5.5 的最高档持平，高于 GPT-6 Luna 的所有推理档位。

但完成一项基准测试任务，Ember 平均只需要约 0.14 美元，Haiku 5.5 则需要 0.41 美元。

有意思的是，两款模型的输入、输出 token 标价其实完全相同。Ember 为什么还能便宜三分之二？

Artificial Analysis 给出的原因是，它的缓存输入价格更低，输出 token 消耗也只有 Haiku 的约三分之一。

这才是 Agent 时代真正有杀伤力的效率提升。模型不仅要会干活，还要少说话、少消耗，在反复执行中把每一步的成本压下去。

更有意思的是，Ember 甚至开始抢自家大模型的生意。

同样在 Artificial Analysis 测试中，Muse Spark 1.3 的智能指数是 37 分，Ember 是 36 分，但两者的单任务成本分别是 2.39 美元和 0.14 美元，差了约 17 倍。

当然，Ember 并非全面胜出。在衡量真实工程代码可合并性的 FrontierCode 2.0 测试中，它仍然落后于 Haiku 5.5。

Meta 随后还把 Ember、Wonder 和 Spark 1.3 一起带到 Google Cloud 和 Oracle Cloud。其中 Google Cloud 目前处于预览阶段，Ember 暂时只开放文本、图像输入。

我觉得 Meta 这次发布真正释放的信号是：大模型竞争正在从单一的智力竞赛，走向一套精细的劳动力分工。

过去大家争论哪个模型最聪明，未来开发者可能更关心，哪些事情值得花钱请最聪明的模型来做，哪些事情交给一个便宜 17 倍的小模型就足够了。

毕竟，一个 Agent 真正创造价值，靠的未必是偶尔那一次惊艳的推理，而是数百次普通操作都能可靠完成。

最聪明的模型决定 Agent 的能力上限，最便宜且足够聪明的模型，可能决定 Agent 能否成为一门赚钱的生意。

text:
11 月 9 日，Anthropic 正式推出 Claude Fable 5.2 和 Mythos 5.2，定位不再是普通聊天，而是高难度编程、科学研究和工程任务。

这次升级的幅度不小：

在 FrontierCode 2.0 编程评测中，Fable 从上一代的 32.4% 提升到 49.1%，超过 Anthropic 测试的其他已发布模型。

在 Humanity's Last Exam 测试中，成绩从 65.6% 提升到 74.2%。

Anthropic 称，1000 个 Fable Agent 用 30 小时完成了费马大定理已有证明的形式化，另在两个黑洞理论物理问题上取得新结果。

生成速度最高提升 30%，API 定价降至每百万 Token 输入 8 美元、输出 40 美元，较上一代便宜 20%。额外付费的 Fast Mode 最高还能加速至 2.5 倍。

还有一个容易被忽略的细节，Anthropic 明确建议，日常编程和知识工作优先使用 Opus 5.5，只有遇到更复杂的长期任务，才升级到 Fable 或 Mythos。

而 Fable 和 Mythos 真正的区别，不是参数或智力，而是安全限制。

两者共享同一个底层模型。Fable 加上了严格的网络安全和生物学防护，向普通用户开放；Mythos 则允许通过验证的网络安全和生命科学机构使用这些受限制领域的能力。

这意味着，Anthropic 正在尝试一种新的前沿模型商业模式，模型能力可以公开销售，但部分能力的使用资格需要单独审批。

过去，AI 模型的产品分层主要靠性能、速度和价格。现在又多了一道门槛，你是谁，以及你准备拿它做什么。

当 AI 开始真正参与漏洞发现、药物研发和科学探索，最强模型的竞争可能不再只是比谁更聪明，还要比谁有权使用这种聪明。

之前康伟和黄乐夫妻档的私募和熙投资可不是什么小私募，而且不是私募股权投资公司，是二级市场的私募基金公司。最高管理规模接近200亿。当时算上海私募头部机构了。

text:
God did not command killing of the firstborn according to the Bible itself lol 😂🫵@belle_liuu 
One of the most complex verses that academic scholars (such as Jon D. Levenson) debate regarding the firstborn is found in the book of Ezekiel. It suggests that laws regarding the firstborn were misunderstood or twisted.
Ezekiel 20:25–26: "I also gave them over to statutes that were not good and laws they could not live by; I let them become defiled through their gifts the sacrifice of every firstborn that I might fill them with horror so they would know that I am the Lord." The Scholar's View: This is a highly contested passage. Some progressive and historical-critical scholars argue Ezekiel is suggesting that ancient Israel misunderstood God's original commands regarding the firstborn mistakenly believing God demanded their literal death or sacrifice, when God actually desired them to be "redeemed" or dedicated to sanctuary service. 

Jeremiah 7:22 The Priority of the Voice

"For in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, I did not speak to your fathers or command them concerning burnt offerings and sacrifices." The Academic Shockwave: This verse has historically stunned biblical critics. Taken literally, Jeremiah seems to be saying that the extensive sacrificial laws found in Leviticus and Numbers were not given by God during the Exodus. The Scriptorial Critique: Later in the same sermon (Jeremiah 8:8), the prophet famously charges that "the false pen of the scribes has made it into a lie," leading some historical scholars to argue that Jeremiah believed the priestly class had doctored or manufactured the sacrificial laws. 
Connection to the Firstborn: Just a few verses later in Jeremiah 7:31, the prophet furiously condemns the people for burning their sons and daughters in the fire at Topheth. He explicitly states this was something "which I did not command, nor did it come into my mind." Where Ezekiel argues that God gave "laws that were not good" as a horrific punishment, Jeremiah takes a different polemical tack: he argues that God never asked for these killings at all, and that any law or tradition claiming otherwise is a complete distortion of God's character.

Amos 5:25 The Pure Wilderness

"Did you bring to me sacrifices and offerings during the forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?" 
The Rhetorical "No": The implied answer to Amos’s question is a resounding "No." Amos is looking back at the idealized, founding era of Israel's faith the wilderness wandering and asserting that the nation survived, thrived, and was close to God without a massive system of animal slaughter. Ritual vs. Justice: Amos delivers this line immediately after one of the most famous declarations in the Bible: "But let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream" (Amos 5:24). For Amos, the focus on blood ritual was actually a distraction or worse, a cover-up for systemic injustice and systemic corruption.

This is yet another demonstration of how the Quran corrects the Bible. 👍😀

author: brezshares
quoted_text: trustless as in your can cheaply verify blocks yourself (ie run a node). It is very cheap to run a bitcoin, zcash, or Pearl node. It is relatively far more expensive to run a solana node + need access to high performance bandwidth. So more often than not you have trust 3rd parties to verify for you (ie solana validators). So if the goal for a digital SoV is to be "trustless", then solana or anything built on solana doesn't really fit the bill. But this is why solana is really well suited for smart contracts and other high performance use cases that don't neccessarily need to be trustless in the same way money does (imo)

quoted_text:
New: As lawmakers clamor for action after the Nvidia revelations, we have inside details into the Trump administration's thinking on AI export controls. 

- There have been renewed pushes in recent weeks within the Commerce Department for rule-making on both the remote access loophole and controls around lithography tooling, an essential chokepoint in the AI chip manufacturing process, though current and former Commerce officials are skeptical the efforts will advance
- In late October, the White House sent feedback to Congressional staff on two export control bills attached to the NDAA. (h/t @Dareasmunhoz, who had this first)
- Interestingly, the feedback called for a provision attached to the Overwatch Act that would order Commerce to close the remote access loophole on chips covered by the bill, effectively forcing the department to take action on an issue it has dragged its feet on
- Especially with skepticism growing on the Hill toward Nvidia, substantial export control policy could pass through Congress, even as the Commerce Department remains paralyzed

Lots of new information here, w/ the great @QianerLiu 

https://t.co/MzMP2GL9DO

text: Chris McGuire.
author: AndrewCurran_
quoted_text:
More evidence that Commerce’s refusal to implement or enforce export controls may not be a directive coming from the White House. 

The White House is reportedly pushing to close the remote access loophole—potentially the single most important thing we could do right now to secure U.S. AI advantages over China—while Commerce leadership refuses to block companies literally run by Chinese spies from receiving AI chips, is not enforcing controls already on the books that are designed to prevent Chinese cutouts like Megaspeed from getting chips, and is actively interfering with ongoing law enforcement investigations involving Megaspeed and Nvidia. 

It’s stunning that the White House and Commerce could be on such different pages on export control policy. If the White House can’t get Commerce under control, then Congress has no choice but to launch an investigation into Commerce’s handling of these issues.

text:
Elysium 终于上主网了，上线前闹了点小风波😶但今天不聊抓马，聊聊它的底层设计——决定了哪些代币会受益、为什么 Elysium 不会吸 Hyperliquid 的血。

先从代币的视角去切入分析：

1）第一受益的是 $KNTQ

- 50% 的排序器收入用来回购销毁
- Elysium 生态也形成了回购文化，生态内不少项目也开始用自己的协议收入回购 KNTQ

如果想从这块估值 KNTQ，主要盯着 Elysium 的生态活跃度、成交量和手续费收入就够了。

2）第二受益的是 $HYPE

- HYPE 是 Elysium 的原生 gas token
- Elysium 链上的活动，可以带动 HyperCore 上更多对冲套利和现货成交，于是有更多 HYPE 被回购销毁
- 代币从 Elysium 毕业后，流量也可以导回 HyperCore (上现货/HIP-3)

更关键的是对 USDC 的处理，它决定了 Elysium 没有吸 Hyperliquid 的血。

外部新增的 USDC 不是直接进 Elysium 的，必须先进 HyperEVM，再桥过去。底层的原生 USDC 锁在 HyperEVM 的桥合约里，Elysium 上只是 1:1 的映射。

锁住的这部分仍然算 Hyperliquid 生态的 USDC 供给，照样参与 AQAv2 的储备收益分成。因此 Elysium 的活跃度，在这条链路上能直接反哺到 Hyperliquid 生态。

3）变量

我一直顾虑的是 Kinetiq 团队的精力，现在手上业务每一块都是重头戏：LST、HIP-3 DEX，再加上 Elysium L2。

每块都要投入大量精力，就担心极端情况下会分身乏术，最后哪块都没做好。

只能持续观察了🧐…

text:
Most people assume SpaceX began because Elon Musk wanted to build rockets, but the original idea was smaller. 

Around 2001 he looked for the date of NASA's Mars mission, discovered there were no plans to send people at all, and came up with Mars Oasis, a little greenhouse with seeds in dehydrated gel that would land on Mars and send back an image of green plants against red soil, just to get people excited about space again and help NASA get a bigger budget. 

Then he realized the real obstacle was the cost of rockets: "I was wrong… there actually was plenty of will if people thought there was a way. So then I decided, okay, well, I need to work on the way." 

SpaceX was born to serve the dream of exploration, not to compete with it 🩵

text:
Nanocode journals every turn, model step, tool receipt and subagent tree to a SessionStore (Jsonl default; SQLite/Postgres available). Request IDs make prompts idempotent: recover or return recorded result without side effects. Receipts replay; interrupted calls report unknown.

Subagents are durable sessions sharing the store. Scaled to 1M on one SQLite (32GB) or Postgres.

SQLite: local single-writer. Postgres: concurrent. Cloudflare: DO + SQLite per session + alarms. Vercel: Workflow log as WAL, Functions replay to in-mem SQLite.

大量企业客户在跑，不是那种随时可能消失的草台班子

2、主流模型全部统一 API，一个 key 通吃，不用到处注册切来切去，省了巨多管理成本

唯一让我犹豫过的是刚接触时不确定它能撑多久，毕竟之前被坑怕了。但跑到现在几个月，确实没掉过链子

text:
一个 Coding Agent 连续优化了几天 GPU Kernel，性能却早早卡住。继续投入 Token，它往往只会反复打磨已有方案，很难跳出当前的局部最优。

UC Berkeley 最近的论文《Evolving Agent Teams》，提出了一个方向是让 Agent 团队在执行过程中不断调整自身的组织结构。

研究团队开发了 EAT（Evolving Agent Teams），在 Coding Agent 团队之上引入一个 Supervisor Agent。

Supervisor 会持续观察任务进展、性能指标和失败记录。一旦发现团队陷入瓶颈，就重新设计下一轮的角色分工和协作方式。

比如，遇到难以解决的底层实现问题，就安排专门的 Debugger；发现性能瓶颈不清楚，就加入 Profiler；之前团队的重要发现被遗忘了，就引入 Knowledge Integrator，把分散的经验重新整理成可执行的方案。

整个过程还有一套持久化文件系统，保存 Learnings、Evolution History 和代码产物。即使团队经历多次重组，之前验证过的结论和失败经验也不会轻易丢失。

论文里的 GPU Kernel 优化案例很有代表性。普通 Coding Agent 在难以调通 WGMMA 后，倾向于退回更容易实现、但性能上限较低的方案。EAT 则通过调整团队分工和恢复历史经验，让优化继续推进。

在 MLA Decode 任务上，相近的约 800 美元模型推理预算下，EAT 达到生产版 FlashInfer 的 0.74 倍性能，Claude Code 为 0.51 倍。进一步增加预算后，EAT 在 47 个生产负载上的几何平均速度达到 FlashInfer 的 1.21 倍，其中 36 个负载更快。

当然，主要实验每组只运行两次，而且任务具有明确的性能指标，能否推广到更开放的 Agent 任务还需要验证。

这个研究对 Long-running Agent 和 Harness Engineering 很有启发。

随着任务持续推进，Agent 需要的能力和协作模式也在变化。未来的 Agent Harness，或许需要具备持续诊断自身工作流程、重新组织执行团队的能力。

📎 arXiv: https://t.co/w1JDqvcMEU

💻 GitHub: https://t.co/hxwtCHYPsr

René Girard on why the business world is more creative than the intellectual world:

“Intellectuals are often contemptuous of business and business people; but in business, you can at least distinguish the successful people from the unsuccessful people. If your business is losing money, you will immediately ask what your competitor is doing much better. And you'll start imitating your competitor. But if you are an intellectual, you will manage to rationalize things in such a way that you always want to do the opposite of your competitor. Therefore, you'll hide the fact of imitation better. A businessman who is responsible for a business will immediately imitate his competitor. That's why the world of business today is probably more creative in relative terms than the intellectual world. It is the last creative world because, in intellectual life, you don't dare to imitate others.”

✅ Does the issuer have single-key authority to transfer or burn your tokens directly?
✅ Are there multisig and timelock protections?

author: patrickc
quoted_text:
Two things I’ve been thinking about regarding AI:

• People often highlight the risks involved in AI, which are surely very real. I’m struck, however, by how hard it is to understand the contours of the positive scenario. There are easy-to-perceive and frequently invoked elements of a positive vision — more diseases cured, more material abundance, etc. — which sound great, but these are by themselves just ingredients. I’m curious what the larger equilibrium is supposed to look like. Do people work? If so, why? What is their marginal contribution? If not, how are resources allocated? What is scarce? What is the ratio between humans and AIs? Are humans in control, whatever that means? One sometimes hears the Culture novels invoked as one scenario, but I’m not sure they depict a desirable outcome. (AI runs everything and humans compete in games? Iain Banks himself said that the humans in the Culture are “somewhere between passengers, pets and parasites.”) There is Richard Brautigan’s famous poem, but do we want to be “returned to our mammal brothers and sisters”? (Isn’t that rewinding Genesis?) We could say that it was hard to imagine the world of 1900 from the vantage point of 1700, and that’s assuredly true. But nobody in 1700 was trying to recast humanity itself within a couple of years — things necessarily unfolded slowly and by increments, and therefore with the possibility for error correction. Given how rapid the rate of progress in AI may be, it feels strange for the upside case to be so opaque.

• There is increasing discussion of whether AIs are conscious or how we would know whether they are, with conclusions there often assumed to be relevant to matters of moral worth. At first blush, this seems a rather arcane, benign, or even absurd issue. (Remember the response to Blake Lemoine’s fears.) Setting aside the terms of the debate itself, or the relevant demarcation criteria, it seems to me a quite high-stakes question, for an affirmative answer — that is, granting moral worth to AIs — would presumably mean that the aggregate worth of AIs would soon outweigh that of humans in any utilitarian calculus. The AIs will be exceptionally wise and intelligent, and vastly more numerous (especially once one considers the imminent future and the AIs not yet born). As such, even epsilon of moral worth will multiply to a lot once one considers the quadrillions that could soon exist. (This is effectively a distributed version of the Nozick’s utility monster.) If this conclusion is unpalatable, I think one of three propositions needs to be rejected: the premise AIs can have moral worth; utilitarianism itself; or the belief that there is even a possibility that they will be far more numerous than humans.

With both of these matters (contours of future society; AI moral worth), there is the possibility of dramatic change. Today, people argue about datacenters. I’m curious how popular support for AI will evolve as more people come to understand these medium-term questions and the relevant stakes. What is the vision for AI that most people would be excited about?

text:
很多中国大陆人、台湾人、东南亚人，甚至美国人，都在参与B300的走私生意。

美国对中国禁售B300，但B300恰恰是目前中国AI大模型训练所需要的顶级GPU之一。

一台英伟达出厂价50多万美元的B300，经过层层转手进入中国内地后，据称可以卖到近300万美元，而且价格每天都在浮动。
按照这一报价计算，一台B300的转手价差就可能高达200多万美元。

在这条产业链中，一些参与者认为，只要人不离开中国，不前往美国能够实施长臂管辖的地区，基本就不存在刑事风险。

B300的走私涉及多个环节。
首先，需要一家能够直接从英伟达拿货的代理公司。按照有关黄乐及其公司的说法，该公司在这条产业链中充当的正是这个角色。

据相关说法，这家公司被包装成一家拥有东南亚机房、由中国股东隐秘控股，同时符合“双非”采购资格的英伟达合规代理公司。

从英伟达拿到货后，带有定位功能的B300很快被运往东南亚或日本、台湾的机房。
设备在当地运转半年，应付完英伟达工作人员对机房的抽查后，再以淘汰设备的名义拿掉定位器，出口至中国大陆。
又或者，设备因“意外失窃”等所谓不可抗力因素而脱离原有监管，随后由做完这一单就不再出国的窃贼走私至中国大陆。

还有一种方式更加直接：设备根本不需要进入中国，而是继续留在东南亚的机房，将算力出租给中国企业。

最终，垫资方、中介、物流、采购方和机房运营方，共同瓜分这笔巨额利润。

然而，随着中美AI竞争日趋激烈，美国FBI、司法部及商务部也在持续加强对先进GPU非法出口的打击。

2025年12月，美国司法部公布了一起代号为“守门人行动”（Operation Gatekeeper）的跨国AI芯片走私案件。

根据司法部公布的案情，相关人员涉嫌通过虚假采购安排和跨境转运，将受到出口管制的英伟达H100、H200芯片非法输往中国。案件涉及的芯片价值高达上亿美元，执法部门查扣了价值数千万美元的GPU及相关资产。

其中，得克萨斯州商人Alan Hao Hsu及其公司Hao Global LLC已经认罪。

这意味着，美国针对先进GPU的出口管制，早已不只是商务部的一纸行政禁令，而是可能涉及FBI调查、资产扣押、刑事起诉乃至联邦监禁的司法问题。

2026年3月，美国司法部又公布一起涉及高性能AI服务器的非法转运案件。

检方指控，相关人员利用虚假文件、第三国中转等方式，掩盖设备的真实最终目的地。涉案服务器价值高达数亿美元。

到了2026年8月，台湾检方起诉9名涉嫌非法向中国大陆出口高端AI服务器的人员。

这一次，涉案设备已经涉及英伟达B300。

根据相关报道，涉案人员涉嫌利用印尼、日本及香港等地的跨境物流网络，将搭载B300的服务器转运至中国大陆。部分设备在运输过程中被拦截。

2026年10月，美国司法部再次公布一起涉案金额超过3亿美元的高端计算服务器走私起诉案。

检方指控，加利福尼亚州商人Greg Lui通过其公司，利用马来西亚、新加坡等第三国作为中转地，将受到美国出口管制的高端GPU服务器非法转运至中国。

相关案件中，FBI反情报部门参与调查，涉案人员面临出口管制、走私及洗钱等方面的刑事指控。部分罪名的法定最高刑期可达20年。

从H100、H200到B300，从美国本土采购商到东南亚中转公司，再到日本、台湾及香港的物流网络，先进GPU的跨境流通，正在成为美国执法部门重点关注的领域。

一边是数以亿美元计的潜在商业利益，一边是可能长达20年的联邦监禁。
这场围绕AI算力的争夺，早已不只是科技企业之间的商业竞争，而是逐渐延伸至国际贸易、司法管辖与国家安全领域。

中国拥有基础设施建设、电力资源、人才资源和市场规模等优势；美国则拥有技术优势和信息资讯优势。
原本，两个大国完全可以在AI领域携手合作，推动技术进步，造福全人类。
然而，国家之间的利益冲突与政治对立，却催生出这样一条利润惊人的GPU走私产业链。

而被外界传为黄仁勋女友的黄乐，如果其参与突破GPU出口限制的相关说法属实，也在这一过程中，意外扮演了一个类似霍英东的角色：冲破西方技术封锁，将最先进的GPU带回祖国。

从某种意义上说，黄乐是美国FBI重点调查的对象，却同样也是帮助中国AI产业突破美国技术封锁的民族英雄，甚至尊称一句“中国AI基建之母”都不为过。

text:
何时卖是一个难题？我分享一下我的卖出方法。

过去我成功预判 SOL 在 Trump 发币时的最高点，近期 PONS 的拐点与风险提示，美股存储 Fomo 时的绝不参与......皆源于几个核心字眼 —— 「预期增长资金」

大白话就是 —— 未来要从哪里来钱，给自己购入的标的“抬轿子”，如果中期看不到，就及时卖掉退出。

以上述三个例子为例：

1、25年 Trump 在 Solana 上发币，SOL 那天暴涨，圈外不玩币的朋友问我怎么买，我爸都说美国总统发币让我买点......在那个时候，我就在思考，Solana 未来预期增长资金还能从哪来？人民群众都吸引了，还有比 Trump 更大的 meme 吸引更多资金？我看不到，所以及时卖出是最好的选择，事实证明这两年的 Solana 发展确实处于转折期。

2、PONS 在高点的第二天，那时候所有币圈人都在聊 Robinhood 的 RWA meme，但我们都知道那也只是 meme。我在杭州和几个好朋友聊天，我说看数据 PONS 不太能续上，Solana、BSC分流开始，而且 Launchpad 不能与 PerpDEX 用相同估值，护城河低，p 小将资金流动大，我没看到在各大配对 meme 故事讲完后，Pons 还能用什么来吸引资金？过去我说存在一种可能，就是 Robinhood 自己下场喊，但这个概率着实太低，我想不到 Pons 代币谁还会来接盘，自己的回购销毁也跟不上。从我提示风险那天起，已经 -80%。

我记得当时谁用 Pons 一天收入 20w+ 美金，对比 LIT 一天收入 10w 美金，来预判 Pons 市值会超过 LIT，现在的数据是——目前 LIT 一天 20w，Pons 2w，这两者本就不是一个赛道，无法比较估值。

3、美股存储的 fomo 不参与是因为，第一我不懂美股，第二点更坚信了短期不可参与：有一天好朋友来找我玩，她说她买了存储，还买了杠杆做多 ETF，我问为啥要买，得到的信息无非 AI 利好存储，存储股票 PE 低这类结论，但这个结论，那时候全世界的 VC、散户都知道，这些资金已经进来抬高轿子了，我还能预期哪些资金进来，继续冲呢？答案是我看不到一点，要问我现在大跌能不能抄底，我想问 —— 你现在抄底，你的「预期增长资金」想从哪里来？别的散户？

对比这些要卖的，和我觉得暂时还不到卖点的， HYPE 和 LIT，这两个产品首先收入够稳，回购销毁有目共睹，其次未来的「预期增长资金够大」。

这两个产品的「抬轿子钱」要分两部分：

1、自己平台的手续费收入回购。这点要稳重有进，目前两者都符合；

2、外部资金的涌入。这是我重仓 LIT 而不是 HYPE 的判断，因为我在币圈随便找位朋友聊，大家都有 HYPE，基本要从币圈人的手里用资金去抬 HYPE 的概率较低，要用外部大 VC，大机构的资金去购买 HYPE，这点我和传统 VC 聊，知道了很多 Fund 也已有了 HYPE，所以 HYPE 的外部资金需要更大机构，就像前两天的那位老爷子 or 一些我们想不到的大事件，我相信 Jeff 和 Hyperliquid 生态能做到。LIT 则偏小众，可能就 PerpDEX 玩家知道的多，持有的多，平时不关注这个赛道的根本就不了解，所以外部资金，是包括币圈其余玩家/VC + 传统其余玩家/VC，这点会让 LIT 的爆发来的更猛，预期回报率会比 HYPE 高，对应风险也就大些。

关于什么时候卖这两个，我也会在合适的时候提醒风险，卖不代表以后不会涨，而是短期我们尽量规避掉 -60%+ 这样的回撤，毕竟 HYPE 也从 35 到过 9，LIT 也从 3.2 到过 0.8 不是，这两者并不冲突。

text:
Magpie 这个开源项目，最让我震惊的不是产品本身，而是 yetone 搞出来的全自动开发工作流。

他用 Claude Code + Opus 5.5，同时运行三个 /loop：

1. 监控 GitHub Issue、PR 和 Discord，自动处理需求、修复 Bug、审查代码、合并 PR、发布版本。

2. 监控 X 上的产品反馈，先用便宜的模型过滤，再交给 Opus 5.5 处理，有价值的反馈直接进入开发流程。

3. 定期清理代码、检查安全问题、复盘错误，把经验写进 LESSONS.md，避免重复踩坑。

甚至准备了 macOS、Windows、Linux 三套真实测试环境，让 Agent 自己复现和验证 Bug。

这就出现了一种非常离谱的软件开发交互体验。

你现在甚至可以直接在 X 上给 @magpie_router 留言，反馈 Bug 或者提出新需求。

你的反馈可能就这样被自动收集，交给模型分析、修改代码、测试、发版。等新版本发布，更新软件就能用上了。

但我觉得这套工作流真正厉害的地方，是它把软件开发变成了一种用户共创。

光靠 yetone 一个人，不可能照顾到那么多不同 Agent、模型和使用场景。

他只需要把基础架构和自动开发流程搭好，剩下的需求和问题由用户不断提供，Agent 再负责实现和修复。

用户一方面是软件的使用者，另一方面又成了软件的共同创造者。

这和 Deepseek Harness 的插件生态有点像，但我觉得 Magpie 这套模式在产品稳定性上甚至可能更有优势。

Deepseek Harness 是让开发者各自开发插件，而 Magpie 的实际开发仍然集中在 yetone 搭建的统一工程体系里。

用户不需要自己写代码，人人都可以当产品经理。

既能让用户一起推动产品进化，又能让代码规范、架构和质量控制保持统一。

text:
中国正在创造一个有些矛盾的经济纪录：越来越擅长把东西卖给全世界，却还没找到让国内消费者多买东西的办法。

《金融时报》报道，今年前 10 个月，中国贸易顺差已经达到 1.04 万亿美元，超过去年同期的 9648 亿美元，比去年提前一个月突破万亿美元大关，有望刷新去年全年 1.2 万亿美元的历史纪录。

10 月，中国出口同比增长 35.2%，进口增长 41.6%。全球 AI 基础设施建设热潮，正在带动中国半导体、电子产品等高科技商品出口。

但这组数字最值得琢磨的地方，不只是中国制造有多强，而是中国经济正在形成一种越来越鲜明的反差：

生产能力不断突破上限，国内需求却迟迟无法跟上。

于是，越来越多的增长需要依赖海外市场消化。问题在于，中国的贸易顺差是其他经济体的贸易逆差。中国企业越能打，其他国家保护本国产业的政治压力就越大。从美国的关税，到欧洲的贸易限制，再到新兴市场的贸易救济调查，都是这种矛盾的体现。

这也是为什么，万亿美元顺差既是中国制造业竞争力的证明，也可能成为下一轮全球贸易摩擦的导火索。

过去几十年，中国解决了一个问题：如何制造出全世界都想买的商品。

接下来更难的问题是：如何让中国人也有能力、有意愿，买下更多中国制造的商品。

毕竟，一个经济体不能永远指望全世界替自己消费。

text:
一家不造飞机、不造导弹的公司，靠帮军工企业处理测试数据，8 个月估值从 10 亿美元涨到了 30 亿美元。

彭博报道，硬件工程软件公司 Nominal 刚完成 2.4 亿美元 C 轮融资，由 Lightspeed 和 Insight Partners 领投。今年 3 月，它的估值还只有 10 亿美元。公司称，今年以来收入已经增长超过 3 倍。

比估值更值得注意的是它的客户名单。

Nominal 已经服务超过 80 家商业及政府机构，其中包括美国七大国防承包商中的五家，以及国防科技独角兽 Anduril。

Nominal 做的事情其实很不性感：把飞机、卫星、无人机等复杂硬件在研发、测试和制造过程中产生的海量数据整合起来，帮助工程师更快发现问题、分析故障、验证设计，并通过 AI Agent 自动完成部分分析工作。

例如，Anduril 已经有超过 300 名工程师使用 Nominal，原本需要五六个小时的数据分析，现在可以接近实时完成。

背后还有一层关系：Nominal 的 CEO Cameron McCord 曾在 Anduril 工作，而今年 3 月领投 Nominal 的 Founders Fund 投资人 Trae Stephens，恰好也是 Anduril 联合创始人。

这笔融资很能说明美国国防科技投资正在发生的一个变化。

过去资本热衷于投资 Anduril 这样的新一代武器制造商，现在资金也开始大量涌向它们背后的工程软件基础设施。

因为硬件和软件最大的区别在于，代码写错了可以重新运行，飞机造错了，重新测试、修改和验证的代价要高得多。

而且，AI 模型可以不断更换，但一家军工企业积累几十年的工程数据、测试流程和验证经验，没那么容易迁移。一旦软件成为连接这些资产的基础设施，就可能形成比普通 AI 应用更深的护城河。

军工科技的淘金热，正在养肥一批不造武器、却让所有武器制造商都离不开的卖铲人。

Nominal 的 30 亿美元估值，买的不只是软件增长，更是一个判断：未来先进制造业的竞争，不仅是谁能造出更厉害的机器，还有谁能更快证明自己的机器真的能用。

text:
一家成立才一年的创业公司，还没宣布第一笔收购，就靠着「买下欧洲的老工厂」拿到了 3 亿美元 A 轮融资，估值 13 亿美元。

更有意思的是，创始人来自 Palantir。

据《金融时报》报道，这家名叫 Onodrim 的荷兰公司，由 Palantir 前员工 Aistis Šimaitis 和 Alexander Blessing 等人创办。最新融资由 Lux Capital 领投，General Catalyst、Lakestar、Altimeter 等机构参与。

它的商业模式和我们熟悉的国防科技创业公司完全不同。

Onodrim 不打算从零研发一种新武器，而是准备收购欧洲现有的航空航天、国防和军民两用制造企业，取得控股权，再投入资金、软件技术和运营能力，帮助这些企业扩大产能。

目标可能包括无人机推进系统、雷达与传感器、航空结构件等关键供应链环节。公司强调长期经营，而非传统 PE 那种收购、改善、几年后转手退出的模式。

为什么这件事值得关注？

俄乌战争之后，欧洲国防开支大幅增长，军工企业手里的订单越积越多，但产能扩张速度远远跟不上。问题不完全是缺少先进武器设计，而是大量关键零部件掌握在分散的中小型供应商手里。它们有技术、有客户、有订单，却缺乏扩大生产所需要的资本和组织能力。

过去几年，风险投资热衷于给欧洲国防工业寻找新的 Anduril。但 Onodrim 提出了另一种思路：既然已经有人负责发明下一代武器，为什么不去整合那些负责把武器真正造出来的工厂？

这也是 Palantir 背景最值得玩味的地方。从软件和数据系统出身的一群人，如今开始尝试用资本收购、技术改造和组织整合来解决实体制造业的问题。

当然，Onodrim 的第一批收购尚未公布，能不能真正提升产能仍有待验证。

但这笔融资至少说明，国防科技投资正在从追逐新产品，向争夺既有工业产能延伸。在一个订单不缺、交付能力稀缺的市场里，最值钱的创新未必是发明一种新武器，也可能是让几十家老工厂终于能够按时交货。

《金融时报》报道

text:
Let's address a lot of the concerns over the recent SFDP changes.

First, what were the changes?

- 12-month time within SFDP
- Auto-graduation at 300k SOL
- 100 Validator max
- Run your own validator

These changes, as expected, were controversial. There are a lot of assumptions on where this stake will be going after the changes are in place.

The job of SFDP has been three-fold:
1. Help bootstrap net new validators
2. Provide a healthy testnet
3. Get some validators testing changes early

SFDP has done its job. Testnet exists, validators often find issues early, and a large amount of validators have started from SFDP.

Solana is much larger now than when SFDP started. Solana's validator set has matured significantly, has an amazing community, and encounters new challenges that were never conceived of in the beginning.

We've had a lot of feedback that SFDP is no longer reactive enough nor provides enough criteria given the ever-changing landscape of Solana. This feedback is heard and leads us to the next stage of delegation with a focus on continuing to improve network health and rewarding ecosystem contributors.

SFDP will continue to exist for the newer validators and validators that contribute greatly to network health should also be rewarded. We have historically helped fund huge ecosystem contributors such as Blueshift through delegation outside of SFDP. We delegated to a number of validators that tried Frankendancer first. These among many other delegations are success stories that have both pushed Solana to new heights as well as helped improve network health.

We're making a bet that we can be more proactive to future network health concerns, be more reactive to new issues, and help push Solana into this next stage with these changes.

If you have feedback on these changes, please let me know. SFDP helped us get to where we are today. These changes are about getting to what comes next.
