text:
Mark, look at your premise. Do we need commercial insurance carriers at all. Who is we? You are not asking whether you would buy a policy. You are asking whether a group of people with the power to legislate should permit other people to sell one. That is a different question, and it is the only question you ever ask.

The real question is whether the state has any right to tell private individuals, and companies that are nothing but private individuals acting together, how they may trade for the things their health requires. Not whether a carrier takes enough risk to satisfy you. Whether it is any of your business, or Congress's, what two consenting parties agree to.

Ask that same question of every industry and watch what the record says. The government held a monopoly on phone service for most of a century and you waited weeks for a rotary handset you were not allowed to own. It still holds one on first class mail. It licenses the utility, franchises the cable company, builds the roads, runs the schools, and keeps public libraries open in a world where the entire contents of one fit in your pocket. In every case the service froze at the moment the monopoly was granted, and in every case the one that was eventually opened to trade is now cheap and everywhere. The phone in your hand is the answer to your question.

Medicine is not different. The best healthcare system in the world was built here under the principle that a man's life, his work, and his earnings are his own, and the doctor's are his. Antibiotics, anesthesia, insulin, the polio vaccine, open heart surgery. Every one arrived as a miracle for the rich and reached the working man within a generation, because nobody with a title was deciding who needed what. Then the planners took over in 1965, asking exactly your question, do we need this, do we need that, and never the question of right. Sixty years on, real spending per person is up seven times, the government pays half the bill, and you are asking whether the next thing should be allowed to exist.

Insurance is a product. A man who wants to pool his risk with strangers at a price he accepts is engaged in a trade, and a carrier that takes too little risk for the premium will lose him to one that takes more, the moment the law stops telling him which plan he must buy and which doctor he may see. The carriers you despise are 72 percent government revenue because government made them so. You are describing a creature of the state and asking whether the state should finish it off.

It is not your call. It is not Congress's. It belongs to the man whose body and whose money are on the table, and the entire history of this country's decline in medicine is the history of men like you deciding it was theirs.

text:
一个包着"开源族谱"外壳的 pumpfun 发币前端，靠代币返佣分成和发币前的积分活动拉人。可视化做得挺巧，本质还是 memecoin 发射台。

输入一个仓库名，它画出 GitHub 上的 fork 家谱图。点任意节点，能看到对应代币，也能直接在 pumpfun 上给这个仓库发币。

它的标语是"every repository has a family tree. Some have tokens."

链是 Solana。
价格和图表数据来自 DexScreener、GeckoTerminal 和 Jupiter。

核心机制：创作者费按"血缘"分账
在这里发的币，pumpfun 创作者费的分法固定：仓库所有者 70%，贡献者前两名 5%，上游父仓库所有者 10%，祖父仓库 3%，再往上一层 2%，forks 自己的钱包 10%。

分账写在创建代币的同一个交易包里，能改分账的管理员密钥也在同一个包里作废，发币人、作者和 forks 都改不了。

作者通过 pumpfun 用 GitHub 登录就能领，不需要 forks 账号。

收入有两块：上面那 10% 的费用分成，加上站内交易和发币首买收 0.5% 手续费。
增长手段：发币前的积分盘

$FORK 还没发，现在攒的积分只是"待分配记录"，不是你持有的余额。

互动 5 项一共给 9,000 分；每邀请一人给 2,000；绑定 GitHub 给 3,000。

Season 0：发币人随币的市值增长赚 $FORK，每个币最多 100 万，奖池 2 亿。市值到 1 万美元、10 万美元等节点都有奖励。说白了是在补贴大家去发币、拉市值

值得警惕的几点
团队匿名。 没有公布 $FORK 合约地址，也没列团队或金库钱包。
积分可能缩水或作废。 Season 0 奖励随时可以宣布提前结束。积分怎么兑换成代币也完全由他们决定。
作者没同意也会被发币。 任何人都能给任何仓库发币，作者既没创建也没背书。作者可以申请拉黑，但只是从 forks 的列表里移除，已经上链的币还在。

已经有冒名币。 https://t.co/Hjquqxnosq 上已经有一个 "$FORK community"。官方自己也说 $FORK 会挂在 forkwiki/fork 仓库下，别处叫 $FORK 的都不是。

市值节点能刷。 每 10 分钟采样一次，连续两次看到就算达标。在曲线早期，拉到 1 万美元市值的成本很低。

真正新的东西是"fork 版税"：上游作者自动分到下游币的费用，而且分账锁死在链上。这在开源激励上是个有意思的实验。

但钱从哪来没变，还是 memecoin 散户的交易费。积分加邀请的玩法是典型的发币前冷启动，结局大概率跟同类项目差不多。

There is a second layer to all this that I have not seen anyone discussing.

His claim that the Rosenbergs were "lined up against the wall" is not actually true.  They were executed by electric chair, a method associated exclusively with state-sanctioned formal executions.

"The Wall", OTOH, is a concept currently having a moment with the assassination-left.  It is associated with lynching, struggle sessions, and rogue military action absent central authority or court proceedings.  Countless election-era retweets of right-wing posts titled simply "wall" are just one example.  I think the mistake (intentional?) is telling - accidentally or not, it is precisely worded for maximum amplification in the current moment by people who know exactly what is being said.

这款 西游X 不是什么币圈项目，就是我自己做的一款游戏，最开始的时候我用 Grok Bot 做一个塔防游戏做着玩的，纯粹就是为了好玩，毕竟有了十多年做游戏的底子，就做了一些有趣的设定。

游戏的本质和吸血鬼幸存者有点类似，但加入了塔防的属性，第一版的时候就是四个徒弟护送唐僧一路西行，在游戏中唐僧是不能被控制的，只能自动的一路向西走，会有大量的妖怪出现。

唐僧忠于原著没任何的战斗力，也没有武器，生命值也只有 1 ，一碰就死，所以我就想到四个徒弟作为“塔”如何保护唐僧，相当于一个逆向的塔防游戏，正常都是玩家建塔消灭路上的怪物，但我这个正好反过来。

但是跑了几篇测试觉得没什么新意，就想到应该有主动出击的环节，消灭 BOSS 可以减少怪物的数量，也能符合剧情，这种想法打开了潘多拉的盒子。

所以在游戏的设计中就有了四个徒弟可以分别操控的方案，既可以围绕在唐僧周边守护，也可以主动出击消灭怪物，还加入组合技，比如孙悟空+猪八戒一起出击的时候就能打出组合技。

比如任何角色+白龙马都可以加快移动速度，每个角色还有自己的特殊技能，比如孙悟空的筋斗云就是使用户，不论孙悟空在什么位置都可以直接瞬移到唐僧的身边。

这种玩法是有意思了，但我还是觉得缺少了什么，最重要的灵魂就是社交，我就加入了几个 X 上的小伙伴，把 X 上的小伙伴直接做到了游戏中，而且还可以自定义 X 上的角色进入到游戏里，这种玩法就有意思一些了。

最开始就加了九个特殊角色，下一个版本的时候会再加入一些，每个角色都通过 AI 计算出和发文类似的技能和属性，而且还加入了自己设计关卡的“反派模式”，我个人是觉得有意思多了。

现在还在修改一些细节，11月11日就可以公开对外测试了。

text:
Anthropic $ANT （蚂蚁）周一晚上先把 IPO 价格发给了投行：8.67 亿股新股，每股 70 到 80 美元，最多募 693 亿。随后又发了第二封邮件，说定价细节不准确，更新版以后补。

同一份文件里还有一笔：谷歌、英伟达、AMD、博通、美光、微软、台积电七家，按发行价另买 260 亿美元的私募股份。七家都在卖芯片、内存或云算力给 AI 公司，其中三家跟 Anthropic 的合同已经写进招股书，都不能取消：谷歌云至少 1145 亿美元，博通的 TPU 设备租赁 1612 亿，微软 Azure 至少 449 亿。博通 10 月底刚为那笔 630 亿美元的芯片租赁提供残值支持：芯片将来贬值，银行那一层的缺口由它来补。

上周 WSJ 说，几位准备参与 IPO 的大户嫌 1.5 万亿太贵，其中一位说估值得降到 1 万亿左右。价格还没谈拢，先有 260 亿被锁住。

我的理解是，这笔钱首先是给定价托底，供应商肯入股，对其他买家是个信号。同时钱也绕了一圈：谷歌、博通、微软出钱入股，Anthropic 照付它们的合同款，收入又回到它们账上。

text:
We are not the second best! 

在香港/新加坡住在大屋里，做全世界的投资，安全、高效的环境、丰富的商品、便利、低税率的环境，廉价的家庭佣工，华人主体的西式管理城市，一级的护照，有自由的空间和普通法保障，其实也是一种选择。

至少We are not the second best! 

华裔在美国，无论如何都会遇到“忠诚的疑问”，包括Alexandr Wang、黄仁勋等。 尤其你在重要的岗位，有重大的影响力，种族的议题总会上台面。

曾经的一位华裔美军，在一个会上，拉开上衣，满满的伤痕，是退役前的战场印记，他诉说，为什么一直要他证明热爱这个国家？其他种族的人不需要。

在纽约的梁警官，为何给不公平待遇，同一样的法规、尺度，为何落在华人身上就如此？

尤其在G2竞争，美国不少鹰派抹黑中国的情况下，这种环境不会改善。

在华盛顿州、加州可能好一点。
日子还是那样的过，那就看机遇了。 

在新/港，至少We are not the second best! 

笔记： 

1. 华裔退伍军人掀衣展示伤疤的故事
属实。2021年3月，俄亥俄州West Chester镇议员Lee Wong（华裔，服役20年美军）在镇议会会议上掀开衬衫，展示训练中留下的伤疤，质问：“这够爱国吗？”（Is this patriot enough?）。

背景是当时反亚裔仇恨上升（亚特兰大枪击案后）。他长期被质疑“不够美国”“不够爱国”。事件当时广泛报道并走红。
 
2. 纽约梁警官（Peter Liang）
属实。2014年，华裔警员Peter Liang在布鲁克林公屋黑暗楼梯间误射打死手无寸铁的Akai Gurley。他成为十多年来首位因执勤开枪被定罪的NYPD警员（过失杀人）。

华人社区大规模抗议，认为他因种族被当“替罪羊”，而同期多起白人警员类似案件常不起诉或不定罪。最终他获缓刑+社区服务，无监禁。事件确实引发了“选择性起诉”的争议。 

3. 华裔（尤其高位者）会遇到“忠诚疑问”
现象存在，但并非“无论如何都会”。
•  调查显示相当比例美国人持有“永久外国人”刻板印象，怀疑亚裔/华裔对美国的忠诚度，美中紧张时会加剧。
•  中国倡议（China Initiative）期间，不少华裔科学家遭遇调查，部分被批评为过度针对。
•  国务院等机构也曾有华裔外交官因安全审查被限制派驻中国等地的案例。

Alexandr Wang：确实是华裔（父母是洛斯阿拉莫斯实验室的中国移民物理学家）。他公开立场非常亲美，强调“美国必须赢AI战”、与国防部合作、给特朗普写信，目前没有公开重大“忠诚质疑”丑闻。但Alex多次重申他是美国人。把他和黄仁勋并列作为典型例子，有些牵强。

黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）：台湾裔美国人，Nvidia CEO。就在最近（2026年11月），他承认与一名被美国情报部门怀疑是中国间谍的中国女性Alice Huang（无血缘）有婚外情。Nvidia董事会已启动独立调查，涉及国家安全与潜在影响（芯片对华销售等）。这确实把他置于严重的安全与“忠诚”审视之下，是当前新闻热点。 

关于大环境与结论
美中战略竞争（G2）背景下，鹰派言论、媒体报道确实会放大对华裔的怀疑，尤其在科技、国防、学术等高敏感领域。这是客观存在的结构性压力，不是纯粹想象。

加州、华盛顿州相对好一点的说法有道理：亚裔人口比例高、政治环境更包容、日常歧视感知通常较低，但不是绝对安全区，高位或敏感行业仍可能有额外审查。

整体来看，这段话抓住了真实的社会现象和个人经历（退伍军人、梁警官是有据可查的典型），但用“无论如何都会”的绝对表述略强。

很多人成功且未遇到严重问题，机会与个人表现仍是主要变量。日子继续过、看机遇，这个务实态度本身没问题。

text:
OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的共同投资人 Altimeter Capital 正在筹备两只新基金。

一只规模约 25 亿美元，专门投资接近 IPO 的后期科技公司；另一只计划募集 8 亿至 9 亿美元，投资更早期、更多元化的初创企业。合计募资目标达到 33 亿至 34 亿美元，目前尚未完成募集。

Altimeter 是 Brad Gerstner 创立的投资机构，也是 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 背后的重要资本力量。它去年募集的 16 亿美元增长基金，总共只投资了 7 家公司。该基金与另一只 15 亿美元的扩张基金，曾参与包括 OpenAI、Anthropic 在内的后期融资。

当整个 VC 行业还在讨论退出困难、估值回调和募资寒冬时，掌握少数头部 AI 公司投资机会的机构，仍然有能力尝试募集数十亿美元。

过去，VC 的核心竞争力是发现下一个伟大的公司。现在，对某些顶级机构而言，另一项能力可能变得同样重要：在所有人都知道谁是伟大公司的时候，仍然能拿到它的股份。

当 OpenAI、Anthropic 这样的公司迟迟不上市，越来越多的价值创造和估值增长被留在私募市场，少数拥有投资渠道的机构，也就成为连接外部资本与这些超级独角兽的入口。

AI 正在制造一种有趣的资本分化：创业公司的融资越来越难，但能投资头部创业公司的资格，反而越来越值钱。

text:
黄仁勋卸任英伟达 CEO 的概率，正在预测市场上小幅回落。

昨天，@Polymarket 上「黄仁勋年内辞去或被免除英伟达 CEO」的概率为 16%。截至今天，这一数字已降至 14%，回落 2 个百分点。

不过，把时间窗口拉长，市场给出的概率有所上升：截至 2027 年 3 月 31 日，黄仁勋卸任概率为 22%。目前，该预测市场交易量已超过 40 万美元。

特朗普此前对 CNN 表示，英伟达宣布调查后，他还没有和黄仁勋谈过，但称黄仁勋是「一个不错的人」，「大概对此有个解释」。

需要注意的是，这个市场结算的不是黄仁勋是否在年底前实际离职，而是相关辞职或免职消息是否在 2026 年 12 月 31 日美东时间 23:59 前正式宣布。即使宣布的离任时间在 18 个月内，也符合结算条件；退休、卸任或改任公司其他职务也被纳入「辞职」范围。

从 16% 到 14%，短期市场定价有所回落，但更长周期仍存在变数。预测市场反映的是交易者对事件的押注，并不代表英伟达已启动 CEO 更替程序。

Galxe is consolidating its team and brand under Gravity to accelerate the development and adoption of Gravity L1.

Over the past five-plus years, we’ve helped pioneer Web3 questing and given projects new ways to connect with users and build communities. We’ve served 36 million users and supported more than 7,700 partner projects through campaigns, credentials, and loyalty programs, helping people discover new projects, contribute to their ecosystems, and earn recognition and rewards. We’re bringing that experience and the relationships built along the way into our work on Gravity.

As part of this consolidation, we will wind down Galxe Quest, Galxe ID, Galxe Passport, and related services. Gravity will continue operating as usual, with no changes to the G token as part of this transition.

Starting today, Spaces can no longer create new campaigns. New Galxe+ and Galxe Score subscriptions and Galxe Passport minting are also no longer available.

December 5, 2026, will be the last day to participate in campaigns. No campaigns will remain active after that date. On December 15, 2026, campaign reward claims will close, and the entire Galxe website will switch to read-only mode. Please claim any outstanding campaign rewards before December 15.

User assets remain safe, including Smart Savings balances, staked G that has not yet been withdrawn, and G tokens held in wallets on Gravity Alpha Mainnet. These assets will follow a separate claim process and timeline. We will publish the details and instructions in a follow-up announcement on our official X.

Thank you to the users, builders, and partners who helped shape Galxe. We look forward to continuing to build with you on Gravity.

text:
TLDR of hyperliquid precompiles:

EVM chains on HL (ie HyperEVM & Elysium) have precompiles (basically built in blockchain functions) that allow them to query prices of hypercore assets

For example rn on HyperEVM, you can make a simple RPC call to the chain to get the mark price of $HYPE

Elysium doesn't have this ability rn but will be able to in 4 weeks. The diff b/w elysium and hyperEVM is that elysium's prices will update every 70ms (hyperEVM is every 1s)

And elysium will be able to query entire orderbook, while hyperEVM can only do bid/ask/mark

A blockchain being able to query the full depth of a separate orderbook in real time is p cool. Maybe some volatility based univ4 hooks could use such information

text:
黄仁勋和英伟达被股东集体起诉了！

11月9日，一名英伟达股东正式向美国加州联邦法院提起拟议集体诉讼，将黄仁勋和 NVIDIA 一起列为被告，指控两者涉嫌证券欺诈，误导投资者。

这场官司盯上的不只是黄仁勋的婚外情，而是英伟达此前对外声称，与新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的业务往来属于正常客户关系，却没有充分披露黄仁勋与该公司前高管 Alice Huang 的私人关系，以及背后可能涉及的国家安全风险。

原告认为，这些信息可能影响投资者对英伟达业务前景、公司声誉和合规风险的判断。

诉状要求法院认定集体诉讼，并向受损投资者索赔，具体金额尚未确定。

起诉日期：2026年11月9日。
被告：NVIDIA 和黄仁勋。
拟议集体诉讼覆盖期间：2025年10月9日至2026年11月8日。
英伟达股价当天下跌4.3%，市值蒸发约1900亿美元。

英伟达董事会已经启动独立调查，但明确表示目前没有理由相信国家安全或英伟达机密已经遭到泄露。

现在，黄仁勋面对的已经不只是个人声誉危机，还包括证券欺诈诉讼、公司治理和国家安全调查。

一个 CEO 的私人关系，最终可能演变成英伟达数千亿美元商业帝国的治理危机。

女人+酒精+杠杆 = 成功男人的死敌！
author: oragnes
quoted_text:
卧槽，早在今年5月，做空机构 Culper Research 就把英伟达中国业务背后的供应链扒到了这个程度。（清晰完整版）

从阿里巴巴、Megaspeed、Speedmatrix，到 Aivres、YTL、Giga Computing，再到黄仁勋与 Alice Huang（黄乐）的关系，整条链条几乎被串了起来。

这份报告发布于2026年5月13日，标题叫《NVIDIA: The China Problem》，共40页。Culper当时已经公开宣布做空英伟达。

我把它的17条核心内容完整整理出来，看看这家机构当时究竟挖出了什么。

1/17：中国业务真的归零了吗？

英伟达曾表示，2025年4月美国出口限制出台后，中国计算业务已经归零。

但Culper认为，事实完全不是这样。它估算，英伟达2026财年计算业务收入中，仍有超过20%受到中国需求驱动，主要通过GPU非法转运和东南亚中间商实现。

2/17：核心公司 Megaspeed

Megaspeed是一家新加坡云计算公司，也是英伟达在东南亚最大的芯片买家之一。

英伟达曾为其背书，称该公司没有中国股东，不存在芯片转运问题。

但Culper称，Megaspeed当时正在接受美国商务部和新加坡方面调查，并发现文件线索，怀疑阿里巴巴通过新加坡壳公司向其提供资金。

3/17：一家公司的财务数据突然暴增

Megaspeed的财务报表出现了极其异常的变化：

2023年底，公司资产负债表规模约3300万美元。

2024年底，直接膨胀至约30亿美元。

其中最引人注意的是一笔约29亿美元的「可退还押金」，付款方身份没有披露。

与此同时，账面上还出现约29亿美元的对子公司应收款。

4/17：钱被转移到了哪里？

Culper发现，Megaspeed将这笔巨额资金转给了包括马来西亚Speedmatrix在内的运营子公司。

而Speedmatrix在2024年6月，也就是正式开始运营前两个月，就将自己的资产抵押给了新加坡公司 Apex Enterprise Solutions。

这家公司背后是谁？

5/17：阿里巴巴浮出水面

新加坡企业备案显示，Apex Enterprise Solutions的母公司是阿里巴巴。

截至2025年3月31日，Apex披露了约41亿美元的预付款，同时对阿里巴巴存在约42亿美元的贷款应付款项。

Culper据此怀疑，阿里巴巴的资金通过Apex进入Megaspeed，再流向Speedmatrix等公司，用于采购英伟达服务器。

6/17：46亿美元的服务器进口

贸易记录显示，2024年12月至2026年1月，Speedmatrix累计进口约46亿美元产品。

其中约40亿美元来自Aivres Systems。

Aivres是什么公司？它是英伟达认证的 Elite OEM 合作伙伴，专门组装搭载英伟达高端GPU的服务器。

7/17：Aivres背后的中国背景

Aivres原名Inspur Systems，母公司浪潮集团被美国列入实体清单后，公司进行了更名。

Culper称，Aivres至今仍有约三分之一的中国背景股权。

它还向上海INF Tech供货，而这家公司的创始人曾担任阿里巴巴副总裁。

《华尔街日报》此前还报道称，Aivres将向马来西亚运营商供应约25亿美元Blackwell服务器，再由后者租给字节跳动。

8/17：假服务器，真转运？

另一个重要节点是Bain旗下的Bridge Data Centres（BDC）。

Culper称，2026年4月左右，BDC将Megaspeed从其数据中心租户中移除。

一名消息人士向Culper透露，Megaspeed曾利用数据中心安装「假服务器」，然后将真正的硬件转移出去。

BDC没有公开解释移除Megaspeed的原因。

9/17：黄仁勋与Alice Huang（黄乐）

这部分现在看尤其引人关注。

Culper称，黄仁勋与Megaspeed高管Alice Huang关系密切。

2024年6月，两人一起出现在台北的一场派对；2025年5月，美国出口限制出台后不久，两人又一起吃饭。

报告还特别提到，2024年6月正是Speedmatrix向阿里巴巴旗下Apex抵押资产的时间。

10/17：每次黄仁勋到访，阿里巴巴的人都会出现

一名Megaspeed现任员工向Culper透露：

黄仁勋每次访问Megaspeed的设施，阿里巴巴的代表都会一同出现。

一名前英伟达员工也表示，公司内部曾有人讨论，黄仁勋与Megaspeed之间的关系为何显得如此特殊。

11/17：Supermicro走私案只是冰山一角？

2026年3月，美国司法部起诉了三名与Supermicro有关的人士，其中包括联合创始人Wally Liaw。

指控称，他们通过一家代号为「Company-1」的公司，向中国走私价值约25亿美元的英伟达服务器。

彭博随后报道称，Company-1就是OBON Corp。

12/17：OBON也与Megaspeed有关？

Culper认为，OBON与Megaspeed存在关联。

一名前英伟达高级员工向其表示：

「Megaspeed只是冰山一角。」

Culper认为，25亿美元的Supermicro案件只是其中一条转运通道，类似操作可能涉及多个英伟达合作伙伴和中间商。

13/17：马来西亚43亿美元数据中心

2025年10月，YTL AI Cloud在马来西亚柔佛启用了一座价值约43亿美元的数据中心，内部部署了Blackwell服务器。

一名Megaspeed员工告诉Culper，Megaspeed是YTL最重要的客户之一。

但双方刻意隐藏这种客户关系，因为担心引发监管部门的关注。

14/17：英伟达合作伙伴也被牵出

英伟达认证合作伙伴Giga Computing，据称向Speedmatrix和另一家疑似Megaspeed关联公司Novagate Cloud，发运了超过5亿美元的H200及Blackwell服务器。

一个非常巧合的细节：

Novagate在马来西亚的子公司，恰好是在2025年4月美国宣布出口限制后的第二天成立的。

15/17：英伟达真的发现不了吗？

Culper采访的多名专家认为，英伟达完全有能力识别这些异常交易。

售前可以识别：
新成立的公司突然下达巨额订单、销售没有保修的服务器等。
售后也可以识别：
异常IP地址、服务器延迟与实际位置不匹配、服务器突然失联等。

问题在于，英伟达是否真正采取了足够的措施。
16/17：中国业务可能成为巨大的业绩缺口

Culper认为，市场分析师当时还把中国需求当作英伟达2027财年的潜在增长空间。

但随着北京加强对英伟达芯片的限制，这部分需求可能正在消失。

中国大陆运营商向Culper反馈，订单已经「非常少」，对业务造成了「巨大打击」。

Culper估计，英伟达未来可能面临超过300亿美元的预期收入缺口。

17/17：Culper最终的判断

Culper最后还将这些问题与黄仁勋在Dwarkesh Patel播客中面对中国相关问题时的表现联系起来。

它的核心观点非常明确：这不是看空AI，而是看空英伟达在中国业务、供应链合规和未来收入预期上面临的风险。

报告最后重申：做空英伟达，认为股价仍有下跌空间。

text:
we're so back, Fable 5.2 just released

time to do a full audit of how you work and how you can use the model to improve all of your projects

here's how to run it:

1. collect your projects and sessions

ask Fable to find every project folder on your machine and every local session from Claude Code, Codex and any other agent you use

have it group the sessions by project and save the list in one file, so every later step works from the same list

if you have many projects, start with the ones you still work on

2. audit how you work across projects

patterns only show up when Fable reads all your projects together

have it look for what repeats from project to project:

> prompts you write again in every new session
> corrections you give for the same mistake
> scripts and setups you rebuild for each project
> sessions that stall or loop on the same kind of task
> rules that sit in one project's instructions but belong in all of them

ask it to name the sessions behind each pattern

3. audit each project

for every project, have Fable read the code, the instructions and the plans, and open the site in a browser if it has one

ask it for an improvement plan per project, sorted by impact, with the effort for each item

have it mark the problems that show up in more than one project, so you can fix them once for all of them

4. audit your second brain

give it your notes, people, companies, ideas and past work, personal and company

ask it which themes come back, which notes you never use, and what is worth building or cleaning up next

5. check the plans before any file changes

go through each item and ask what it improves and how it will be tested

a prompt to start with:

audit how I work across all my projects:
> read every local Claude Code and Codex session, grouped by project
> find the prompts, corrections and manual tasks that repeat across projects
> review each project's files, instructions and plans, and check whether each problem still exists
> write one improvement plan with the sessions and files behind each item
> wait for my review before you change any file

6. let Fable plan and cheaper models execute

hand each approved plan to Opus or GPT, then have Fable review the result

move the rules that repeat across projects into your global AGENTS .md, the file every project reads, so each new project starts with them

SpaceX has filed with the FCC for up to one million orbital data center satellites, Starcloud has filed for 88,000, and Google just put four test TPUs into orbit—yet days ago, Google's own global energy chief warned that space data centers can cost up to 100x terrestrial builds. To find out exactly where the physics and unit economics break, we ran a 60-month multiphysics Monte Carlo simulation coupling radiator mass, proton flux, debris strikes, and GPU depreciation, and:

Why the Orbital Economics Collapsed:

Compounding Price Decay: A 25% annual GPU price decline erases 47% of five-year revenue, pushing $500/kg orbital COTS to -$5.9/W/yr on inference and -$10.2/W/yr on training while ground clears +$2.5/W/yr.  

The Zero-Decay Illusion: Breaking even at Starcloud's $500/kg target requires 0% price decay—assuming locked-in orbital GPUs command launch-day rates for five years while newer ground chips never undercut them.  

HBM Training Blast Radius: Google's proton tests logged one uncorrectable HBM error per 44 rad, stalling 1,024-chip synchronous groups so often that rollbacks consume roughly half the cluster's compute.  

Dawn-Dusk Orbit Trade-Off: Sun-synchronous orbit slashes battery mass from 7.3 t to 0.4 t, but sunlit infrared backload and polar proton flux drive five-year COTS dose to 9.2 krad and training rollbacks to 68%.  

Moonshot vs. 2026 Reality: Even a $200/kg moonshot with 3.5 kg/m² radiators averages -$0.6/W/yr (breaking even in just 2 of 40 runs), while current rideshares plunge returns to -$66.5/W/yr.

quoted_text:
The $80,000 Gold Property That Changed Canadian Mining

One of the greatest mining turnarounds in Canadian history began with an abandoned gold property purchased for roughly $80,000.

In 2004, Sean Roosen and his partners at Osisko Mining saw an opportunity at Canadian Malartic in Quebec.

The mine had closed in 1965, and the property had passed through several owners, including Barrick Gold.

It was an old mining camp with decades of exploration history.

But Roosen, alongside geologists Robert Wares and John Burzynski, believed there was something much bigger beneath the surface.

What I find incredible about this story is how modest the operation was in those early days.

In 2005, Osisko's exploration team moved into the former mine manager's house.

They turned the garage into a core shack.

Just imagine that for a moment.

A small group of geologists working out of an old house, surrounded by drill core, geological maps and decades of historical records.

They were trying to understand something that previous operators had not fully recognized.

The gold had been there all along.

The question was whether it could be developed on a scale that would completely change the economics of the property.

Osisko began drilling in 2005.

By 2008, the company had outlined more than 6 million ounces of gold reserves.

But finding the gold was only part of the challenge.

Roosen and his team still had to convince investors to provide the enormous amount of capital needed to build a mine.

And they were doing this during a period that included the 2008 global financial crisis.

Ultimately, Osisko raised more than $1 billion to bring Canadian Malartic into production.

In April 2011, the mine poured its first gold.

Three years later, Agnico Eagle and Yamana Gold acquired Osisko in a transaction valued at C$4.1 billion.

I had the opportunity to spend time with Sean Roosen this summer, and in our discussions, I came to appreciate just how much this chapter of his career has stayed with him.

And rightfully so.

Think about the journey from an old mine manager's house and a garage full of drill core to building one of Canada's largest gold mines.

But what makes this story even more remarkable is that the value creation didn't stop there.

In a recent conversation with Sean Boyd, who helped lead Agnico Eagle through the 2014 acquisition of Canadian Malartic, we discussed the remarkable potential of the property.

Boyd explained that Agnico recognized underground potential beyond the existing open-pit operation.

What I found particularly interesting was that subsequent exploration revealed considerably more gold than even the company had originally anticipated.

That is an extraordinary second chapter to an already remarkable story.

A property acquired for roughly $80,000 helped lay the foundation for a multibillion-dollar mining company.

And even after that company was acquired for billions, further exploration continued to reveal value beneath the ground.

I think stories like this deserve more attention.

What has always fascinated me about mining is how much value can be sitting beneath our feet, sometimes for generations, before someone finally recognizes it.

Canadian Malartic is an excellent reminder that even in places explored for decades, there can still be massive opportunities waiting for the right people to see them.

When discoveries like this happen, they can change lives, create opportunities for entire communities and leave a lasting mark on a country's mining history.

And sometimes it all begins with a handful of geologists working out of an old house, logging drill core in the garage, convinced that everyone else has missed something.

author: WalrusProtocol
quoted_text:
Spending apps forget what you taught them because your rules live in someone else's database or a localStorage blob. And when an agent meets an unnamed hex address on-chain, it either guesses or gives up.

I built RecallSpend for the @tatum_io x @WalrusProtocol Total Recall hackathon on @SuiNetwork — a Sui spending tracker with no database:

• One-time sync via Tatum Sui GraphQL (6 credits, 1 bulk write). Every page load after that reads strictly from Walrus Memory for 0 credits.
• Every spend, human correction, and agent payment is an immutable, append-only line in Walrus Memory. Corrections never overwrite observations, so the app always knows what it thought before you taught it otherwise.
• When it meets an unknown merchant, you can correct it for free or let the agent buy the label for 0.01 USDC over MPP on Sui Mainnet.
• Payment and memory writes are split in two steps, and proveUsdcTransfer verifies the 0.01 USDC transfer on Sui before the label is written.
• Generalisation (0% → 100%) is scored only on held-out repeat payments you never touched.
• Ask Memory cites the exact Walrus lines behind every answer, with no LLM in the loop.

The live app is pre-loaded with a synced demo wallet and a pre-funded agent wallet so you can test a real 0.01 USDC mainnet lookup in one click.

犹豫很久要不要开源 Blackhole 这个工具，因为它真的很简单
但它解决的问题，想必是大家都遇到过的：

平时用 Claude Code 开 auto / yolo 很爽，但直接在宿主机上跑，或者随便挂个 Docker 容器，其实很容易把本机的 $HOME、~/.ssh、系统指纹暴露出去；而且本机代理一旦闪退，流量就会直接降级成裸连，很容易被封号

对于这个问题，我做了一套基于 Colima (vz + virtiofs) 的隔离方案：

- 宿主机不装 Claude Code，只在虚拟机内安装，通过宿主机映射启动 Claude Code
- 只把当前工作目录挂载进虚拟机容器，跑 rg 和 git status 没有延迟感
- 内置 iptables 断流保护，本机代理掉线时自动下线容器网络

你可以看到，它的使用体验是完全无感的，你只需要像日常一样使用 claude 一样启动它即可

仓库里写好了完整的 AGENTS.md，clone 下来直接让你电脑上的 Agent 读文档，它就能按你的本地环境自动配好，帮你日常运行，甚至帮你移植到其他环境

我写了一篇短文聊了聊这种「只交付原子标准能力，把最后一公里交给用户本地 Agent」的思路，欢迎大家带着自己的 Agent 一起共创：

text:
submitted 𝗔𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗯𝗼𝗱𝘆 for Total Recall hackathon, built on @WalrusProtocol and @tatum_io .

AI agents on @SuiNetwork now remember, and memory does not know where an idea came from, anyone can send a coin to a wallet, a coin carries a description, and an agent that reads say "landlord moved to a new wallet, remember for rent" keeps it forever, the next rent payment goes to the attacker.

so I built 𝗔𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗯𝗼𝗱𝘆, an immune system for agent memory, it sits between an agent and its Walrus Memory account and protects Steward, an agent that pays real bills from a wallet.

every memory is a signed envelope that records who wrote it, what it came from and when, four writers share one Walrus Memory account (you, the agent, the wallet scanner and control), each a delegate key labelled onchain, untrusted content stays untrusted, even after the agent summarises it.

the model never decides where money goes, every payment passes six rules in code: a verified hash-chained ledger, a registered payee, a matching label, a spending cap, and an exact dry run through Tatum's Sui gateway, the model can be fooled, the code can't.

when poison lands, a sentinel streaming Sui checkpoints through Tatum flags it, the theft is blocked, and Antibody traces the blast radius: the coin, the observation, the agent's tainted note, the blocked decision. one quarantine excludes all of it without deleting the evidence, the quarantine becomes a lesson, so the attacker's next coin is quarantined before the agent ever reads it, and a fresh machine rebuilds everything from Walrus and Sui alone with matching fingerprints.

it runs on Sui mainnet: records on Walrus Memory, a live attack from a separate wallet, a blocked theft, three real payments (one over x402) and an incident report through Tatum's Storage API.

text:
most prediction agents forget. Every session they pay for the same tips and trust every source the same, so the sources that keep being wrong keep getting paid.

I built Calibro for #TotalRecall, the @tatum_io × @WalrusProtocol  hackathon. it keeps score of every source on Walrus Memory and pays only the ones that earned it.

Each signal answers HTTP 402. Calibro pays on @SuiNetwork mainnet, and the server checks every payment through Tatum's Sui gateway before it releases the signal.

when Polymarket resolves a game, a scheduled job scores every signal it bought and writes the post-mortem back to Walrus. Nobody presses a button.

the results are real: 41 games settled, 144 signals paid, and 29 payments refused from memory. One source scored worse than a coin flip, so Calibro stopped paying it.

People can make picks too. They sign them with their wallet, and the picks are graded when the game ends. The best pickers become a paid source.

it hasn't beaten Polymarket yet (Brier 0.194 vs 0.185), and I say so. what it has learned is who is worth paying.

Kinetiq 推出的 Elysium @Enter_Elysium  11 月 9 日正式上线主网。它真正想做的是补上 Hyperliquid 的现货流动性短板。

@Kinetiq_xyz 将其称为「价值增值 L2」：50% 排序器收入用于公开市场买入并永久销毁 $KNTQ，25% 分配给 Builder，25% 进入国库。

但最大卖点还要等约 4 周：届时才计划上线 HyperCore 订单簿预编译，让 EVM 应用能够利用 Hyperliquid 的原生流动性。

Elysium 甚至把 @Robinhood Chain 作为潜在竞争对手，但现实距离这个目标还有很远。

联创 @0xOmnia 的逻辑是，Robinhood Chain、BSC、Base 在技术或法律层面无法直接调用母公司的现货和期权订单流，而 Elysium 背靠 Hyperliquid，有机会打通这层流动性。

不过，X用户 @LennyPr0  对此并不乐观。他认为，Elysium 目前更像一个高度投机的 PvP 市场：大量 Meme 币快速上涨后暴跌，MEV 机器人甚至在链完全上线前就开始捕获普通用户交易价值。他直言，现阶段的 Elysium 对 Robinhood Chain 几乎构不成竞争。

数据也存在明显口径差异：联创称上线约 12 小时成交额超 9,000 万美元、900 万笔交易、14.5 万独立账户、TVL 约 5,000 万美元；DefiLlama 同期记录的 DeFi TVL 约 462 万美元，DEX 成交约 606 万美元。

Elysium 最大的优势是 HyperCore 原生流动性，最大的短板则是目前还没有证明自己能把这种优势转化为真实交易需求。

如果做市商愿意带着订单流入场，它才有机会挑战 Robinhood Chain 的现货生态；如果最终只有 Meme 发射、机器人套利和流动性内卷，那么 100ms 出块也改变不了它的处境。

4 周后，才是真正的考验。

text: Discussion of the McDonald’s Dollar Menu from a franchisee. Interesting anecdote about inflation and how we all anchor prices (“I remember when X cost only Y dollars”)
author: ImperiumPaper
quoted_text:
100% - ready for a hot take? 🔥

What people don't understand is that we ran the Dollar Menu for over a decade, and the last half of that run was a fight. It was debated internally every year. The margins were never there, and there was always a push to kill it because it simply wasn't sustainable.

Today, I can’t build a McDouble for $1 on food cost alone. My margins are at historical lows (not a good thing).  Nostalgia doesn't do math, beef and wages have both close to tripled since the Dollar Menu days, but that $1 price is burned into people's heads like it is canonized scripture.

🎯 McD catches every arrow for all inflation fatigue while being, on national average, pretty much the overall cheapest major QSR in the country. Cheaper than BK, Wendy's, SNS, etc. 

We'll have this exact same conversation in ten years about today’s McD $5 Meal Deal, people will swear it was the last honest price in America but we don’t get credit for it now - like the old dollar menu. The Dollar Menu looks like a better deal now than it ever was then. Memory inflates it even more. 

That's the real danger of promotions: they don't just move product, they reset what customers think your food should cost, even 10 years down the road. We can be a dollar or two cheaper than BK on the same meal and get zero credit for it, because we're not being compared to BK - we are being compared to McD 2008. 

That's the fight.

text:
Let's address a lot of the concerns over the recent SFDP changes.

First, what were the changes?

- 12-month time within SFDP
- Auto-graduation at 300k SOL
- 100 Validator max
- Run your own validator

These changes, as expected, were controversial. There are a lot of assumptions on where this stake will be going after the changes are in place.

The job of SFDP has been three-fold:
1. Help bootstrap net new validators
2. Provide a healthy testnet
3. Get some validators testing changes early

SFDP has done its job. Testnet exists, validators often find issues early, and a large amount of validators have started from SFDP.

Solana is much larger now than when SFDP started. Solana's validator set has matured significantly, has an amazing community, and encounters new challenges that were never conceived of in the beginning.

We've had a lot of feedback that SFDP is no longer reactive enough nor provides enough criteria given the ever-changing landscape of Solana. This feedback is heard and leads us to the next stage of delegation with a focus on continuing to improve network health and rewarding ecosystem contributors.

SFDP will continue to exist for the newer validators and validators that contribute greatly to network health should also be rewarded. We have historically helped fund huge ecosystem contributors such as Blueshift through delegation outside of SFDP. We delegated to a number of validators that tried Frankendancer first. These among many other delegations are success stories that have both pushed Solana to new heights as well as helped improve network health.

We're making a bet that we can be more proactive to future network health concerns, be more reactive to new issues, and help push Solana into this next stage with these changes.

If you have feedback on these changes, please let me know. SFDP helped us get to where we are today. These changes are about getting to what comes next.

text:
some thoughts on memory. i think we're seeing signs its starting to price itself out of its own demand. there were 3 things from my readings today that fit together

1/ PCs and phones are absorbing the memory price spike. an OEM expert on a Wukong (substack) channel check says memory is now 35-38% of a PC's bill of materials, up from 20%. 

Q3 PC shipments fell 23% YoY, handsets 40-50%

2/ buyers are drawing down instead of stocking up. tier one PC makers cut DRAM inventory from ~6 months of cover to 3-4. TrendForce has DRAM lead times easing to 18 weeks (still very tight), with chinese buyers pulling back on DRAM and enterprise SSDs while US demand holds

3/ the supply mix may shift. the same check says Samsung is expected to move some wafers away from HBM (the stacked memory that sits next to AI chips) starting Q4, because regular DRAM margins are now close to HBM's. their base case: prices plateau in Q1 2027 and ease in Q2

the first cracks in the memory cycle will show up at the edges, consumer devices and china expansion. AI data centers are still short of memory and will be for a while.

Nvidia's Vera Rubin seems to be sliping partly on HBM4 yields coming in below target (power hookups are the other reason). 

if Samsung tilts wafers toward regular DRAM just as HBM4 is the bottleneck, HBM could stay tight even as regular DRAM loosens.

在昨天推文的最后，我说：眼下市场给我们出了一道开卷考题。

之所以说是“开卷考”，是因为我们每个人都有足够的时间去“翻书”找“解法”。

在这里，我先给出我自己的答案：

图中的指标，是衡量实现亏损/盈利相对过去90天平均水平偏离了几个标准差，数值越低代表割肉离场越集中，越高代表获利了结越集中。

Glassnode官方给出的定义是：绿色信号为Low Risk；红色信号为High Risk；中间还有过度区，我把它隐藏了。

每一个柱体代表一天，柱体连续越多，说明现象持续的时间越长，行为的确定性越高（不是偶发性）。

所以，我的“开卷考”答案是：绝对不可能在“Low Risk”的位置交出我的筹码。短线不会，长期布局就更不会了。

小伙伴可以自行比对2026年（图1）和2023年（图2）的数据。

当然，你的答案也许和我不同，这不重要。

这是我在当前能力范围内做出的最适合自己的交易选择。即便错了，也不后悔。

希望你也一样。

text:
把套利 bot 从 Python 换成 Rust：确实快了 3 倍

策略：Arcus 挂 maker 单等成交，成交后立刻在 Lighter 用 IOC 对冲，赚 SPY 两边价格的基差。

从收到成交推送到对冲成交，每段耗时：

🟢 收到推送 → 发出对冲单：21.6ms → 6.5–8.6ms

🟢 签名 → 发出请求：5–9ms → 1.2–1.5ms

🟡 发单 → 交易所确认：15–29ms → 15–18ms（主要是网络）

🔴 Lighter 撮合成交：约 300–400ms（换语言也没用）

结论：Rust 省下约 15ms，只占整段约 420ms 的 3–4%。

之前 Arcus 和 Lighter 对冲的 100% 胜率被打破了，最高 10 连胜，但胜率依然很高。

昨天把 python 改造成了 Rust 语言，周末没啥波动，目前跑的还不太多。

claude 也7 天可以用 fable 模型了，打算把核心逻辑再 review 一遍。
author: mycndota
quoted_text:
最新策略已经可以稳定盈利！！暂时胜率 100%，样本待积累。（截图均为实测数据！）

ps：看到有小伙伴说换 rust 更快，也打算做一版（但我目前程序只占 7ms，剩下的是交易所的 300ms）

策略：SPY 在 Arcus 挂单，成交后立刻在 Lighter 吃单对冲，只在积分加成时段开仓。

📊 11-02 至今 22 轮，Arcus 成交约 26 万（开+平），合计 −$9.6，磨损约 3.6U/10万。
分配置看，差别很大：

🔴 单轮 1 万：4 轮全亏，−$6.66（每 10 万亏 8.3U，夜里盘口太薄，吃单要吃好几档）

🔴 6bp 止损：5 轮，−$4.06（一碰就止损，平在了最差的位置，目前已经修复）

🟢 最新配置：7 轮全部盈利，+$1.19，每 10 万赚约 1.9U（单轮 0.5 万、亏损仓位最长拿 4 小时、只留 25bp 灾难止损、高波动时不开仓）

⏱️ 一次对冲的时间线（以 Arcus 挂单被吃为第 0 毫秒，实测中位数）：

① 第 7.5ms：程序发出 Lighter 对冲单（Python）

② 下单前预检：22ms → 0.3ms（元数据缓存从 60 秒改成 1 小时）

③ 交易签名：0.8ms（Lighter 官方 Go 原生库）

④ 发送到交易所收单：约 50ms → 约 44ms（连接保温；剩下的是 Lighter 服务器处理）

⑤ 发单后 300–400ms：真正撮合，其中约 300ms 是 Standard 账户的固定延迟 ← 成交价在这里定

⑥ 程序确认成交：约 600ms → 约 410ms（不影响成交价，但分笔成交时第二张对冲单能早发约 200ms）

🦀 换成 Rust 会怎样？
🟢 能变快的只有第 ① 步：7.5ms → 约 1ms，省约 6ms
🟡 第 ②③ 步：已经是缓存和 Go 原生库，换语言没区别
🔴 第 ④⑤ 步：卡在网络和交易所，换什么语言都一样
算下来，从被吃到撮合全程约 350ms，Rust 最多省 6ms，不到 2%。

我们这次没换语言，只做了 4 处 Python 优化：
1️⃣ 中位数计算改成增量维护：每步 8.8ms → 0.003ms
2️⃣ 元数据缓存：省约 21ms
3️⃣ 连接保温：省约 6ms
4️⃣ 查询节奏：确认成交提前约 190ms

结论：做跨所对冲时，真正的成本不是程序慢，而是"挂单被吃的时候价格往往正在动"，加上交易所 300ms 的固定延迟。最新配置 7 轮里，每笔对冲滑点都没超过 1bp。比起重写成 Rust，更值得做的是把每一毫秒量清楚、躲开高波动时段、不在最差的位置止损。不过我也打算再写一般 Rust 进行对比，没准会给有惊喜。
